title: The Hong Kong digital-asset map
md:
This module is for the bank's Head of Compliance (digital assets). After it, you can name who regulates each digital-asset activity in Hong Kong. You can also say which regimes are live and which are still coming.

## In 60 seconds

Hong Kong splits digital-asset regulation among several bodies. Each body covers particular activities. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) supervises banks, known in law as Authorized Institutions (AIs). [S:8934af8cc884, para 2.1.1] The HKMA also licenses stablecoin issuers (firms that issue tokens designed to hold a steady value against a currency). [S:270f1f7324ab, Register introduction] Virtual assets (VAs) are digital tokens such as cryptocurrencies. The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) licenses virtual-asset (VA) trading platforms (VATPs). [S:b14be2203d39, Licensed platforms table] The SFC also sets codes of conduct for regulated securities activities. [S:8934af8cc884, para 2.1.2] The Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau (FSTB) sets policy. [S:a29b51bffc6b, para 2] The FSTB and the SFC consult the public on new laws. [S:6186c01c6649, cover page] The Legislative Council (LegCo) passes bills. [S:b12bd88c7aee, p.1]

A bank that carries on SFC-regulated activities must register with the SFC as a Registered Institution (RI). [S:8934af8cc884, paras 2.1.2-2.1.3] Even so, the HKMA is the bank's day-to-day, frontline supervisor. [S:8934af8cc884, paras 2.1.2-2.1.3]

Live today (see Status board):
- the VA trading-platform regime
- the Stablecoins Ordinance
- the joint SFC–HKMA circulars
- HKMA guidance on custody (holding assets for clients) and on tokenisation (recording assets as tokens on a blockchain)
- the Basel cryptoasset capital standard (global rules on how much capital banks hold against cryptoassets)

Coming:
- statutory licensing (licensing set by law) for VA dealing, custody, advisory and management [S:6186c01c6649, paras 31, 36]; [S:01c5c5c4045f, para 62]
- crypto-asset tax reporting under the Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF) [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, Overview section]

## Status board

As of 25 Sep 2026.

| Instrument | Issuer | Date | Status (chip) | Applies to | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (AMLO) Part 5B VA trading platform (VATP) licensing + VATP Guidelines | LegCo / SFC | 1 Jun 2023 | In force | VATPs. Banks and other intermediaries (SFC-licensed or SFC-registered firms) may deal in VAs only through SFC-licensed VATPs. | [S:b12bd88c7aee, p.2]; [S:f1bbafccd556, para 1.2]; [S:8a016a912528, para 17] |
| Stablecoins Ordinance (Cap. 656) | LegCo / HKMA | 1 Aug 2025 | In force | Stablecoin issuers. Only regulated entities specified in the Ordinance may offer stablecoins to the public. | [S:0df2de5234dc, para 1]; [S:c6df52e680de, Reply part (3)] |
| Joint circular on intermediaries' VA-related activities (Dec 2023) + supplement (Sep 2025) | SFC + HKMA | 22 Dec 2023; 30 Sep 2025 | In force | Licensed corporations (LCs), the non-bank firms the SFC licenses. RIs (banks), with the HKMA as frontline supervisor. | [S:8a016a912528, p.1, para 31]; [S:b79266f3da51, paras 1, 10] |
| RI circular on Relevant Stablecoins | HKMA (with SFC) | 27 May 2026 | In force | RIs | [S:a0bd48559762, p.1] |
| Banks' interface with VAs and VA service providers (VASPs) | HKMA | 28 Jan 2022 | In force | All AIs | [S:642680fa4467, p.5] |
| Updated custody guidance (replaces the Feb 2024 version) | HKMA | 27 May 2026 | In force | AIs + subsidiaries of locally incorporated AIs | [S:ed61d7c335e7, p.2] |
| Sale and distribution of tokenised products | HKMA | 20 Feb 2024 | In force | AIs | [S:b2719f3dcb37, p.1] |
| Risk-management considerations for distributed ledger technology (blockchain-type systems) | HKMA | 16 Apr 2024 | In force | AIs (non-binding considerations) | [S:1884530ff235, p.1] |
| Basel cryptoasset standard (amendment rules + HKMA manual module CRP-1) | HKMA / LegCo | 1 Jan 2026 | In force | All AIs | [S:974899bbef4d, p.1]; [S:b7d630146e6c, para 1.4.1] |
| VA dealing + VA custodian licensing | FSTB + SFC | 24 Dec 2025 | Conclusions published | Banks would register with the SFC. HKMA proposed as frontline regulator. | [S:6186c01c6649, paras 31, 36]; [S:f41a543388bc, para 48]; [S:f673ef6dcb63, para 1.10]; [S:a29b51bffc6b, para 6] |
| VA advisory + VA management licensing | FSTB + SFC | 26 May 2026 | Conclusions published | Only banks could register for these services, rather than be licensed. Current RIs would need to register. | [S:6186c01c6649, fns 9-10]; [S:01c5c5c4045f, para 62] |
| CARF / amended Common Reporting Standard (CRS) bill | FSTB / Inland Revenue Department (IRD) / LegCo | 22 May 2026 | Bill before LegCo | Reporting crypto-asset service providers | [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, Overview] |
| Ensemble TX (tokenised deposits: bank deposits recorded as tokens) | HKMA | 13 Nov 2025 | Pilot | Participating banks | [S:8b67e8dc510f, paras 1-3] |

## Key facts

- The HKMA does not currently plan to stop banks taking on VA exposures, as long as controls and senior-management oversight are adequate. [S:642680fa4467, Prudential supervision section, p.3]
- A bank intending any VA activity should discuss it with the HKMA before launch, and get feedback on its risk controls. [S:642680fa4467, AIs' VA-related proposals, p.5]
- A bank carrying on regulated activities (securities business the SFC regulates) must register with the SFC as an RI. [S:8934af8cc884, paras 2.1.2-2.1.3] The SFC keeps ultimate responsibility, but the HKMA supervises the RI day to day. [S:8934af8cc884, paras 2.1.2-2.1.3] The SFC may rely on that HKMA supervision. [S:8934af8cc884, paras 2.1.2-2.1.3]
- Banks follow the joint circular in their role as RIs, with the HKMA as frontline supervisor. [S:8934af8cc884, para 2.1.3] The circular reminds intermediaries to tell the SFC, and the HKMA where applicable, before they start or change VA-related activities. [S:8a016a912528, para 31]
- The SFC and HKMA require intermediaries to offer VA dealing services only by partnering with SFC-licensed VATPs. [S:8a016a912528, para 17]
- The Stablecoins Ordinance came into force on 1 August 2025. [S:0df2de5234dc, para 1]
- The HKMA register lists two licensed stablecoin issuers. [S:270f1f7324ab, Register table] They are Anchorpoint Financial Limited (FRS01) and The Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation Limited (FRS02). [S:270f1f7324ab, Register table] Both licences took effect on 10 April 2026. [S:270f1f7324ab, Register table]
- The Secretary for Financial Services and the Treasury (SFST) told LegCo that the HKMA received 36 applications in the initial application period. [S:3f0fcc104e61, Reply para 1 and (2)] The SFST also said any further licences would keep the overall number very limited. [S:3f0fcc104e61, Reply para 1 and (2)]
- The SFC's online list showed 13 licensed VATPs at its 29 May 2026 update. [S:b14be2203d39, Licensed platforms table; applicant section] Being on the applicant list is not the same as being licensed. [S:b14be2203d39, Licensed platforms table; applicant section]
- The HKMA's 2026 custody annex expects banks to keep 98% of client VAs in cold storage (offline). [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(b), para 11(l) and fn 8] The annex also expects banks to create, store and back up seeds and private keys in Hong Kong. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(b), para 11(l) and fn 8] Private keys are the secret codes that control the assets, and seeds are used to generate them.
- The Basel cryptoasset rules on capital, disclosure and exposure limits came into force on 1 January 2026. [S:974899bbef4d, p.1]
- CRP-1 is the HKMA's Supervisory Policy Manual (SPM) module on classifying cryptoassets. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2] Under it, a bank that acquires a new type of cryptoasset must notify the HKMA. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2] The bank must treat the asset as Group 2b until the HKMA agrees the bank's own classification. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2] Group 2b is the capital category where the bank gets no credit for hedging.
- For the coming VA dealing and custody regimes, the Government proposed that the SFC lead licensing and standard-setting. The HKMA would be the frontline regulator for banks. [S:a29b51bffc6b, paras 5-6]
- Under the proposed dealing regime, banks would need to register with the SFC to deal in VAs. The SFC would register banks in consultation with the HKMA. [S:f673ef6dcb63, para 1.10]
- No arrangement is planned to let existing providers carry on while they apply once the VA dealing and custody regimes start. [S:6186c01c6649, paras 31, 35-36]; [S:f41a543388bc, paras 48, 51] SFC-licensed VATPs, LCs, RIs and banks already providing these services are to get a faster (expedited) approval process. [S:6186c01c6649, paras 31, 35-36]; [S:f41a543388bc, paras 48, 51]
- The CARF bill was published in the Gazette (the Government's official record) on 22 May 2026. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, Overview section] It had its First Reading (the first formal stage of a bill) in LegCo on 3 June 2026. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, Overview section] If the bill passes, CARF duties start on 1 January 2027. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, Overview section]; [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, Clause 1(3)]
- The IRD plans a dedicated CARF portal. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, Reporting portal section] The bill proposes that every in-scope reporting crypto-asset service provider register an account on it. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, Reporting portal section]

## What your bank must do

**Obligations**
- [ ] Discuss any planned VA activity with the HKMA before launch. [S:642680fa4467, p.5]
- [ ] As an RI, notify the SFC and HKMA when the bank intends to start or change VA dealing, advice or asset management. This includes a change of client type. [S:8934af8cc884, para 5.6]
- [ ] From 1 January 2026, classify cryptoasset exposures under Part 12 of the Banking (Capital) Rules. Read CRP-1 alongside Part 12. [S:b7d630146e6c, paras 1.1.4, 1.4.1]

**Controls & monitoring**
- [ ] Set prudent limits on VA exposures. Set conservative loan-to-value ratios (loan size compared with collateral value) when VAs are used as collateral. [S:642680fa4467, p.3]
- [ ] Keep client digital assets held in custody separate (segregated) from the bank's own assets. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 6]

**Notify / consult HKMA or SFC**
- [ ] Notify the HKMA when the bank acquires any new type of cryptoasset. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2]
- [ ] Discuss custody plans with the HKMA before offering custody. [S:ed61d7c335e7, Implementation, p.2]

**Counterparty due diligence**
- [ ] For VA dealing, route business only through SFC-licensed VATPs. [S:8a016a912528, para 17]
- [ ] Check a VATP's status on the SFC's licensed list, not the applicant list. [S:b14be2203d39, applicant section]
- [ ] Check a stablecoin issuer against the HKMA register. The HKMA says the register holds the latest list of licensees. [S:afb6cd0da6ff, paras 4-5]

## Talking points

**To the chief compliance officer (CCO)**
- The bank's VA conduct duties (rules on how it treats clients) apply to the bank as an RI. The HKMA supervises the bank day to day, not the SFC directly. [S:8934af8cc884, para 2.1.3]
- The bank must comply with the HKMA's anti-money laundering (AML) and counter-financing of terrorism (CFT) Guideline. [S:7bfdad704174, Ch.1 fn 1] As an RI, it must also take into account the SFC's AML/CFT Guideline, including its Chapter 12 on VAs. [S:7bfdad704174, Ch.1 fn 1]

**To business heads**
- Any new VA product needs an HKMA discussion before launch. [S:642680fa4467, p.5] RIs must also tell the SFC and HKMA in advance. [S:8934af8cc884, para 5.6]
- Only two stablecoin issuers are licensed. [S:270f1f7324ab, Register table] The Government says any further licences would keep the total very limited. [S:3f0fcc104e61, Reply (2)]

**To the CEO**
- The Government proposed that the SFC lead licensing for VA dealing and custody. The HKMA would be the banks' frontline regulator. [S:a29b51bffc6b, paras 5-6]
- No arrangement is planned to let existing firms carry on while they apply when these regimes start. [S:6186c01c6649, para 31]

**To Risk / chief risk officer (CRO)**
- The Basel cryptoasset standard applies from 1 January 2026. [S:b7d630146e6c, paras 1.4.1-1.4.2, 2.1.2] Until the HKMA agrees the bank's classification, two things stay in Group 2b: exposures held before that date and any new cryptoasset type. [S:b7d630146e6c, paras 1.4.1-1.4.2, 2.1.2]
- The HKMA's custody annex expects banks to keep 98% of client VAs in cold storage. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(l) and fn 8]

## Common mix-ups

- **Myth:** "The SFC supervises our VA business directly." **Fact:** The SFC holds ultimate responsibility. But the HKMA is the RI's day-to-day supervisor. [S:8934af8cc884, para 2.1.3]
- **Myth:** "The 50%/100% insurance rule applies to our custody." **Fact:** That rule is an SFC expectation for VATPs. [S:f1bbafccd556, para 10.22] It calls for an SFC-approved compensation arrangement covering 50% of client VAs in cold storage and 100% in hot (online) and other storage. [S:f1bbafccd556, para 10.22] The HKMA's 2026 annex takes a different approach. It makes the bank liable to clients for losses from incidents the bank is responsible for. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(n)] It also expects the bank to hold adequate financial resources to cover such losses. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(n)]
- **Myth:** "A platform on the SFC's applicant list is licensed." **Fact:** Applicants are not licensed, even those allowed to keep operating while they apply. Only the licensed list shows licensed platforms. [S:b14be2203d39, applicant section]
- **Myth:** "The 2022 joint circular still applies." **Fact:** The December 2023 joint circular replaced the January 2022 and October 2023 versions. [S:8a016a912528, note after para 3, p.1]
- **Myth:** "The dealing and custody bills are law." **Fact:** They are at the consultation-conclusions stage. [S:6186c01c6649, para 31] The Government's stated target was to introduce a bill in 2026. [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 104]

## Read these first

1. **Regulatory approaches to AIs' interface with VAs and VASPs** — HKMA, 28 Jan 2022. Read pp.3-5 on prudential rules (bank safety and soundness), anti-money laundering, investor protection and prior discussion. This document sets out the HKMA's base position on banks and VAs. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/20220128-1-EN
2. **SPM SB-1 Supervision of Regulated Activities of SFC-Registered AIs (V.4)** — HKMA, 12 Sep 2025. Read paras 2.1.3, 2.2.4, 4.16.1 and 5.6. This module explains why the HKMA, not the SFC, supervises your RI business day to day. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20250909-3-EN/SB-1.PDF
3. **Policy Statement 2.0 on the Development of Digital Assets in Hong Kong** — FSTB, 26 Jun 2025. Read paras 4-6 and 16. This statement sets out the LEAP framework. LEAP stands for Legal and regulatory streamlining, Expanding tokenised products, Advancing use cases and collaboration, and People and partnership development. The statement also proposes that the SFC lead the new regimes, with the HKMA as frontline regulator for banks. https://gia.info.gov.hk/general/202506/26/P2025062600269_500089_1_1750909574183.pdf

## Open items

- The VA dealing, custodian, advisory and management bill: the SFST said on 24 June 2026 that it would be introduced this year. [S:c6df52e680de, Reply part (3)] As of 25 Sep 2026, no bill text or Gazette notice appears in the documents reviewed for this guide.
- CARF bill: it had its First Reading on 3 June 2026. No document reviewed for this guide records its passage. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, Overview section]
- No Insurance Authority rulebook on digital assets is in the documents reviewed for this guide. Rules for insurers are a gap.
- The VATP list is live and changes over time. The 13-platform count is a snapshot from 29 May 2026. [S:b14be2203d39, Footer]

## Related modules

[A2](#m-A2), [A3](#m-A3), [B1](#m-B1), [B2](#m-B2), [B3](#m-B3)

title: How Hong Kong rules are made and how to read them
md:
This module is for the bank's Head of Compliance (digital assets). After it, you can place any document on the law-making path. You can also tell how binding it is and cite it to the paragraph.

## In 60 seconds

Hong Kong's stablecoin regime shows the path a digital-asset rule can take. [S:54aa01e7396e, Introduction, para 1]; [S:a9a82f2b38ce, paras 1, 6]; [S:35e1ac2b815a, paras 1, 3]; [S:0df2de5234dc, paras 1, 3] The path has five steps:

- A consultation paper lays out the proposals. [S:54aa01e7396e, Introduction, para 1]
- The Government publishes its conclusions on the consultation. [S:54aa01e7396e, Introduction, para 1]
- A bill is gazetted (published in the Government Gazette) and passed by the Legislative Council (LegCo). [S:a9a82f2b38ce, paras 1, 6]; [S:35e1ac2b815a, paras 1, 3]
- A notice in the Gazette sets the date the law starts. [S:0df2de5234dc, paras 1, 3]
- A transition period follows. [S:35e1ac2b815a, paras 1, 3]

Below Ordinances (the main laws) sit other documents with different legal force. [S:974899bbef4d, letter, para 1] They include:

- rules made as subsidiary legislation (detailed law made under an Ordinance) [S:974899bbef4d, letter, para 1]
- Supervisory Policy Manual (SPM) modules, the supervisory guidance chapters of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) [S:8934af8cc884, cover, Classification]; [S:b7d630146e6c, cover, Classification]
- guidelines
- circulars.

Each SPM module states its own classification on its cover, so check it. [S:8934af8cc884, cover, Classification]; [S:b7d630146e6c, cover, Classification]

For a bank, one key reading rule sits in the HKMA's anti-money-laundering (AML) Guideline. In that Guideline, both *must* and *should* mark a mandatory requirement. [S:7bfdad704174, para 1.6]

Where to find the documents:

- The HKMA publishes its circulars and SPM modules in its Banking Regulatory Document Repository (BRDR). [S:974899bbef4d, landing page]
- Circulars of the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) open from its e-Distribution site. [S:8a016a912528, p.1]
- Conclusions of the Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau (FSTB) record the legislative milestones. [S:6186c01c6649, p.4, Next step]
- Government press releases record them too. [S:0df2de5234dc, para 1]

## Status board

As of 25 September 2026. Each row is a worked example of one stage.

- AI = authorized institution (a bank). AIs = authorized institutions.
- RIs = registered institutions (banks registered with the SFC).
- LCs = licensed corporations (firms licensed by the SFC).
- VA = virtual asset. VATP = VA trading platform. VATPs = VA trading platforms.

| Instrument | Issuer | Date | Status (chip) | Applies to | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Stablecoin issuer regime: consultation paper, then conclusions (July 2024) | FSTB + HKMA | 27 December 2023 | Superseded | Future issuers | [S:54aa01e7396e, cover, p.1; Introduction, para 1] |
| Stablecoins Bill gazetted; First Reading (formal start in LegCo) set for 18 December 2024 | Government / LegCo | 6 December 2024 | Superseded | Issuers | [S:a9a82f2b38ce, paras 1, 6] |
| Notice setting the start date of the Stablecoins Ordinance (Cap. 656), made by the Secretary for Financial Services and the Treasury (SFST) | SFST | Gazetted 6 June 2025; started 1 August 2025 | In force | Issuers, offerors | [S:0df2de5234dc, paras 1, 3-4] |
| Banking (Capital) (Amendment) Rules 2025, plus matching amendment rules on Disclosure and Exposure Limits | HKMA / LegCo | HKMA letter on gazettal 11 July 2025; applies from 1 January 2026 | In force | All AIs | [S:974899bbef4d, landing page, Directly related Document; letter, paras 1-2] |
| HKMA letter clarifying para 2.6.4 of CRP-1 (the SPM module on classifying cryptoassets) | HKMA | 3 June 2026 | In force | All AIs | [S:dca53ff0a62c, p.1, paras 3-4] |
| VA dealing and VA custodian regimes | FSTB + SFC | 24 December 2025 | Conclusions published | VA dealing and custodian service providers, including LCs and RIs | [S:6186c01c6649, p.3, footnote 2; para 35]; [S:f41a543388bc, para 48] |
| VA advisory and VA management regimes | FSTB + SFC | May 2026 | Conclusions published | Advisory and management providers, including SFC-licensed or registered intermediaries | [S:01c5c5c4045f, cover, p.1; para 62] |
| Bill for the Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF) and the amended Common Reporting Standard (CRS), both tax reporting standards | FSTB / LegCo | Gazetted 22 May 2026; First Reading 3 June 2026 | Bill before LegCo | Reporting crypto-asset service providers | [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, Overview] |

## Key facts

- The July 2024 stablecoin conclusions said a bill was being prepared for LegCo later that year. [S:54aa01e7396e, Way Forward, para 12.1, p.29]
- The Stablecoins Bill was gazetted on 6 December 2024. Its First Reading in LegCo was set for 18 December 2024. [S:a9a82f2b38ce, paras 1, 6]
- LegCo passed the bill on 21 May 2025. The government release refers to a six-month grace period. [S:35e1ac2b815a, paras 1, 3]
- The SFST made a notice setting 1 August 2025 as the start date. It was gazetted on 6 June 2025. [S:0df2de5234dc, paras 1, 3, 7] The notices were due to go to LegCo on 11 June 2025 for negative vetting. [S:0df2de5234dc, paras 1, 3, 7] Under negative vetting, a notice stands unless LegCo amends or repeals it within a set period.
- The Banking (Capital), (Disclosure) and (Exposure Limits) (Amendment) Rules 2025 went through 28 days of negative vetting in LegCo. That period expired without extension. [S:974899bbef4d, letter, para 1]
- LegCo passed amendments to the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (AMLO) on 7 December 2022. [S:b12bd88c7aee, letter, pp.1-2] The HKMA said the changes relevant to banks would start on 1 June 2023. It said the gap allowed time to prepare. [S:b12bd88c7aee, letter, pp.1-2]
- Transition periods can end in a hard stop. [S:2e5c35b38cc3, paras 6, 20] VATPs operating before 1 June 2023 could carry on for 12 months, to 31 May 2024, without breaching the licensing rules. [S:2e5c35b38cc3, paras 6, 20] Only applications made by 29 February 2024 could qualify for the transitional arrangement that treated existing platforms as licensed. The SFC had no power to extend that deadline. [S:2e5c35b38cc3, paras 6, 20]
- Under current plans, the conclusions on the coming VA dealing and custodian regimes offer existing providers no arrangement that treats them as licensed while they apply. [S:6186c01c6649, para 31]; [S:f41a543388bc, para 48]
- The HKMA issues its AML Guideline under section 7 of AMLO and section 7(3) of the Banking Ordinance. Compliance is enforced through both Ordinances. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 1.1, 1.3]
- In that Guideline, both *must* and *should* mean a mandatory requirement. [S:7bfdad704174, para 1.6]
- Each SPM module states its own force on its cover. [S:8934af8cc884, cover, Classification]; [S:b7d630146e6c, cover, Classification]
- SB-1 (the module on supervising banks' SFC-regulated activities) is a statutory guideline under section 7(3) of the Banking Ordinance. [S:8934af8cc884, cover, Classification] CRP-1 is a non-statutory guideline, issued as a guidance note. [S:b7d630146e6c, cover, Classification]
- Where CRP-1 and the Banking (Capital) Rules (BCR) differ, the BCR take priority. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 1.1.4]
- Some HKMA papers say they are not binding. [S:1884530ff235, Annex, Introduction, 4th bullet, p.1] One example is the April 2024 paper on distributed ledger technology (DLT), such as blockchain. [S:1884530ff235, Annex, Introduction, 4th bullet, p.1] That paper is non-binding and does not cover every case. The HKMA discusses its detailed expectations with each AI one to one. [S:1884530ff235, Annex, Introduction, 4th bullet, p.1]
- A circular can change how a module applies at once. [S:dca53ff0a62c, p.1, paras 3-4] The HKMA's letter of 3 June 2026 clarified the condition in CRP-1 para 2.6.4. [S:dca53ff0a62c, p.1, paras 3-4] The condition may also be met where a financial market regulator supervises the business activities of the tokenised asset. [S:dca53ff0a62c, p.1, paras 3-4] A tokenised asset is a traditional asset recorded as a token on a blockchain. The change took effect immediately, and the module's wording is to be updated later. [S:dca53ff0a62c, p.1, paras 3-4]
- The SFC issues its Guidelines for VATP operators under two laws. [S:f1bbafccd556, para 1.1, Note] These are section 399 of the Securities and Futures Ordinance (SFO) and section 53ZTK of AMLO. [S:f1bbafccd556, para 1.1, Note]
- A later circular can replace earlier ones outright. [S:8a016a912528, para 3, closing sentence, p.1] The December 2023 joint circular replaced the January 2022 and October 2023 versions. [S:8a016a912528, para 3, closing sentence, p.1]
- The HKMA's custody letter of 27 May 2026 replaces its custody circular of 20 February 2024. [S:ed61d7c335e7, Implementation, p.2]
- Budget speeches announce plans, not rules. [S:654fa5eba8cf, paras 104, 108] The 2026-27 Budget said a bill would be introduced in 2026 for VA dealing and custodian licensing. [S:654fa5eba8cf, paras 104, 108] It gave the first half of 2026 as the timing for a CARF amendment bill. [S:654fa5eba8cf, paras 104, 108]

## What your bank must do

**Obligations**
- [ ] Treat *should* in the HKMA AML Guideline as mandatory, not optional. [S:7bfdad704174, para 1.6]
- [ ] Follow the BCR where CRP-1 and the BCR differ. Part 12 of the BCR sets the classification principles. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 1.1.4]
- [ ] Apply the 3 June 2026 clarification of CRP-1 para 2.6.4. It took effect immediately. [S:dca53ff0a62c, p.1, paras 3-4]

**Controls & monitoring**
- [ ] Keep a register of regulatory documents. Record each document's classification and whether a later document replaced it. [S:ed61d7c335e7, Implementation, p.2] For example, the 2026 letter replaced the 2024 custody circular. [S:ed61d7c335e7, Implementation, p.2]
- [ ] Track start dates separately from passage dates. [S:b12bd88c7aee, letter, pp.1-2] For example, LegCo passed the AMLO amendments in December 2022. The relevant changes applied from 1 June 2023. [S:b12bd88c7aee, letter, pp.1-2]

**Notify / consult HKMA or SFC**
- [ ] Note that the dealing conclusions encourage firms that provide, or plan, VA dealing to contact the SFC or HKMA (as applicable) early. [S:6186c01c6649, paras 33-34] One example is to start pre-application (early talks before a formal licence application). [S:6186c01c6649, paras 33-34] The conclusions say dealing providers that do not make contact for pre-application will have to stop operating when the regime starts. [S:6186c01c6649, paras 33-34]

**Counterparty due diligence**
- [ ] Tell a formally licensed VATP apart from two kinds of applicant: an ordinary applicant, and an applicant that the law treats as licensed while its application is pending. [S:b14be2203d39, List of VATP applicants; Last update] The SFC keeps them on separate lists, last updated 29 May 2026. [S:b14be2203d39, List of VATP applicants; Last update]

## Talking points

**To the CCO (Chief Compliance Officer)**
- Our AML Guideline says *should* is mandatory, the same as *must*. [S:7bfdad704174, para 1.6]
- Check each SPM module's classification. SB-1 is statutory; CRP-1 is a guidance note that gives way to the BCR. [S:8934af8cc884, cover, Classification]; [S:b7d630146e6c, para 1.1.4]

**To business heads**
- Conclusions papers are not law. The FSTB and SFC aim to put a dealing bill into LegCo in 2026. [S:6186c01c6649, p.4, Next step]
- The Budget said the same for the dealing and custodian regimes. [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 104]
- The conclusions state no plan to treat existing firms as licensed while they apply. They encourage early talks with the SFC or HKMA. [S:6186c01c6649, paras 31, 33-34]

**To the CEO**
- Hong Kong rules move from consultation to conclusions, bill, start date and transition. [S:54aa01e7396e, Introduction, para 1]; [S:0df2de5234dc, para 1] For stablecoins, consultation began on 27 December 2023. [S:54aa01e7396e, Introduction, para 1] The Ordinance started on 1 August 2025, about 19 months later. [S:0df2de5234dc, para 1]
- Planned bills in the Budget are stated intentions, not obligations. [S:654fa5eba8cf, paras 104, 108]

**To Risk / CRO (Chief Risk Officer)**
- LegCo's negative-vetting period for the cryptoasset capital rules expired without extension. The rules apply from 1 January 2026. [S:974899bbef4d, letter, paras 1-2]
- HKMA letters can change how capital guidance applies with immediate effect, as one did in June 2026. [S:dca53ff0a62c, p.1, paras 3-4]

## Common mix-ups

- **Myth:** "*Should* in HKMA guidance means best practice." **Fact:** In the AML Guideline, *should* is mandatory. [S:7bfdad704174, para 1.6]
- **Myth:** "All SPM modules have the same force." **Fact:** SB-1 is statutory. CRP-1 is non-statutory and gives way to the BCR. [S:8934af8cc884, cover, Classification]; [S:b7d630146e6c, para 1.1.4]
- **Myth:** "The June 2026 CRP-1 letter tightened the Group 1 tests." **Fact:** It widened the ways to meet para 2.6.4. [S:dca53ff0a62c, p.1, para 3] Group 1 is the class of cryptoassets that meets the CRP-1 classification conditions.
- **Myth:** "Once LegCo passes a law, it is in force." **Fact:** LegCo passed the AMLO amendments in December 2022. The HKMA said the relevant changes would start in June 2023. [S:b12bd88c7aee, letter, pp.1-2]
- **Myth:** "Existing firms can carry on under the new VA regimes while they apply." **Fact:** The dealing conclusions state no plan for that. [S:6186c01c6649, para 31]

## Read these first

1. **Guideline on AML/CFT (For Authorized Institutions), revised May 2023** — HKMA, 25 May 2023. This is the HKMA's guideline for banks on anti-money laundering and counter-financing of terrorism. Read Chapter 1, paras 1.1-1.8 and footnote 1. These parts set out how binding the text is and whom it binds. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20230525-4-EN/AML-2.pdf
2. **SPM CRP-1 Classification of Cryptoassets** — HKMA, 27 November 2025 (V.1, applies from 1 January 2026). Read the cover page and paras 1.1.4 and 1.4.1-1.4.2. They show how a guidance note sits under statutory rules. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20251125-15-EN/CRP-1.pdf
3. **Rules on cryptoassets standard and other updates** — HKMA, 15 August 2025. Read paras 1-2 of the letter. They give a short view of negative vetting and start dates. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/20250815-1-EN

**How to use paragraph references.** Cite HKMA SPM modules and guidelines by paragraph, for example CRP-1 para 2.1.2. HKMA circulars often have no numbered paragraphs. Cite them by heading and page, for example Implementation, p.2. [S:ed61d7c335e7, Implementation, p.2] SFC circulars number their paragraphs, for example joint circular para 31. [S:8a016a912528, para 31] BRDR landing pages (brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/…) link to the PDF and related documents. SFC circulars open from apps.sfc.hk/edistributionWeb by reference number, for example 23EC66.

## Open items

- The documents reviewed for this guide do not show how SFO section 399 guidelines are weighed in proceedings. They include no FAQ, code of practice or SFC Code of Conduct text on this point. This module does not state their legal effect beyond what the documents say.
- The CRP-1 text itself had not yet been updated for the June 2026 clarification at the date of the letter. [S:dca53ff0a62c, p.1, para 4]
- When the conclusions came out, the Government and the SFC had still to decide start dates for the VA dealing, custodian, advisory and management regimes. [S:6186c01c6649, para 32]; [S:f41a543388bc, para 49]; [S:01c5c5c4045f, para 64]
- The CARF bill had its First and Second Readings on 3 June 2026. [S:d5097f447cf9, para 2] LegCo adjourned the Second Reading debate (the debate on the bill's general principles). [S:d5097f447cf9, para 2] The documents reviewed for this guide do not record its passage.

## Related modules

[A1](#m-A1), [A3](#m-A3), [B1](#m-B1), [B2](#m-B2)

title: Where policy is heading
md:
For the bank's Head of Compliance (digital assets). After this module, you can say what each body has officially said it will do next, and by when. The bodies are the government, the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) and the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA). This module uses only their own words and dates.

## In 60 seconds

A short set of official strategy papers sets Hong Kong's direction on digital assets. The Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau (FSTB) issued a Policy Statement in 2022. [S:f587b828e3fa, para 4] It set out the government's founding principle for regulation (quoted in Key facts below). [S:f587b828e3fa, para 4] The FSTB's 2025 Policy Statement 2.0 added a framework called LEAP (four policy areas, spelled out in Key facts below). [S:a29b51bffc6b, paras 4-6] It also proposed the SFC as the lead licensing authority for digital-asset dealing and custody (holding assets for clients). [S:a29b51bffc6b, paras 4-6] The HKMA's role in that model is frontline regulator for banks, meaning the regulator that supervises them directly. [S:a29b51bffc6b, paras 4-6] ASPIRe (the SFC's roadmap for the digital-asset market, issued in Feb 2025) lists 12 initiatives. [S:d461c2db6af2, Executive Summary; Initiatives 3, 6-9, 11] Half of them are framed as things the SFC will explore or consider. [S:d461c2db6af2, Executive Summary; Initiatives 3, 6-9, 11] The HKMA closed its Fintech 2025 strategy and launched Fintech 2030. [S:1131a8814d96, photo caption] It then published a Fintech Promotion Blueprint (Feb 2026). [S:b0607b779270, para 1] It also asked bank boards to endorse a plan for their business model. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, p.2] The 2026-27 Budget and the 16 Sep 2026 Policy Address add dated targets. [S:654fa5eba8cf, paras 104, 109; S:ef3648ff1610, paras 35(ii), 50] These targets include a digital-asset licensing bill in 2026. [S:654fa5eba8cf, paras 104, 109] They also include upgrades to EnsembleTX (the HKMA's live pilot for settling tokenised money between banks). [S:654fa5eba8cf, paras 104, 109; S:ef3648ff1610, paras 35(ii), 50] The targets also cover tests of tokenised Exchange Fund Bills (short-term HKMA debt issued as digital tokens). [S:ef3648ff1610, paras 35(ii), 50]

## Status board

As of 25 Sep 2026.

| Instrument | Issuer | Date | Status (chip) | Applies to | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Policy Statement on Development of Virtual Assets in Hong Kong | FSTB | 31 Oct 2022 | Superseded | Whole market (Policy Statement 2.0 is the next phase) | [S:f587b828e3fa, p.6]; [S:a29b51bffc6b, para 3] |
| Fintech 2025 | HKMA | 8 Jun 2021 | Superseded | Banks (ended when the HKMA unveiled Fintech 2030) | [S:f8eed6b2e069, para 1]; [S:1131a8814d96, photo caption] |
| ASPIRe roadmap | SFC | 19 Feb 2025 | Exploratory | Virtual-asset service providers and SFC-regulated firms. Only the custody law timeline has a date. | [S:d461c2db6af2, Executive Summary; Pillar A, Initiative 1] |
| Policy Statement 2.0 (LEAP) | FSTB | 26 Jun 2025 | Stated target | Whole market; banks through the HKMA | [S:a29b51bffc6b, paras 4-6] |
| Fintech 2030 (DART) | HKMA | 3 Nov 2025 | Stated target | Banks | [S:1131a8814d96, para 3] |
| Fintech Promotion Blueprint | HKMA | 3 Feb 2026 | Stated target | Banks, fintech providers | [S:b0607b779270, paras 2-8] |
| Strategic Review of Business Models circular | HKMA | 9 Mar 2026 | In force | All authorized institutions | [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, p.2] |
| 2026-27 Budget | Financial Secretary | 25 Feb 2026 | Stated target | Whole market | [S:654fa5eba8cf, paras 104-114] |
| Chief Executive's 2026 Policy Address | Chief Executive | 16 Sep 2026 | Stated target | Whole market | [S:ef3648ff1610, paras 35, 49-51] |

Authorized institution: a bank or other deposit-taker authorized by the HKMA. Virtual asset: the legal term for crypto-type assets. Chip meanings: Superseded means a later document replaced it. Exploratory means ideas the regulator will study. Stated target means an official goal, not yet law. In force means it applies now.

## Key facts

- The 2022 Policy Statement said the government would follow the principle of "same activity, same risks, same regulation". [S:f587b828e3fa, paras 4, 6] It said its next step was a licensing regime for virtual-asset service providers. [S:f587b828e3fa, paras 4, 6]
- The 2022 Policy Statement also named stablecoins (tokens designed to hold a steady value) as another key area of focus. [S:f587b828e3fa, paras 9-10] It listed three pilots: issuing non-fungible tokens, tokenised government green bonds, and e-HKD (a possible central bank digital currency for public use). [S:f587b828e3fa, paras 9-10]
- Policy Statement 2.0 says the government will use the term *digital assets* instead of *virtual assets*. [S:a29b51bffc6b, footnote 1] The anti-money-laundering law still uses the legal term *virtual asset*. [S:f1bbafccd556, para 1.1] That law is the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (AMLO), section 53ZRA. [S:f1bbafccd556, para 1.1]
- LEAP stands for: Legal and regulatory streamlining; Expanding the suite of tokenised products; Advancing use cases and cross-sectoral collaboration; People and partnership development. [S:a29b51bffc6b, para 4]
- Policy Statement 2.0 proposes the SFC as the lead authority for licensing and registering digital-asset dealers and custodians. [S:a29b51bffc6b, paras 5-6] For banks, it names the HKMA as frontline regulator of their dealing and custody activities. [S:a29b51bffc6b, paras 5-6]
- Policy Statement 2.0 also said the government would propose laws on profits tax concessions (tax breaks). [S:a29b51bffc6b, para 15] Privately offered funds and family-owned investment holding vehicles already get these breaks. [S:a29b51bffc6b, para 15] The change is to extend them to cover specified digital assets. [S:a29b51bffc6b, para 15] The start date is the 2025/26 tax year, if the Legislative Council (LegCo) approves. [S:a29b51bffc6b, para 15]
- ASPIRe has five pillars and 12 initiatives. [S:d461c2db6af2, Executive Summary] The pillars are Access, Safeguards, Products, Infrastructure and Relationships. [S:d461c2db6af2, Executive Summary] ASPIRe says the government-led work to prepare laws for a custodian licensing regime aimed to finish by end-2025. [S:d461c2db6af2, Pillar A, Initiative 1]
- ASPIRe says the SFC will explore new custody standards. [S:d461c2db6af2, Pillar S, Initiative 3] The idea is standards that focus on outcomes and suit any technology, instead of fixed hardware and cold-storage ratios. [S:d461c2db6af2, Pillar S, Initiative 3] Cold storage means keeping the keys to client assets offline.
- Fintech 2030 has four pillars, known as DART, and over 40 initiatives. [S:1131a8814d96, paras 3-7] DART stands for Data and payment infrastructure, Artificial intelligence, Resilience and Tokenisation. [S:1131a8814d96, paras 3-7] The initiatives include regular issuance of tokenised government bonds and the Project Ensemble pilot. [S:1131a8814d96, paras 3-7]
- The Fintech Promotion Blueprint announced four flagship projects. [S:b0607b779270, paras 3, 4, 6] One is a Quantum Preparedness Index. [S:b0607b779270, paras 3, 4, 6] Another is a Fintech Cybersecurity Baseline for fintech firms using artificial intelligence and distributed ledger technology (DLT). [S:b0607b779270, paras 3, 4, 6] DLT is the shared-ledger technology behind blockchains.
- The HKMA expects each authorized institution's board to oversee and endorse a formal strategic business plan covering DLT and other technology change. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, p.2] The board has six months from the 9 March 2026 circular. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, p.2]
- The 2025 Policy Address set a target: a bill in LegCo in 2026 to license digital-asset dealing and custody service providers. [S:cc2fa9fc0772, Annex, New Indicators, item 22]
- The 2026-27 Budget repeated the plan for a licensing bill in 2026. [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 104] It said the government would change the Inland Revenue Ordinance over the coming two years. [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 108] The change puts into effect two international tax-reporting standards. [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 108] They are the amended Common Reporting Standard (CRS) and the Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF). [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 108] Both help tax authorities share information across borders. The bill was due in the first half of 2026. [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 108]
- CMU OmniClear: the company that runs the HKMA's Central Moneymarkets Unit (CMU), a system for holding and settling bonds. The Budget said CMU OmniClear would set up a digital asset platform in 2026. [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 114] The platform is for issuing and settling digital bonds. [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 114]
- The 2026 Policy Address says the HKMA will test tokenised Exchange Fund Bills by year-end. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(ii)] The tests are meant to help banks use more than HK$1.3 trillion of these bills more efficiently. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(ii)] Banks could then use them around the clock. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(ii)]
- The HKMA plans to add two features to EnsembleTX by around end-2026. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 50] One is settlement in central bank digital currency (CBDC). The other is round-the-clock operation. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 50] The HKMA will also keep exploring uses for tokenised deposits (bank deposits in digital token form). [S:ef3648ff1610, para 50]
- The Policy Address lists three SFC steps: [S:ef3648ff1610, paras 49(i), 49(iii), 51(iii)]
  - improve its virtual-asset licensing regimes; [S:ef3648ff1610, paras 49(i), 49(iii), 51(iii)]
  - promote trading of regulated stablecoins on licensed platforms; [S:ef3648ff1610, paras 49(i), 49(iii), 51(iii)]
  - start running its digital-asset custody monitoring system in the second half of 2026. [S:ef3648ff1610, paras 49(i), 49(iii), 51(iii)]
- The Customs and Excise Department aims to launch a Digital Asset Transaction Analytics System by 2029. [S:ef3648ff1610, Annex, New Indicators, item 209]

## What your bank must do

**Obligations**
- [ ] Have the board oversee and endorse a formal strategic business plan covering DLT and related technology. The deadline is six months after 9 March 2026. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, p.2]

**Controls & monitoring**
- [ ] Track the 2026 target for a bill to license digital-asset dealing and custody. [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 104] Policy Statement 2.0 proposes the SFC as lead licensing and registration authority, with the HKMA as frontline regulator for banks. [S:a29b51bffc6b, paras 5-6]
- [ ] Track the start dates proposed in the CARF bill. These are 1 Jan 2027 for the CARF part and 1 Jan 2028 for the amended CRS part. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, Clause 1(3)-(4)]

**Notify / consult HKMA or SFC**
- [ ] Discuss any new digital-asset activity with the HKMA before launch. The March 2026 circular restates this. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, p.2]
- [ ] Be ready to submit the business plan through the HKMA Survey Tool if invited. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, p.2]

**Counterparty due diligence**
- [ ] None set by the policy documents in this module. See B2 and B3 for the current rules.

## Talking points

**To the CCO (Chief Compliance Officer)**
- The 2026 licensing regime is still only a target. The bill has yet to go to LegCo. [S:cc2fa9fc0772, Annex, New Indicators, item 22] By contrast, the business-model circular already sets a board expectation for every authorized institution. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, p.2]
- The government now says *digital assets*, but AMLO still says *virtual asset*. [S:a29b51bffc6b, footnote 1]; [S:f1bbafccd556, para 1.1]

**To business heads**
- The SFC will promote trading of regulated stablecoins on licensed platforms. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 49(iii)] It will also promote their use to settle tokenised money market funds. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 49(iii)]
- EnsembleTX is to add CBDC settlement and 24/7 operation by around end-2026. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 50]

**To the CEO**
- The HKMA sees a chance for banks to link traditional finance and digital assets as a key intermediary. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, pp.1-2] It expects a board-endorsed plan. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, pp.1-2]
- The government's stated 2026 target is a bill to license digital-asset dealing and custody. [S:cc2fa9fc0772, Annex, New Indicators, item 22]

**To Risk / CRO (Chief Risk Officer)**
- The Blueprint's Quantum Preparedness Index measures how ready banks are for post-quantum cryptography. [S:b0607b779270, para 4] Post-quantum cryptography is encryption built to resist future quantum computers. The first index reading was 2.3 out of 10. [S:a50e9dc16dc7, slide 11]
- ASPIRe may shift custody rules toward outcome-based standards. That idea is still exploratory. [S:d461c2db6af2, Pillar S, Initiative 3]

## Common mix-ups

- **Myth:** "Policy Statement 2.0 changed the law." **Fact:** It sets directions. The tax breaks, for example, need LegCo approval. [S:a29b51bffc6b, para 15]
- **Myth:** "ASPIRe items are rules." **Fact:** Half of the 12 initiatives are framed as things the SFC will explore or consider. [S:d461c2db6af2, Initiatives 3, 6-9, 11]
- **Myth:** "The first stablecoin licences came in March 2026, as the Budget said." **Fact:** The Budget (25 Feb 2026) said the first licences would come the next month. [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 105] The HKMA granted them on 10 April 2026. [S:afb6cd0da6ff, para 1]
- **Myth:** "The business-model circular is about crypto only." **Fact:** It covers DLT, agentic AI (systems that act on their own) and cloud computing. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, pp.1-2] It also reminds banks to discuss new digital-asset activities before launch. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, pp.1-2]

## Read these first

1. **Policy Statement 2.0 on the Development of Digital Assets in Hong Kong** — FSTB, 26 Jun 2025. Read paras 3-6, 9-11, 15-16. It sets out the current government framework (LEAP) and each regulator's role. https://gia.info.gov.hk/general/202506/26/P2025062600269_500089_1_1750909574183.pdf
2. **Strategic Review of Business Models amid Digital Transformation** — HKMA, 9 Mar 2026. Read both pages. It is the one policy document here that asks something of your board. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20260309-1-EN/20260309-1-EN.pdf
3. **The Chief Executive's 2026 Policy Address** — 16 Sep 2026. Read paras 35, 49-51 and 99 (PDF pp.22-23, 26-27, 33). It has the latest dated targets for the HKMA, the SFC and CMU OmniClear. https://www.policyaddress.gov.hk/2026/public/pdf/policy/policy-full_en.pdf

## Open items

- The 2026 virtual-asset licensing bill was not in the documents reviewed for this guide by 25 Sep 2026. In June 2026 the government said it and the SFC would introduce the bill this year. [S:c6df52e680de, Reply part (3)] The bill is to cover providers of virtual-asset dealing, custody, advisory and management services. [S:c6df52e680de, Reply part (3)]
- The detailed documents for the Blueprint's Fintech Cybersecurity Baseline and Quantum Preparedness Index are not in the documents reviewed for this guide.
- The 2023 Policy Address does not mention virtual assets. Its nearest items are blockchain-based e-licences and a green fintech subsidy scheme. [S:61458655f37b, paras 41, 72(iv)]
- Locator correction: the 2026 Policy Address digital-bond items are in para 35(ii)-(iv) on p.23. One entry in our internal source notes says para 34. This module follows the Policy Address text.

## Related modules

[A1](#m-A1), [A2](#m-A2), [B2](#m-B2), [B3](#m-B3)

title: Your bank's legal status for digital assets
partTitle: Your bank as a regulated entity
md:
For the bank's Head of Compliance (digital assets). After this module you can explain the bank's legal role in each digital-asset activity. You can also say who supervises each activity and which rules bind which company in the group.

## In 60 seconds

A bank in Hong Kong is an Authorized Institution (AI). The Banking Ordinance governs how it is authorized and supervised. [S:8934af8cc884, para 2.1.1] Some banks carry on "regulated activities", a term the Securities and Futures Ordinance (SFO) defines. A bank doing so must register with the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) as a Registered Institution (RI). [S:8934af8cc884, paras 2.1.2-2.1.3] The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) is the RI's front-line (day-to-day) supervisor. Its Supervisory Policy Manual (SPM) module SB-1 explains how. [S:8934af8cc884, paras 2.1.2-2.1.3] A company the SFC licenses under SFO section 116 or 117 is a Licensed Corporation (LC). [S:8934af8cc884, para 1.1.1] The joint SFC–HKMA circulars on virtual-asset (VA) activities address "intermediaries". That term covers both licensed corporations (LCs) and registered institutions (RIs). [S:8934af8cc884, para 1.1.1; S:8a016a912528, para 31] Under the proposed VA dealing and custody regimes, banks would register with the SFC, with the HKMA as their frontline regulator. [S:f673ef6dcb63, paras 1.10, 2.36; S:30b60438f017, para 2.12(a)] VA custodians owned by locally incorporated banks would be regulated by the SFC instead. [S:f673ef6dcb63, paras 1.10, 2.36; S:30b60438f017, para 2.12(a)] Some May 2026 HKMA circulars go to all authorized institutions (AIs), and others only to RIs. So always check which firms a circular covers. [S:1babdb609fc8, p.1; S:a0bd48559762, p.1]

## Status board

As of 25 September 2026.

| Instrument | Issuer | Date | Status (chip) | Applies to | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SPM SB-1 (V.4) Supervision of SFC-registered AIs | HKMA | 12 Sep 2025 | In force | RIs | [S:8934af8cc884, cover, Application] |
| Guideline on Anti-Money Laundering (AML) and Counter-Financing of Terrorism (CFT) for AIs | HKMA | 25 May 2023 | In force | All AIs, including RIs | [S:7bfdad704174, para 1.3] |
| Joint circular on VA-related activities, plus supplement | SFC + HKMA | 22 Dec 2023; 30 Sep 2025 | In force (changed for Relevant Stablecoins by the 27 May 2026 RI circular) | LCs; RIs | [S:8a016a912528, para 31]; [S:b79266f3da51, para 4]; [S:a0bd48559762, p.2] |
| RI circular: Relevant Stablecoins | HKMA (formulated jointly with SFC) | 27 May 2026 | In force | RIs only | [S:a0bd48559762, p.1; footnote 3, p.2] |
| AI letter: Relevant Stablecoin-related activities | HKMA | 27 May 2026 | In force | All AIs | [S:1babdb609fc8, p.1] |
| RI circular: VA financing, shared order book, withdrawals | HKMA | 27 May 2026 | In force | RIs only | [S:e64b7b0267b2, p.1] |
| Custody guidance (updated) | HKMA | 27 May 2026 | In force | AIs, plus subsidiaries of locally incorporated AIs | [S:ed61d7c335e7, p.2] |
| VA dealing regime (banks register; HKMA is frontline regulator) | Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau (FSTB) + SFC | 24 Dec 2025 | Conclusions published | Banks and stored value facilities register. LCs, RIs and SFC-licensed VA trading platforms (VATPs) get fast-track approval | [S:f673ef6dcb63, paras 1.10, 2.36]; [S:6186c01c6649, paras 35-36] |
| VA custodian regime | FSTB + SFC | 24 Dec 2025 | Conclusions published | Banks, bank subsidiaries, custodians | [S:30b60438f017, paras 2.12(a), 2.48]; [S:f41a543388bc, para 41] |
| VA advisory and management regimes | FSTB + SFC | 24 Dec 2025 (proposal); 26 May 2026 (conclusions) | Conclusions published | Proposal: only banks could register (others licensed) | [S:6186c01c6649, footnotes 9-10]; [S:01c5c5c4045f, Introduction, p.3] |

## Key facts

- An AI that carries on business in regulated activities is required to register with the SFC as an RI. The SFC registers AIs under SFO section 119. [S:8934af8cc884, paras 2.1.2, 2.2.1]
- The SFC holds ultimate responsibility for RIs. The HKMA is the RI's front-line supervisor. Under SFO section 5(3), the SFC may rely on the HKMA's supervision. [S:8934af8cc884, para 2.1.3]
- Each RI needs at least two executive officers for each regulated activity. Executive officers are the senior staff who directly supervise that activity. [S:8934af8cc884, paras 1.1.1, 2.2.4]
- Each executive officer needs the written consent of the Monetary Authority (MA). At least one of them must be available at all times. [S:8934af8cc884, paras 1.1.1, 2.2.4]
- Only people entered on the HKMA Register (the HKMA's public list of RI staff) may perform a regulated function for an RI. So the RI should submit their details before they start. [S:8934af8cc884, paras 4.3.1, 4.3.5]
- An associated entity is a company linked to an RI through control that receives or holds the RI's client assets in Hong Kong. [S:8934af8cc884, para 1.1.1]
- An RI should tell the SFC and HKMA if it plans to start any VA activity. It should also tell them before changing one, including the type of clients it serves. [S:8934af8cc884, para 5.6]
- The HKMA AML/CFT Guideline applies to all AIs, including RIs. [S:7bfdad704174, para 1.3 and footnote 1]
- RIs, and associated entities that are AIs, must also take into account the SFC's AML/CFT guideline. That includes its Chapter 12 on virtual assets. [S:7bfdad704174, para 1.3 and footnote 1]
- The joint circular addresses intermediaries, meaning LCs and RIs. [S:8a016a912528, para 31]; [S:8934af8cc884, para 1.1.1]
- The joint circular reminds intermediaries to tell the SFC (and the HKMA, where relevant) before starting or changing VA activities. [S:8a016a912528, para 31]; [S:8934af8cc884, para 1.1.1]
- The September 2025 supplement lets LCs and RIs offer staking to clients they deal in virtual assets for. Staking means locking up clients' tokens to help run a blockchain, in return for rewards. [S:b79266f3da51, paras 4-5]
- Firms may offer staking only through segregated (ring-fenced) accounts. Those accounts are held with an SFC-licensed platform, an AI, or a subsidiary of a locally incorporated AI. [S:b79266f3da51, paras 4-5]
- The May 2026 Relevant Stablecoin circular is addressed to RIs. Relevant Stablecoins are stablecoins issued by HKMA-licensed issuers. [S:a0bd48559762, p.1; footnote 3, p.2]
- That circular's VA dealing, advisory and asset management rules do not apply to AIs that are not RIs. The same goes for the joint circulars' rules. [S:a0bd48559762, p.1; footnote 3, p.2]
- Those rules also do not apply to an HKMA-licensed issuer for the coin it issues itself. The HKMA expects these firms to meet similar standards that it issues separately. [S:a0bd48559762, p.1; footnote 3, p.2]
- A separate HKMA letter covers all AIs that deal in, advise on or manage portfolios of Relevant Stablecoins. They should follow the RI standards. [S:1babdb609fc8, p.1; Implementation, p.2]
- The same letter reminds these AIs to discuss their plans with the HKMA in advance. [S:1babdb609fc8, p.1; Implementation, p.2]
- Under the Stablecoins Ordinance, only specified licensed institutions may offer a fiat-referenced stablecoin (one tied to an official currency) in Hong Kong. [S:35e1ac2b815a, para 3]
- The HKMA register of licensed stablecoin issuers lists The Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation Limited. Its licence is FRS02, effective 10 Apr 2026. [S:270f1f7324ab, Register table]
- The HKMA's guideline for licensed stablecoin issuers sets board expectations in para 7.1.3. These include having at least one-third independent non-executive directors. Those expectations do not apply to a licensed issuer that is an AI. [S:240be6833157, para 7.1.3]
- Such an issuer should follow the Banking Ordinance and related guidance instead. [S:240be6833157, para 7.1.3]
- The June 2025 VA dealing proposal said banks would have to register with the SFC. The SFC would register them in consultation with the HKMA. [S:f673ef6dcb63, para 1.10]
- The proposal also said the HKMA would be the frontline regulator for banks' VA dealing, with powers to inspect premises and investigate suspected breaches. [S:f673ef6dcb63, para 2.36]
- For VA custody, the proposal made the HKMA the frontline regulator for banks. VA custodians owned by locally incorporated banks would be regulated by the SFC. [S:30b60438f017, para 2.12(a)]
- The December 2025 custody conclusions describe a minimum capital level (a floor) for custodians: HK$10m paid-up capital and HK$3m liquid capital. [S:f41a543388bc, paras 41-42]
- The conclusions exempt banks from that floor because existing HKMA capital requirements already apply to them. [S:f41a543388bc, paras 41-42]
- The December 2025 further consultation proposed that only banks could register with the SFC, rather than be licensed, for VA advisory or VA management services. [S:6186c01c6649, footnotes 9-10]

## What your bank must do

**Obligations**
- [ ] Hold SFC registration for each regulated activity the bank carries on. [S:8934af8cc884, paras 2.2.1, 2.2.4]
- [ ] Have at least two executive officers per activity, each with HKMA consent. [S:8934af8cc884, paras 2.2.1, 2.2.4]
- [ ] Register relevant individuals (staff who carry out the RI's regulated activities) on the HKMA Register before they start. [S:8934af8cc884, paras 4.3.1, 4.3.5]
- [ ] Apply the HKMA AML/CFT Guideline across the whole bank. [S:7bfdad704174, footnote 1]
- [ ] For the RI and any associated entities that are AIs, also take into account Chapter 12 of the SFC AML/CFT guideline. [S:7bfdad704174, footnote 1]
- [ ] If the bank is locally incorporated, check that its subsidiaries meet the HKMA standards when they provide digital-asset custody or staking from custody. [S:ed61d7c335e7, p.2]; [S:4641e6c404d2, p.1]

**Controls & monitoring**
- [ ] Before applying a circular, map each digital-asset activity to the company and role doing it: AI, RI, LC subsidiary or associated entity. [S:a0bd48559762, footnote 3, p.2]
- [ ] Keep the relevant-individual database up to date. [S:8934af8cc884, paras 4.3.3, 4.3.6, 5.5]
- [ ] Report Register changes and specified fitness information within 7 business days. [S:8934af8cc884, paras 4.3.3, 4.3.6, 5.5]

**Notify / consult HKMA or SFC**
- [ ] Tell the SFC and HKMA before starting or changing VA activities. [S:8934af8cc884, para 5.6]
- [ ] Tell the HKMA in advance before applying to the SFC for registration. [S:8934af8cc884, para 2.2.3]
- [ ] Consider early contact with the SFC or HKMA before applying under the coming dealing regime. The conclusions encourage this. [S:6186c01c6649, para 33]

**Counterparty due diligence**
- [ ] Check that any stablecoin issuer you deal with is on the HKMA register. [S:270f1f7324ab, Register note]
- [ ] Check that VA dealing partners are SFC-licensed VATPs. [S:8a016a912528, para 17]; [S:a0bd48559762, para (1), p.3]
- [ ] For Relevant Stablecoins only, treat the HKMA-licensed issuer of that coin as an allowed dealing partner too. [S:8a016a912528, para 17]; [S:a0bd48559762, para (1), p.3]

## Talking points

**To the Chief Compliance Officer (CCO)**
- Our VA conduct rules apply to us because we are an RI. The HKMA supervises us; the SFC keeps ultimate responsibility. [S:8934af8cc884, para 2.1.3]
- Check who each paper covers. The May 2026 Relevant Stablecoin circular is addressed to RIs. The separate stablecoin letter covers all AIs. [S:a0bd48559762, p.1; footnote 3, p.2]; [S:1babdb609fc8, p.1]

**To business heads**
- As an RI, we should tell the SFC and HKMA when we plan to start or change VA services. [S:8934af8cc884, para 5.6]
- Under the proposed custodian regime, the SFC would regulate a custody subsidiary. The HKMA would be frontline regulator for the bank itself. [S:30b60438f017, para 2.12(a)]

**To the CEO**
- Under the proposed dealing and custody regimes, the SFC would license and register providers. The HKMA would be frontline regulator for banks. [S:a29b51bffc6b, paras 5-6]
- The MA can withdraw or suspend an executive officer's consent for misconduct. Each regulated activity must always have at least one executive officer available. [S:8934af8cc884, paras 2.2.4, 6.3]

**To Risk / Chief Risk Officer (CRO)**
- A bank VA custodian would use existing HKMA capital rules, not the custodian capital floor. [S:f41a543388bc, para 41]
- The RI financing circular requires loans secured only by virtual assets to be treated as clean (unsecured) loans for capital purposes. [S:e64b7b0267b2, para (9), p.5]

## Common mix-ups

- **Myth:** "SFC AML Chapter 12 binds the whole bank." **Fact:** It reaches only RIs, and associated entities that are AIs. They must take it into account, but it does not bind the rest of the bank. [S:7bfdad704174, footnote 1]
- **Myth:** "The joint circular is an SFC rule for brokers, not us." **Fact:** It addresses RIs too. It reaches banks through HKMA frontline supervision. [S:8a016a912528, para 31]; [S:8934af8cc884, paras 1.1.1, 2.1.3]
- **Myth:** "The May 2026 RI stablecoin circular covers all AIs." **Fact:** It is addressed to RIs. A separate HKMA letter covers AIs that are not RIs. [S:a0bd48559762, p.1; footnote 3, p.2]; [S:1babdb609fc8, p.1]
- **Myth:** "A custodian owned by a bank is supervised like the bank." **Fact:** Under the proposal, the SFC would regulate it. [S:30b60438f017, para 2.12(a)]
- **Myth:** "VA financing rules apply to every AI." **Fact:** The May 2026 financing circular is addressed to RIs. [S:e64b7b0267b2, p.1-2]

## Read these first

1. **SPM SB-1 Supervision of Regulated Activities of SFC-Registered AIs (V.4)** — HKMA, 12 Sep 2025. Read paras 1.1.1, 2.1-2.2, 4.3, 4.16.1 and 5.6. This is the rulebook for your RI status. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20250909-3-EN/SB-1.PDF
2. **Public Consultation on Legislative Proposal to Regulate Dealing in Virtual Assets** — FSTB/SFC, 27 Jun 2025. Read paras 1.10 and 2.36. They show how banks would be registered and supervised. https://www.fstb.gov.hk/fsb/en/publication/consult/doc/VADEALING_consultation_paper_en.pdf
3. **Virtual asset-related activities in relation to relevant stablecoins** — HKMA, 27 May 2026. Read footnote 3 (p.2), paras (1)-(4) and Implementation (p.9). It is a worked example of a circular that covers RIs only. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20260527-2-EN/20260527-2-EN.pdf

## Open items

- On 24 Jun 2026 the Government said it would put a bill to the Legislative Council this year. The bill would cover the VA dealing, custodian, advisory and management regimes. [S:c6df52e680de, Reply part (3)]
- The documents reviewed hold no bill text. So the final rules on how banks register are not yet in law. [S:c6df52e680de, Reply part (3)]
- The HKMA and SFC documents reviewed do not say how registration under the new VA regimes will fit with an RI's existing SFO registration. They mention only fast-track approval. [S:6186c01c6649, paras 35-36]; [S:01c5c5c4045f, para 67]
- The documents reviewed do not include the Banking Ordinance or SFO text on executive officers. SB-1 is the only source used here.

## Related modules

[A1](#m-A1), [A2](#m-A2), [B2](#m-B2), [B3](#m-B3)

title: Engaging the HKMA and SFC
partTitle: Your bank as a regulated entity
md:
For the bank's Head of Compliance (digital assets): the HKMA (Hong Kong Monetary Authority) and the SFC (Securities and Futures Commission) are your two regulators. After this module you can list the main duties to talk to a regulator before acting on digital-asset plans. You can also explain the HKMA's engagement channels: the Supervisory Incubator, the 2026 business-model review and the superseded (replaced) stablecoin issuer sandbox.

## In 60 seconds

In HKMA rules, banks are called authorized institutions (AIs). Virtual assets (VAs) are crypto tokens and similar digital assets. Since January 2022, the HKMA has expected any bank planning a virtual-asset (VA) activity to discuss it with the HKMA first. [S:642680fa4467, AIs' VA-related proposals section, p.5] The bank should get the HKMA's feedback on its risk controls before launch. [S:642680fa4467, AIs' VA-related proposals section, p.5]

Later HKMA circulars (formal letters to banks) repeat this discuss-first step for:
- tokenised products (assets recorded as digital tokens on a blockchain) [S:b2719f3dcb37, Implementation, p.6]
- custody (holding digital assets for clients) [S:ed61d7c335e7, Implementation, p.2]
- staking (locking up tokens to help run a blockchain, in return for rewards) [S:4641e6c404d2, p.3, Implementation]
- services in Relevant Stablecoins (stablecoins issued under an HKMA licence) [S:1babdb609fc8, Implementation, p.2]

Some banks are also registered with the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) for securities business. These banks are called registered institutions (RIs). A bank acting as a registered institution (RI) should tell both regulators before it starts or changes VA dealing, advice or asset management. [S:8934af8cc884, para 5.6]

The capital rules (rules on how much capital a bank holds against its risks) add a separate trigger. A bank must notify the HKMA when it acquires a new type of cryptoasset. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2]

For distributed ledger technology (DLT) projects, the HKMA runs a Supervisory Incubator. [S:1b1a0de5de5a, para 3] DLT means shared digital records, such as blockchains. The Incubator offers a dedicated HKMA team and optional live trials. [S:1b1a0de5de5a, para 3]

In March 2026 the HKMA said it expects every bank's board to endorse a strategic business plan on digital change within six months. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, para 4]

## Status board

As of 25 Sep 2026.

| Instrument | Issuer | Date | Status (chip) | Applies to | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| AIs' interface with VAs and VA service providers (VASPs) | HKMA | 28 Jan 2022 | In force | All Authorized Institutions (AIs) | [S:642680fa4467, p.5] |
| Joint circular on intermediaries' VA-related activities | SFC + HKMA | 22 Dec 2023 | In force | Licensed corporations (LCs); RIs via HKMA | [S:8a016a912528, para 31] |
| Sale and distribution of tokenised products | HKMA | 20 Feb 2024 | In force | AIs | [S:b2719f3dcb37, Implementation, p.6] |
| Custody circular (first version) | HKMA | 20 Feb 2024 | Superseded | AIs | [S:ed61d7c335e7, Implementation, p.2] |
| Updated custody guidance and Annex | HKMA | 27 May 2026 | In force | AIs and subsidiaries of local AIs | [S:ed61d7c335e7, Implementation, p.2] |
| Staking from custodial services | HKMA | 7 Apr 2025 | In force | AIs and subsidiaries of local AIs | [S:4641e6c404d2, p.3, Implementation] |
| Supervisory Incubator for DLT | HKMA | 8 Jan 2025 | Pilot | AIs | [S:1b1a0de5de5a, paras 2-3] |
| Supervisory Policy Manual (SPM) SB-1 (V.4) | HKMA | 12 Sep 2025 | In force | RIs | [S:8934af8cc884, para 5.6] |
| Supplemental joint circular | SFC + HKMA | 30 Sep 2025 | In force | LCs; RIs | [S:b79266f3da51, para 10] |
| SPM CRP-1 Classification of Cryptoassets | HKMA | 27 Nov 2025 (applies from 1 Jan 2026) | In force | All AIs | [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2] |
| SPM CR-L-5 Major Acquisitions (V.3) | HKMA | 27 Nov 2025 | In force | Locally incorporated AIs | [S:13365a31e794, para 1.1 and fn 1] |
| Strategic Review of Business Models | HKMA | 9 Mar 2026 | In force | All AIs | [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, para 4] |
| RI circular and AI letter on Relevant Stablecoins | HKMA (with SFC) | 27 May 2026 | In force | RIs; all AIs | [S:a0bd48559762, Implementation, p.9]; [S:1babdb609fc8, Implementation, p.2] |
| SFC circular 26EC26 on Relevant Stablecoin services | SFC | 27 May 2026 | In force | VA trading platforms (VATPs); LCs | [S:19d52ade6849, para 12] |
| Stablecoin issuer sandbox | HKMA | 12 Mar 2024 | Superseded | Would-be issuers | [S:28616d929735, opening para] |

## Key facts

- A bank planning any VA activity should discuss it with the HKMA, and with other regulators where relevant, before launch. [S:642680fa4467, AIs' VA-related proposals section, p.5] The bank should get feedback on its risk controls before launch. [S:642680fa4467, AIs' VA-related proposals section, p.5]
- Before selling or issuing tokenised products, a bank should have policies and controls in place and discuss its plans with the HKMA in advance. [S:b2719f3dcb37, Implementation, p.6]
- A bank, or a local bank's subsidiary, that intends to offer digital-asset custody should first discuss it with the HKMA. [S:ed61d7c335e7, Implementation, p.2] It should also satisfy the HKMA that it meets the custody standards in the guidance's Annex. [S:ed61d7c335e7, Implementation, p.2]
- The February 2024 custody circular asked existing custodians to confirm compliance to the HKMA within six months. [S:6bccca749ac2, Implementation, p.2] The May 2026 letter supersedes (replaces) that circular. [S:ed61d7c335e7, Implementation, p.2] The new letter simply asks existing custodians to review and revise their controls. [S:ed61d7c335e7, Implementation, p.2]
- Before offering staking from custody, a bank should have adequate policies and controls and discuss its plans with the HKMA in advance. [S:4641e6c404d2, p.3, Implementation]
- Intermediaries (firms licensed or registered with the SFC, including RIs) should give the SFC advance notice before starting or changing VA activities. [S:8a016a912528, para 31] Where relevant, they should also give the HKMA advance notice. [S:8a016a912528, para 31] A change in client type counts as a change. [S:8a016a912528, para 31]
- The September 2025 supplementary joint circular lists changes that need prior notice: [S:b79266f3da51, para 10]
  - a change in client type
  - first VA deposits or withdrawals
  - first staking service
  - first subscriptions or redemptions (buying into or cashing out of a product) paid in VAs
  - other material changes
- SB-1 is the Supervisory Policy Manual (SPM) chapter on supervising RIs. It expects an RI to tell the SFC and the HKMA when it plans to start or change VA activities. [S:8934af8cc884, para 5.6]
- An RI needs at least two executive officers (senior staff who directly supervise the business) for each regulated activity. [S:8934af8cc884, paras 2.2.4, 4.3.9-4.3.10] Each executive officer needs written consent from the Monetary Authority (MA), applied for through the HKMA. [S:8934af8cc884, paras 2.2.4, 4.3.9-4.3.10]
- RIs should give the HKMA and SFC advance notice before they do any of these: [S:a0bd48559762, Implementation, p.9]
  - distribute products linked to Relevant Stablecoins
  - deal in, advise on or manage Relevant Stablecoins
  - materially change those arrangements
- All AIs, not only RIs, should discuss Relevant Stablecoin dealing, advice or portfolio management with the HKMA before starting. [S:1babdb609fc8, Implementation, p.2]
- CRP-1 is the SPM chapter on classifying cryptoassets. Under CRP-1, a bank that acquires a new type of cryptoasset must notify the HKMA. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2] It must treat the asset as Group 2b (the group with the strictest capital treatment) until the HKMA agrees to the bank's own classification. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2]
- A locally incorporated AI (one set up in Hong Kong) needs the MA's written consent for some share purchases. [S:13365a31e794, para 1.1 and fn 1] Consent is needed when the shares bought are worth at least 5% of the bank's own Tier 1 capital (its core capital). [S:13365a31e794, para 1.1 and fn 1] Equity-like cryptoassets (tokens that act like shares) count as shares for this test. [S:13365a31e794, para 1.1 and fn 1]
- The HKMA launched the Supervisory Incubator on 8 January 2025. [S:1b1a0de5de5a, paras 2-3] The Incubator gives banks one supervisory contact point to confirm DLT risk controls before a full launch. [S:1b1a0de5de5a, paras 2-3] Live trials are optional. [S:1b1a0de5de5a, paras 2-3] Tokenised deposits (bank deposits recorded as digital tokens) were an initial focus. [S:1b1a0de5de5a, paras 2-3]
- Incubator participants may get some supervisory flexibility, decided case by case. [S:fae36c380174, p.1 and fn 2]
- The HKMA expects each bank's board to oversee and endorse a formal strategic business plan for these technology changes. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, para 4] The deadline is six months from 9 March 2026. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, para 4]
- The same March 2026 circular repeats that banks should discuss new digital-asset activities with the HKMA before launch. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, para 5]
- The stablecoin issuer sandbox (March 2024) let would-be issuers test their plans on a limited scale. [S:28616d929735, Testing in the sandbox section, paras 1-2] Admission did not mean HKMA endorsement or regulation. [S:28616d929735, Testing in the sandbox section, paras 1-2] A licence would need a separate application. [S:28616d929735, Testing in the sandbox section, paras 1-2]
- The HKMA later said sandbox participation is not a condition for a licence and does not guarantee one. [S:e0b249a7eb8c, Licensing regime section, para 5]

## What your bank must do

**Obligations**
- [ ] Discuss each new VA product or service with the HKMA before launch, and get its feedback on risk controls. [S:642680fa4467, p.5]
- [ ] Have the board oversee and endorse the strategic business plan that the March 2026 circular asks for. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, para 4]
- [ ] Get the MA's written consent for each RI executive officer, applying through the HKMA. [S:8934af8cc884, para 2.2.4]

**Controls & monitoring**
- [ ] Track the changes that trigger prior notice: new client type, first VA deposits or withdrawals, first staking, first VA-funded subscriptions and other material changes. [S:b79266f3da51, para 10]
- [ ] If the bank already offers custody, review and revise its controls against the 2026 Annex. [S:ed61d7c335e7, Implementation, p.2]
- [ ] If a cryptoasset stops meeting the conditions for its HKMA-agreed group (1a, 1b or 2a), move it to Group 2b at once. [S:b7d630146e6c, paras 2.1.3, 2.1.5] Any later move to another group needs the HKMA's agreement. [S:b7d630146e6c, paras 2.1.3, 2.1.5]

**Notify / consult HKMA or SFC**
- [ ] Discuss tokenised products, custody and staking with the HKMA in advance. [S:b2719f3dcb37, p.6]; [S:ed61d7c335e7, p.2]; [S:4641e6c404d2, p.3]
- [ ] Notify the SFC and the HKMA in advance of RI VA activities and of changes to them. [S:8934af8cc884, para 5.6]; [S:8a016a912528, para 31]
- [ ] Relevant Stablecoin activities: if the bank is an RI, notify the HKMA and SFC. [S:a0bd48559762, p.9] Every bank: discuss them with the HKMA. [S:1babdb609fc8, p.2]
- [ ] Notify the HKMA when the bank acquires a new type of cryptoasset. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2]
- [ ] Seek consent before taking a stake in equity-like tokens worth 5% or more of Tier 1 capital. [S:13365a31e794, paras 1.1, 2.9.1] Give the MA at least one month's notice of other significant acquisitions. [S:13365a31e794, paras 1.1, 2.9.1]

**Counterparty due diligence**
- [ ] Do not treat a firm's sandbox status as a licence. [S:28616d929735, Testing in the sandbox section, para 2] Check the HKMA's Register of Licensed Stablecoin Issuers instead. [S:afb6cd0da6ff, paras 4-5]

## Talking points

**To the CCO**
- Every new VA, tokenisation, custody, staking or stablecoin launch starts with an HKMA discussion. [S:642680fa4467, p.5] For RI activities, the SFC and HKMA also expect advance notice. [S:8934af8cc884, para 5.6]
- The 2026 custody letter dropped the six-month confirmation. [S:ed61d7c335e7, Implementation, p.2] Existing custodians should review and revise their controls instead. [S:ed61d7c335e7, Implementation, p.2]

**To business heads**
- We talk to the HKMA before go-live on any new digital-asset activity. The March 2026 circular restates that step. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, para 5]
- We should flag a new client type to the SFC in advance, and to the HKMA where relevant. [S:b79266f3da51, para 10] The same goes for our first VA deposits, staking or VA-funded subscriptions. [S:b79266f3da51, para 10]

**To the CEO**
- The HKMA asked each board to endorse a digital-transformation business plan within six months of 9 March 2026. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, para 4]
- The Supervisory Incubator gives us a dedicated HKMA team for feedback before a full DLT launch. [S:1b1a0de5de5a, para 3] Live trials there are optional. [S:1b1a0de5de5a, para 3]

**To Risk / CRO**
- We must notify the HKMA when we acquire a new type of cryptoasset. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2] The asset sits in Group 2b until the HKMA agrees with our classification. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2]
- Equity-like tokens count as shares for the 5%-of-Tier-1 consent test. [S:13365a31e794, fn 1]

## Common mix-ups

- **Myth:** Telling the SFC is enough. **Fact:** SB-1 expects RIs to tell both regulators. [S:8934af8cc884, para 5.6] The HKMA's own circulars add a discuss-first step. [S:642680fa4467, p.5]
- **Myth:** The advance-notice rule in SFC circular 26EC26, on admitting Relevant Stablecoins, binds us. **Fact:** That circular is addressed to VATPs and LCs. [S:19d52ade6849, para 12] For RIs, the HKMA's RI circular sets the advance-notice duty. [S:a0bd48559762, Implementation, p.9]
- **Myth:** Every crypto trade needs a CRP-1 notice. **Fact:** Only a new type of cryptoasset does. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2 and fn 7] A first Bitcoin position triggers a notice. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2 and fn 7] Bitcoin futures after existing spot (direct) holdings do not. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2 and fn 7]
- **Myth:** The six-month custody confirmation still applies. **Fact:** It belonged to the 2024 circular. [S:6bccca749ac2, Implementation, p.2] That circular has been superseded. [S:ed61d7c335e7, Implementation, p.2]
- **Myth:** Incubator or sandbox entry means approval. **Fact:** Incubator flexibility is case by case. [S:fae36c380174, p.1] Sandbox admission was not an endorsement. [S:28616d929735, Testing in the sandbox section, para 2]

## Read these first

1. **Regulatory approaches to AIs' interface with VAs and VASPs**, HKMA, 28 Jan 2022. Read pp.3-5, ending with the AIs' VA-related proposals section. This is where the discuss-first expectation starts. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/20220128-1-EN
2. **SPM SB-1 Supervision of Regulated Activities of SFC-Registered AIs (V.4)**, HKMA, 12 Sep 2025. Read paras 2.1.3, 2.2.4, 4.3 and 5.6. It sets the RI duties to notify regulators and to get consent for executive officers. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20250909-3-EN/SB-1.PDF
3. **HKMA circular to RIs on VA-related activities involving Relevant Stablecoins**, HKMA, 27 May 2026. Read Background (pp.1-2) and Implementation (p.9). It sets the newest advance-notice duty. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20260527-2-EN/20260527-2-EN.pdf

## Open items

- The documents reviewed for this guide contain no HKMA form, template or response timeline for the discuss-first step.
- The six-month window in the March 2026 business-model circular ran to about 9 September 2026. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, para 4] No document reviewed for this guide shows any HKMA follow-up on these plans.
- No document reviewed for this guide has a public list of Supervisory Incubator participants.
- The December 2025 consultation conclusions on VA custodian services cover banks that safekeep private keys (the secret codes that control crypto) for client VAs. [S:f41a543388bc, paras 35(b), 65] They also cover subsidiaries of locally incorporated banks that do so. [S:f41a543388bc, paras 35(b), 65] These firms would need a licence or registration under the proposed regime. [S:f41a543388bc, paras 35(b), 65] The stated aim is to introduce a bill into the Legislative Council in 2026. [S:f41a543388bc, paras 35(b), 65] No bill text is in the documents reviewed for this guide (see A1).

## Related modules

[A1](#m-A1), [B1](#m-B1), [B3](#m-B3), [C1](#m-C1), [C3](#m-C3), [C4](#m-C4)

title: Governance, risk and technology expectations
partTitle: Your bank as a regulated entity
md:
This module is for the bank's Head of Compliance (digital assets). After it, you can explain what the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) expects in four areas. You can also point to the paragraph for each:

- the board's role;
- risk assessment of new products;
- distributed ledger technology (DLT), the shared-database technology behind crypto, and vendor risk;
