- control of private keys (the secret codes that move digital assets).

## In 60 seconds

The HKMA's Supervisory Policy Manual (SPM) has a Pillar 2 module, CA-G-5. [S:349a543ae2f0, Application, p.1; para 4.2.8, p.63] Pillar 2 is the HKMA's review of whether a bank holds enough capital for all its risks. [S:349a543ae2f0, Application, p.1; para 4.2.8, p.63] CA-G-5 applies to locally incorporated authorized institutions (AIs), meaning banks and deposit-takers set up as companies in Hong Kong. [S:349a543ae2f0, Application, p.1; para 4.2.8, p.63] CA-G-5 says the board and senior management should understand the risks of new or complex activities. [S:349a543ae2f0, Application, p.1; para 4.2.8, p.63] It names cryptoasset activities as an example. [S:349a543ae2f0, Application, p.1; para 4.2.8, p.63]

The HKMA has a guideline on anti-money laundering (AML) and counter-financing of terrorism (CFT). [S:7bfdad704174, paras 1.6, 2.10-2.11] Before any new product, business practice or technology goes live, that guideline requires a risk assessment. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 1.6, 2.10-2.11] The assessment covers money laundering (ML) and terrorist financing (TF) risks. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 1.6, 2.10-2.11]

For DLT, the HKMA published ten risk considerations in April 2024, and they are not binding. [S:cd5d66ba08a2, p.2] It followed with a longer research study in March 2025. [S:e0fd558b3dbc, Introduction, p.4]

Circulars on custody (holding assets for clients), staking and tokenised products add concrete expectations. They cover vendor due diligence (checks on suppliers) and key management. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(a), (b), (i), (l) and fn 8]; [S:4641e6c404d2, section C, pp.2-3]; [S:b2719f3dcb37, Section A, p.3] The main key-management expectations are:

- keys held in tamper-resistant devices; [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(a), (b), (i)]
- keys generated and backed up in Hong Kong; [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(a), (b), (i)]
- no "single point of failure" (one part whose loss stops everything); [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(a), (b), (i)]
- 98% of client virtual assets (VA) in cold storage, with keys kept offline. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(l) and fn 8]

If a bank's capital or risk management around cryptoassets falls short, the HKMA may consider extra measures. [S:349a543ae2f0, para 3.6.6] These include capital add-ons (extra capital), provisioning (money set aside for losses), limits or other measures. [S:349a543ae2f0, para 3.6.6]

## Status board

As of 25 September 2026.

| Instrument | Issuer | Date | Status (chip) | Applies to | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SPM CA-G-5 Supervisory Review Process (V.7) | HKMA | 19 December 2025 | In force | Locally incorporated AIs | [S:349a543ae2f0, Application, p.1; paras 3.6.6, 4.2.8] |
| AML/CFT Guideline for AIs (revised May 2023) | HKMA | 25 May 2023 | In force | AIs, including Registered Institutions (RIs) | [S:7bfdad704174, paras 1.3, 2.10-2.11] |
| DLT risk-management considerations (cover letter + Annex) | HKMA | 16 April 2024 | In force | AIs (non-binding considerations) | [S:cd5d66ba08a2, p.2]; [S:1884530ff235, Annex, Introduction] |
| DLT in the Financial Sector: study | HKMA | 19 March 2025 | Exploratory | AIs (research, not a rule) | [S:e0fd558b3dbc, Introduction, p.4] |
| Sale and distribution of tokenised products | HKMA | 20 February 2024 | In force | AIs (tokenised products not regulated under the Securities and Futures Ordinance) | [S:b2719f3dcb37, Coverage, p.1; Section A, p.3] |
| Staking from custodial services | HKMA | 7 April 2025 | In force | AIs and subsidiaries of locally incorporated AIs | [S:4641e6c404d2, p.1] |
| Updated custody guidance Annex | HKMA | 27 May 2026 | In force | AIs and subsidiaries of locally incorporated AIs | [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 1, 11, 14-19] |
| SPM CRP-1 Classification of Cryptoassets | HKMA | 1 January 2026 | In force | All AIs | [S:b7d630146e6c, Application, p.1; para 2.1.1] |
| Strategic Review of Business Models | HKMA | 9 March 2026 | In force | All AIs | [S:3ec5b269b5dc, p.2, para 4] |

## Key facts

- Directors and senior managers of a locally incorporated AI should understand the firm-wide risks of new or complex products and activities. [S:349a543ae2f0, para 4.2.8, p.63] CA-G-5 names cryptoasset activities as an example. [S:349a543ae2f0, para 4.2.8, p.63]
- CA-G-5 notes: "Cryptoasset activities and associated risks are relatively new and evolving." [S:349a543ae2f0, para 3.6.6, p.53] For related gaps in capital adequacy (having enough capital) or risk management, the HKMA may consider these measures: [S:349a543ae2f0, para 3.6.6, p.53]
  - capital add-ons (extra capital on top of the minimum);
  - provisioning (setting money aside) for foreseeable and estimable cryptoasset losses;
  - limits;
  - other measures.
- The HKMA expects each AI's board to oversee and endorse a formal strategic business plan. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, p.2, para 4] The board has six months from the 9 March 2026 circular. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, p.2, para 4] The plan looks at adapting products, revenue models, customer engagement, risk management and operations. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, p.2, para 4]
- A bank should identify and weigh the ML/TF risks of: [S:7bfdad704174, paras 2.10-2.11]
  - new products;
  - new business practices, including delivery mechanisms (how the product reaches customers);
  - new or developing technologies.

  It should do this assessment before launch. It should then take measures to manage and reduce the risks it finds. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 2.10-2.11]
- In the HKMA AML/CFT Guideline, the word "should" signals a mandatory requirement, just as "must" does. [S:7bfdad704174, para 1.6]
- The April 2024 DLT considerations are non-binding and non-exhaustive (not a complete list). [S:cd5d66ba08a2, pp.1-2] The HKMA supervises on a risk-based, technology-neutral basis. [S:cd5d66ba08a2, pp.1-2] It checks whether a bank has adequate systems and controls for the extra risks DLT may bring. [S:cd5d66ba08a2, pp.1-2]
- The board and senior management carry full responsibility for DLT adoption. [S:1884530ff235, Annex, item 1] The bank should update its technology-risk, business-continuity and outsourcing policies for DLT factors as needed, and have enough staff with DLT expertise. [S:1884530ff235, Annex, item 1]
- A bank should choose a DLT network type that suits the application's nature and risks. [S:1884530ff235, Annex, items 2 and 5] It should also consider whether the node operators (the parties that validate and confirm changes to the ledger) are trustworthy, reliable and diverse. [S:1884530ff235, Annex, items 2 and 5] A permissionless network (one anyone can join) would likely be inappropriate for highly critical or sensitive functions without adequate compensating controls. [S:1884530ff235, Annex, items 2 and 5]
- Where a bank uses DLT for critical functions, its business continuity plans should include DLT test scenarios such as: [S:1884530ff235, Annex, item 10]
  - cyberattacks;
  - loss or theft of private keys;
  - forks (splits of a blockchain into two versions).
- The March 2025 study drew on input from three other regulators. [S:e0fd558b3dbc, Foreword, p.3; Introduction, p.4; Section 4.2.4, p.48] They are the Insurance Authority, the Mandatory Provident Fund Schemes Authority and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC). [S:e0fd558b3dbc, Foreword, p.3; Introduction, p.4; Section 4.2.4, p.48] It surveyed 113 financial institutions and builds on the 2024 circular. [S:e0fd558b3dbc, Foreword, p.3; Introduction, p.4; Section 4.2.4, p.48] The study is research, not a new rule. [S:e0fd558b3dbc, Foreword, p.3; Introduction, p.4; Section 4.2.4, p.48]
- For outsourced DLT work, the study suggests three steps: [S:e0fd558b3dbc, Section 4.2.4, item 1, p.48]
  - assess vendors at every stage;
  - set contract terms on performance and data security;
  - line up backup vendors or failover plans (switching to a backup) in advance.
- Before launching custody, a bank should complete a comprehensive risk assessment, with effective oversight by the board and senior management before and after launch. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 1]
- As a general principle, a bank may delegate or outsource VA custody only to one of three types of firm: [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 14]
  - another AI, or a subsidiary of an AI incorporated in Hong Kong;
  - a VA trading platform licensed by the SFC;
  - an HKMA-licensed stablecoin issuer that has HKMA consent to hold the stablecoins it issues.
- Due diligence on a custody delegate covers, among other things, independent code reviews and the provider's software release process. [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 15, 19] After that, the bank keeps reviewing the provider's security controls and disaster-recovery testing. [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 15, 19] Ultimate responsibility stays with the bank. [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 15, 19]
- The HKMA sets these key-management expectations for client VAs: [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(a), (b), (i)]
  - Keep keys in tamper-resistant devices such as hardware security modules (HSM), and do due diligence on the HSM vendor.
  - Generate, store and back up seeds (master secrets that create keys) and keys in Hong Kong.
  - Use key sharding (splitting a key into parts held separately) or similar, so no single point of failure exists.
  - Show signers the transaction details in human-readable form.
- If the client assets in custody are VAs, 98% should sit in cold storage. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(l) and fn 8]
- Some tokenised products (assets recorded as tokens on a DLT network) fall outside the Securities and Futures Ordinance. [S:b2719f3dcb37, Section A, pp.3-4] For these, due diligence on issuers and their technology vendors should cover: [S:b2719f3dcb37, Section A, pp.3-4]
  - key management;
  - safeguards against theft and hacking;
  - smart-contract audits (checks of the code that runs on the blockchain);
  - contingency plans for DLT failures.
- For staking (locking up tokens to help run a blockchain, for rewards), the bank should do three things: [S:4641e6c404d2, p.2, section A and fn 2; pp.2-3, section C]
  - Keep possession or control of the means to unstake client VAs, such as the private keys of withdrawal addresses.
  - Do due diligence on each blockchain protocol.
  - Vet and monitor any third-party staking provider.
- CRP-1 says AIs must have policies, governance, staff and information technology able to assess cryptoasset risk. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.1] They must document the basis for each classification and make it available to the HKMA on request. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.1]

## What your bank must do

**Obligations**
- [ ] Run the ML/TF risk assessment before launching any new product, new business practice or new technology. Examples of new products are a VA, tokenisation or stablecoin service. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 2.10-2.11]
- [ ] Brief the board so it understands cryptoasset risks firm-wide and can set limits. Those limits sit within the bank's risk appetite (the level of risk it is willing to accept). [S:349a543ae2f0, para 4.2.8, pp.63-64]
- [ ] Complete a comprehensive risk assessment before custody launch, under board oversight. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 1]

**Controls & monitoring**
- [ ] Update technology-risk, continuity and outsourcing policies for DLT factors. [S:1884530ff235, Annex, item 1]
- [ ] Apply the para 11 key controls to client VAs, including 98% cold storage. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11 and fn 8]
- [ ] Monitor custody security 24/7, test system changes before deployment and monitor dependencies. [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 23-25]
- [ ] Keep documented classification evidence for each cryptoasset exposure. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.1]

**Notify / consult HKMA or SFC**
- [ ] Take the DLT considerations into account when preparing DLT-related submissions. The HKMA encourages this. [S:cd5d66ba08a2, p.2]
- [ ] Obtain HKMA consent before appointing an HKMA-licensed stablecoin issuer to hold the stablecoins it issues. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(b) and fn 7; para 14] The issuer's keys must be kept in Hong Kong or a location the HKMA accepts. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(b) and fn 7; para 14]

**Counterparty due diligence**
- [ ] Document due diligence on custody delegates and HSM vendors, and review them regularly. [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 11(a), 15]
- [ ] Vet tokenisation platforms and staking providers before use, and monitor them afterwards. [S:b2719f3dcb37, Section A, p.3]; [S:4641e6c404d2, section C, p.3]
- [ ] Consider whether DLT node operators are trustworthy, reliable and diverse. [S:1884530ff235, Annex, item 5]

## Talking points

**To the CCO**
- The HKMA AML/CFT Guideline requires an ML/TF risk assessment before any new product, practice or technology launch. In that guideline, "should" is mandatory. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 1.6, 2.10-2.11]
- The DLT considerations are non-binding. Even so, the HKMA encourages banks to take them into account in DLT-related submissions. [S:cd5d66ba08a2, p.2]

**To business heads**
- As a general principle, we can outsource VA custody only to another AI, an SFC-licensed platform, or a licensed stablecoin issuer. A stablecoin issuer qualifies only for the coins it issues, and only with HKMA consent. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 14]
- Before we offer tokenised products to customers, we need due diligence on the issuer and its technology vendors. [S:b2719f3dcb37, Section A, p.3]

**To the CEO**
- The HKMA expects the board to understand cryptoasset risks. [S:349a543ae2f0, para 4.2.8] It also expects the board to endorse a digital-transformation business plan within six months of 9 March 2026. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, p.2, para 4]
- If our capital or risk management for crypto falls short, the HKMA may consider capital add-ons, provisioning or limits. [S:349a543ae2f0, para 3.6.6]

**To Risk / CRO**
- For custody keys, the HKMA looks for HSM devices, a Hong Kong location and sharding. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11 and fn 8] It also looks for no blind signing (approving unseen details) and 98% of client VAs in cold storage. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11 and fn 8]
- DLT continuity plans should test key loss, cyberattacks and forks. [S:1884530ff235, Annex, item 10]

## Common mix-ups

- **Myth:** "The DLT considerations are rules with deadlines." **Fact:** They are non-binding and set no deadline. [S:cd5d66ba08a2, p.2] The firm numbers sit in the custody Annex. [S:ce05e67bcdce, fn 8]
- **Myth:** "The March 2025 DLT study sets new rules." **Fact:** It is a research study. It builds on the 2024 circular. [S:e0fd558b3dbc, Introduction, p.4; Section 4.2.4, p.48]
- **Myth:** "Outsourcing custody moves the risk away." **Fact:** Ultimate responsibility stays with the bank. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 19]
- **Myth:** "Insurance must cover 100% of hot-wallet assets." **Fact:** That fixed cover came from the February 2024 guidance. [S:86e064b2a8d0, fn 8] It set 50% cover for cold storage, and 100% for hot storage (keys kept online) and other storage. [S:86e064b2a8d0, fn 8] The May 2026 circular replaced that guidance. [S:ed61d7c335e7, p.2] The 2026 Annex instead makes the bank liable for losses attributable to it. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(n)] It also requires adequate financial resources, which may include insurance. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(n)]
- **Myth:** "The SFC's VA chapter on money laundering sets our new-product rule." **Fact:** For a bank, the HKMA guideline governs. [S:7bfdad704174, para 1.3 and fn 1] RIs must also take into account the SFC guideline, including its VA chapter. [S:7bfdad704174, para 1.3 and fn 1]

## Read these first

1. **Risk management considerations related to the use of DLT (Annex)**, HKMA, 16 April 2024. Read all ten items. This is the HKMA's DLT checklist. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20240416-2-EN/20240416-2-EN.pdf
2. **Updated Guidance on Expected Standards on Custodial Services (Annex)**, HKMA, 27 May 2026. Read paras 1, 10-11, 14-19 and 23-25. It covers governance, keys and outsourcing in one place. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20260527-7-EN/20260527-7-EN.pdf
3. **SPM CA-G-5 Supervisory Review Process (V.7)**, HKMA, 19 December 2025. Read paras 3.6.6 (p.53) and 4.2.8 (pp.63-64). These hold the board-understanding and Pillar 2 hooks. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20251217-2-EN/CA-G-5.pdf

## Open items

- The HKMA AML/CFT Guideline for AIs has no provisions on stablecoins, unhosted wallets (wallets held without a service provider) or VA red flags (warning signs). [S:7bfdad704174, paras 4.2.1, 11.23] The guideline mentions VAs only in passing, in two places: [S:7bfdad704174, paras 4.2.1, 11.23]
  - VA transfers as occasional transactions (one-off dealings outside an ongoing relationship);
  - VA service providers in correspondent-type relationships (a bank providing services similar to correspondent banking to another firm).
  
  See D3 for how the gap is handled.
- No general HKMA outsourcing or technology-risk module is among the documents reviewed for this guide. Only DLT- and custody-specific outsourcing text is covered.
- Two copies of CA-G-5 V.7 exist. One is dated 27 November 2025 and has a placeholder header date (xx.12.2025). The other is the 19 December 2025 version. [S:04bbb675089e, p.1]; [S:349a543ae2f0, p.1] This module cites the 19 December 2025 text, and the crypto paragraphs match. [S:04bbb675089e, p.1]; [S:349a543ae2f0, p.1]

## Related modules

[B2](#m-B2), [C3](#m-C3), [C5](#m-C5), [D3](#m-D3), [D4](#m-D4)

title: Selling, dealing and advising on virtual assets
md:
This module is for the Head of Compliance at a bank that is also a Registered Institution (RI). An RI is a bank registered with the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) for securities business. After this module you can explain what the bank can do with virtual assets (VAs), such as bitcoin. That covers selling, dealing, advising and staking. You can also explain what the bank must check first. The rules come from a joint regime of the SFC and the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA).

## In 60 seconds

Since January 2022, the SFC and the HKMA have set out their expectations in a joint circular on virtual-asset (VA) activities [S:e4828fcba126, p.1]. The circular covers intermediaries, including banks registered with the SFC [S:e4828fcba126, p.1]. The current base text is dated 22 December 2023. It replaced the two earlier versions [S:8a016a912528, para 3]. A supplemental circular of 30 September 2025 added refinements and relaxations [S:d5ebca32c92b, para 2]. HKMA guidance of 27 May 2026 eased the rules for licensed stablecoins [S:a0bd48559762, Background]. Licensed stablecoins are tokens pegged to one or more official currencies [S:a0bd48559762, Background]. The same guidance allowed VA financing, meaning credit for VA dealing [S:e64b7b0267b2, p.2]. The regulators say VA-related products are very likely complex [S:8a016a912528, para 5]. Complex ones should generally go only to professional investors (PIs), who meet set wealth or institutional tests [S:8a016a912528, paras 5, 6.1]. Firms should test the VA knowledge of clients other than institutional and qualified corporate PIs [S:8a016a912528, paras 6.2, 17]. Dealing should go through SFC-licensed platforms [S:8a016a912528, paras 6.2, 17]. For licensed stablecoins, dealing can also go through the licensed issuer [S:a0bd48559762, para (1)]. The SFC imposes the detailed conduct rules as conditions on the bank's SFC registration [S:8a016a912528, paras 19, 31]. The bank should tell the SFC in advance of new VA activities or changes, and the HKMA where applicable [S:8a016a912528, paras 19, 31].

## Status board

As of 25 September 2026.

LCs = licensed corporations (firms licensed by the SFC). RIs = registered institutions (banks registered with the SFC). AIs = authorized institutions (banks licensed under the Banking Ordinance). VATPs = VA trading platforms licensed by the SFC. PI = professional investor. FSTB = Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau. T&Cs = terms and conditions.

| Instrument | Issuer | Date | Status (chip) | Applies to | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Joint circular on intermediaries' VA-related activities | SFC + HKMA | 28 Jan 2022 | Superseded | LCs, RIs | [S:e4828fcba126, p.1] |
| Joint circular (revised) | SFC + HKMA | 20 Oct 2023 | Superseded | LCs, RIs | [S:a37d28d879cf, p.1; S:8a016a912528, para 3] |
| Joint circular (current base) + Appendices 1–7 | SFC + HKMA | 22 Dec 2023 | In force | LCs, RIs | [S:8a016a912528, p.1], [S:0027a8747112, landing page] |
| Supplemental joint circular (staking, off-platform trades, in-kind flows) | SFC + HKMA | 30 Sep 2025 | In force | LCs, RIs | [S:d5ebca32c92b, p.1] |
| HKMA circular on Relevant Stablecoin activities + Appendix A1 (dealing and advice T&Cs) and A2 (portfolio management T&Cs) | HKMA (with SFC) | 27 May 2026 | In force | RIs | [S:a0bd48559762, pp.1–2], [S:31b4f67e0233, p.1] |
| Letter on Relevant Stablecoin-related activities | HKMA | 27 May 2026 | In force | All AIs | [S:1babdb609fc8, p.1] |
| Circular on Relevant Stablecoin services (26EC26) | SFC | 27 May 2026 | In force | VATPs, LCs (bank's counterparties) | [S:19d52ade6849, p.1] |
| Guidance on VA financing, shared order book and client VA withdrawals | HKMA | 27 May 2026 | In force | RIs | [S:e64b7b0267b2, p.1] |
| Standalone licensing regimes for VA dealing, advisory and management | FSTB + SFC | Dec 2025 / May 2026 | Conclusions published | Banks would register with the SFC for VA advisory and management | [S:6186c01c6649, p.1, paras 52, 58 and fns 9–10], [S:01c5c5c4045f, para 62] |

## Key facts

- The 22 December 2023 circular fully replaced both earlier joint circulars [S:8a016a912528, para 3].
- VA-related products mainly invest in VAs, get their value mainly from VAs, or track VA returns [S:8a016a912528, para 5]. The regulators say such products are very likely complex [S:8a016a912528, para 5]. So suitability checks (does the product fit the client?) apply even without a solicitation or recommendation [S:8a016a912528, para 5]. The exception is the exchange-traded products in paras 7 and 9 [S:8a016a912528, para 5].
- Complex VA-related products should be offered only to PIs, apart from a limited set of products [S:8a016a912528, para 6.1]. The set covers certain VA derivatives traded on exchanges the SFC specifies, plus SFC-authorised VA funds [S:8a016a912528, paras 7, 9, 9.1]. For the funds, the exchange is the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong (SEHK). For these exchange-traded products, a firm can execute a client's order without a suitability check if it made no solicitation or recommendation [S:8a016a912528, paras 7, 9, 9.1]. The knowledge test still applies [S:8a016a912528, paras 7, 9, 9.1].
- Firms should assess the VA knowledge of every client except institutional PIs and qualified corporate PIs [S:8a016a912528, para 6.2 and fn 10]. A one-off test is acceptable [S:8a016a912528, para 6.2 and fn 10]. A client without the knowledge may trade only after the firm has trained them [S:8a016a912528, para 6.2 and fn 10].
- Firms should partner only with SFC-licensed platforms for VA dealing [S:8a016a912528, paras 17–18]. They can introduce clients to the platform or use an omnibus account (one account holding many clients' assets) [S:8a016a912528, paras 17–18]. They should offer VA dealing only to clients of their Type 1 (dealing in securities) business [S:8a016a912528, paras 17–18].
- Before serving retail dealing clients, a firm should set an exposure limit for each client [S:8a016a912528, para 20(a)(ii), (iv)]. The limit should reflect the client's financial situation, including net worth [S:8a016a912528, para 20(a)(ii), (iv)]. The firm should also restrict these clients to tokens the platform offers to retail investors [S:8a016a912528, para 20(a)(ii), (iv)].
- Advice on VAs is limited to Type 1 or Type 4 (advising on securities) clients [S:8a016a912528, paras 26, 28(a)]. Any VA recommended to a retail client should appear in at least two acceptable indices [S:8a016a912528, paras 26, 28(a)]. Those indices should come from at least two different index providers [S:8a016a912528, paras 26, 28(a)].
- Appendix 7 sets extra terms for managing some portfolios that invest in VAs (RA9: Type 9 regulated activity, asset management) [S:8a016a912528, paras 23–24]. A portfolio triggers these terms if it has a stated VA objective [S:8a016a912528, paras 23–24]. It also triggers them if it plans to put 10% or more of gross asset value (GAV) into VAs [S:8a016a912528, paras 23–24]. Discretionary VA dealing that is only incidental to Type 1 business should stay below 10% of GAV [S:8a016a912528, paras 23–24].
- The September 2025 supplement allows staking for clients the firm already deals VAs for [S:d5ebca32c92b, paras 4–5]. Staking means locking up tokens to help run a blockchain in return for rewards. Staking should go only through segregated accounts at an SFC-licensed platform or an AI [S:d5ebca32c92b, paras 4–5]. Segregated accounts keep client assets apart from the firm's own.
- The same supplement allows trades through a licensed platform's off-platform trading services [S:d5ebca32c92b, paras 6–7]. These are services the platform runs outside its main trading venue. The regulators do not treat a client's subscription for, or redemption of, products using VAs as providing VA dealing services [S:d5ebca32c92b, paras 6–7]. The same applies to in-kind fund flows (paying in or taking out VAs instead of cash) [S:d5ebca32c92b, paras 6–7].
- The net-worth check and the VA-futures risk disclosure do not apply to institutional or qualified corporate PIs [S:d5ebca32c92b, paras 8–9].
- From May 2026, RIs may partner with the licensed issuer of a Relevant Stablecoin as well as with VATPs [S:a0bd48559762, p.1 and para (1)]. A Relevant Stablecoin is a specified stablecoin issued under a Stablecoins Ordinance licence [S:a0bd48559762, p.1 and para (1)]. The same guidance removes paragraph 20(a)(iii) [S:a0bd48559762, p.1 and para (1)]. So retail omnibus dealing may now go through a VA trading platform (VATP) that serves PIs only [S:a0bd48559762, p.1 and para (1)]. The condition is that retail clients trade only tokens that VATP has admitted for retail trading [S:a0bd48559762, p.1 and para (1)].
- Some clients have accounts clearly marked as Relevant-Stablecoin-only. For them, no knowledge test or exposure limit is needed [S:a0bd48559762, para (3)(a)–(b); S:31b4f67e0233, paras 6.2A, 6.4, 6.4A]. For any client, Relevant Stablecoin holdings need not count towards the exposure limit [S:a0bd48559762, para (3)(a)–(b); S:31b4f67e0233, paras 6.2A, 6.4, 6.4A].
- RIs providing VA dealing may now offer VA financing, but only to their securities margin clients [S:e64b7b0267b2, paras (1), (2), (4) and fn 5]. Where the RI relies on VA collateral, only bitcoin, ether and Relevant Stablecoins are eligible [S:e64b7b0267b2, paras (1), (2), (4) and fn 5]. Bitcoin and ether get a haircut of at least 60% [S:e64b7b0267b2, paras (1), (2), (4) and fn 5]. A haircut is a cut to the value the lender counts.
- In January 2026 the SFC reprimanded and fined a licensed broker HK$4 million [S:415e4629a80f, paras 1–5]. Between November 2018 and November 2022, the broker let retail clients trade VA products that the 2018 and 2022 circulars limited to PIs [S:415e4629a80f, paras 1–5]. The 1,446 trades involved 32 VA products [S:415e4629a80f, paras 1–5]. The broker did not assess VA knowledge or give VA-specific warnings [S:415e4629a80f, paras 1–5]. It had no specific product due diligence procedures for VA products [S:415e4629a80f, paras 1–5].

## What your bank must do

**Obligations**
- Classify every VA-linked product [S:8a016a912528, paras 5–10]. Then apply the PI-only, suitability and knowledge-test rules that follow from that classification [S:8a016a912528, paras 5–10].
- Carry out extra due diligence, using Appendix 4, on any VA fund the SFC has not authorised [S:8a016a912528, para 12.3].
- Give VA risk disclosures and warning statements to clients other than institutional or qualified corporate PIs [S:8a016a912528, para 15].
- Receive or withdraw client VAs only through segregated accounts [S:8a016a912528, para 20(b)]. Use accounts held at the partner platform or at an AI that meets HKMA custody standards [S:8a016a912528, para 20(b)].
- For Relevant Stablecoins, disclose material information on how the coin keeps its value and how redemption works [S:a0bd48559762, paras (5), (8), (10)]. Commission rebates or other benefits should not be the main basis for soliciting or recommending a coin [S:a0bd48559762, paras (5), (8), (10)].

**Controls & monitoring**
- Have adequate policies, procedures and controls for Relevant Stablecoin activities, and train staff [S:a0bd48559762, Implementation, p.9].
- Keep Relevant-Stablecoin-only clients to Relevant Stablecoins [S:a0bd48559762, fn 4]. Apply the full rules, including the knowledge test, before dealing in any other VA for them [S:a0bd48559762, fn 4].
- Keep the listed records on client VAs, staking and VA financing for at least seven years [S:31b4f67e0233, paras 9.6–9.8]. Keep records of orders and instructions on client VAs for at least two years [S:31b4f67e0233, paras 9.6–9.8].
- Get a signed staking-risk acknowledgement before staking for clients other than institutional or qualified corporate PIs [S:31b4f67e0233, paras 8.7(b), 8.8].
- Monitor the volatility of VA collateral in real time when relying on it [S:e64b7b0267b2, paras (5)(b), (9)]. Treat loans secured only by VAs as clean loans, meaning unsecured for capital purposes [S:e64b7b0267b2, paras (5)(b), (9)]. The reason is that the Banking (Capital) Rules do not recognise VA collateral [S:e64b7b0267b2, paras (5)(b), (9)].

**Notify / consult HKMA or SFC**
- Tell the SFC in advance, and the HKMA where applicable, about any new VA activity or change to one [S:8a016a912528, para 31]. That includes a change in the type of client served [S:8a016a912528, para 31].
- Notify before the first client VA deposit or withdrawal, the first staking service, or the first VA-funded subscription or redemption [S:d5ebca32c92b, para 10].
- A bank that is an AI but not an RI should follow the same standards [S:1babdb609fc8, pp.1–2]. It should discuss any Relevant Stablecoin dealing, advice or portfolio management with the HKMA before starting [S:1babdb609fc8, pp.1–2].
- Report any actual or suspected material breach of the terms to the SFC and the HKMA as soon as practicable [S:31b4f67e0233, para 12.1].

**Counterparty due diligence**
- Confirm that the platform holds an actual SFC licence [S:8a016a912528, para 17 and fn 20]. Some platforms are only treated as licensed under Schedule 3G of the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (AMLO). Those platforms do not count [S:8a016a912528, para 17 and fn 20].
- Use only an SFC-licensed platform or an AI as the staking service provider [S:31b4f67e0233, paras 8.2–8.3]. Confirm it has SFC approval or has discussed the service with the HKMA [S:31b4f67e0233, paras 8.2–8.3].
- For in-kind or VA-funded subscriptions, hold the VAs only at SFC-licensed platforms or AIs [S:d5ebca32c92b, para 7(b)–(c)]. For those transfers, comply with the VA chapter (Chapter 12) of the SFC's anti-money-laundering (AML) guideline [S:d5ebca32c92b, para 7(b)–(c)].

## Talking points

**To the CCO**
- The regime reaches us as an RI through conditions the SFC puts on our registration, consulting the HKMA where applicable [S:8a016a912528, para 19; S:8934af8cc884, para 2.1.3]. The HKMA is our frontline, day-to-day supervisor [S:8a016a912528, para 19; S:8934af8cc884, para 2.1.3].
- Our AML baseline is the HKMA AML Guideline [S:7bfdad704174, para 1.3 fn 1]. As an RI we are also required to take into account the VA chapter (Chapter 12) of the SFC guideline [S:7bfdad704174, para 1.3 fn 1].

**To business heads**
- SFC-authorised VA funds are not PI-only, and retail clients can buy listed ones on SEHK [S:8a016a912528, paras 6.1, 6.2, 9, 9.1]. We should still assess VA knowledge first. Overseas VA exchange-traded products that are not derivatives remain PI-only [S:8a016a912528, paras 6.1, 6.2, 9, 9.1].
- Since May 2026, clearly ring-fenced Relevant-Stablecoin-only accounts need no knowledge test and no exposure limit [S:a0bd48559762, p.1 and para (3)]. The coin must come from an HKMA-licensed issuer [S:a0bd48559762, p.1 and para (3)].

**To the CEO**
- The regulators relaxed parts of the regime in December 2023, September 2025 and May 2026 [S:8a016a912528, para 9; S:d5ebca32c92b, para 2; S:a0bd48559762, Background]. Complex-product rules, knowledge tests and licensed venues remain [S:8a016a912528, paras 5, 6.2, 17].
- In January 2026 the SFC fined a broker HK$4 million for VA distribution failures from 2018 to 2022 [S:415e4629a80f, paras 1–2].

**To Risk / CRO**
- Margin clients can get VA financing [S:e64b7b0267b2, paras (4), (9) and fn 5]. Only bitcoin, ether and Relevant Stablecoins count as VA collateral, with at least a 60% haircut on bitcoin and ether [S:e64b7b0267b2, paras (4), (9) and fn 5]. VA collateral gets no capital recognition [S:e64b7b0267b2, paras (4), (9) and fn 5].
- Discretionary VA exposure under Type 1 should stay below 10% of the client account's GAV [S:31b4f67e0233, para 4.7].

## Common mix-ups

- **Myth:** All VA products are PI-only. **Fact:** SFC-authorised VA funds are not PI-only [S:8a016a912528, paras 6.1, 7, 9]. Certain VA derivatives traded on specified exchanges are also exempt. A knowledge test is still needed [S:8a016a912528, paras 6.1, 7, 9].
- **Myth:** VA financing is banned. **Fact:** For RIs, that was true until May 2026 [S:e64b7b0267b2, Background and paras (1)–(2)]. RIs providing VA dealing may now offer it to their securities margin clients under HKMA conditions [S:e64b7b0267b2, Background and paras (1)–(2)].
- **Myth:** The 2026 stablecoin relief covers any stablecoin and any bank. **Fact:** It covers only Relevant Stablecoins and only RIs [S:a0bd48559762, p.2 and fn 3]. It does not cover a licensed issuer for its own coin [S:a0bd48559762, p.2 and fn 3]. A separate letter tells AIs that are not RIs to follow the same standards [S:1babdb609fc8, p.1].
- **Myth:** Deleting para 20(a)(iii) only matters for stablecoins. **Fact:** The deletion lets RIs serve retail clients in any VA through PI-only VATPs [S:a0bd48559762, para (1)]. This works only if each token has been admitted for retail trading [S:a0bd48559762, para (1)].
- **Myth:** The 2022 circular still sets the rules. **Fact:** The December 2023 circular replaced the 2022 and October 2023 circulars [S:8a016a912528, para 3]. Firms could keep serving existing clients found to have VA knowledge by tests done before 22 December 2023 [S:8a016a912528, fn 40].

## Read these first

1. **Joint circular on intermediaries' VA-related activities**, SFC + HKMA, 22 Dec 2023. Read paras 5–15 (distribution), 16–22 (dealing), 23–29 (management and advice) and 30–31 (implementation). This is the base rulebook. https://apps.sfc.hk/edistributionWeb/api/circular/openFile?lang=EN&refNo=23EC66
2. **Supplemental joint circular**, SFC + HKMA, 30 Sep 2025. Read paras 4–10. They cover staking, off-platform trades, in-kind flows, carve-outs for PIs and notifications. https://apps.sfc.hk/edistributionWeb/api/circular/openFile?lang=EN&refNo=25EC50
3. **VA-related activities in relation to relevant stablecoins**, HKMA to RIs, 27 May 2026. Read Sections I–IV, paras (1)–(17), fn 3–4 and Implementation (p.9). This is the current relief for banks that are RIs. It removes para 20(a)(iii). https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20260527-2-EN/20260527-2-EN.pdf

## Open items

- The standalone licensing regimes for VA dealing, advisory and management are at the conclusions stage [S:01c5c5c4045f, para 62]. The conclusions state that they will replace the current approach of putting terms and conditions on SFC registrations [S:01c5c5c4045f, para 62].
- No arrangement is planned to let existing VA advisory or management providers carry on while they apply for a licence [S:01c5c5c4045f, paras 63, 67]. Instead, a faster approval process is planned for LCs and RIs already providing those services [S:01c5c5c4045f, paras 63, 67]. The sources reviewed contain no bill text or start date.
- A June 2026 reply to a Legislative Council (LegCo) question covered a bill for VA dealing, custodian, advisory and management regimes [S:c6df52e680de, Reply part (3)]. The reply said the bill would go to LegCo within 2026 [S:c6df52e680de, Reply part (3)]. The sources reviewed do not show that it has been introduced.
- The SFC press release on the January 2026 fine refers to a Statement of Disciplinary Action [S:415e4629a80f, Notes 3 and 5]. We have not reviewed that statement here.
- Footnote 25 of the 2023 circular says firms should not provide financial accommodation (credit) for clients to acquire VAs [S:8a016a912528, fn 25]. For RIs, the May 2026 terms now allow it where the firm engages in securities margin financing [S:31b4f67e0233, para 4.3; S:e64b7b0267b2, p.5]. Registry summaries of the 2023 circular that still describe financing as prohibited are out of date.

## Related modules

[C2](#m-C2) (VA funds and exchange-traded funds), [C3](#m-C3) (Custody and key management) and [C4](#m-C4) (Stablecoins). Also see the modules on AML and counter-terrorist financing, and on VATPs.


**Business angle:** [Virtual-asset distribution and brokerage](#b-va-distribution) and [Virtual-asset financing and margin](#b-va-financing) in the Business tab.

title: VA funds and ETFs
md:
This module covers virtual asset (VA) funds and exchange-traded funds (ETFs). It is for the Head of Compliance at a bank that sells funds or acts as a participating dealer. A participating dealer is a firm allowed to create and redeem units in an exchange-traded fund. Tokenised funds are funds whose units are recorded as digital tokens. After this module, you can explain which crypto funds and tokenised funds may be sold in Hong Kong, and on what terms. You can also explain what the bank checks before it sells, creates or redeems units.

## In 60 seconds

In October 2022 the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) began taking applications to authorise VA ETFs [S:51dac2cabe78, para 6; S:c79c4686c5e0, para 5]. These ETFs got their exposure to virtual assets (VAs) mainly through futures (contracts to buy or sell at a set price on a future date) [S:51dac2cabe78, para 6; S:c79c4686c5e0, para 5]. A December 2023 circular let authorised funds invest directly in spot VAs (the crypto itself, not contracts on it) [S:5b6530666cc2, paras 2, 5]. An April 2025 revision added staking (locking up tokens to help run a blockchain in return for rewards) and other VA-related activities [S:353535602a83, paras 1–2, 27]. A new version, reference 26EC31, replaced the April 2025 revision on 27 May 2026 [S:c79c4686c5e0, para 3]. A fund that wants more than 10% of its net asset value (NAV) in VAs needs to consult the SFC and get its approval first [S:c79c4686c5e0, para 31]. Such a fund should invest only in tokens that the Hong Kong public can trade on SFC-licensed virtual asset trading platforms (VATPs) [S:c79c4686c5e0, paras 11, 15]. The fund should not use leverage (borrowing or derivatives that magnify exposure) to increase its VA exposure at fund level [S:c79c4686c5e0, paras 11, 15]. The fund's trustee may delegate VA custody (safekeeping) only to three types of firm [S:c79c4686c5e0, para 20]. These are licensed VATPs, qualifying authorized institutions (AIs), and other firms the SFC accepts [S:c79c4686c5e0, para 20]. A qualifying AI is a bank or other AI that meets the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) custody standards [S:c79c4686c5e0, para 20]. Separate SFC circulars allow tokenised versions of authorised products, including tokenised fund classes [S:58ea8520974d, para 5 and fn 8]. Since the 20 April 2026 revision, investors may also trade these tokenised products with each other on licensed VATPs [S:58ea8520974d, para 6; S:a64e364fd912, para 8]. When a bank sells SFC-authorised VA funds, the joint SFC–HKMA circular sets the selling rules [S:c79c4686c5e0, para 27; S:8a016a912528, para 9]. Participating dealers (PDs) for spot VA ETFs should be SFC-licensed corporations (LCs) or registered institutions (RIs), meaning banks registered with the SFC [S:c79c4686c5e0, para 19 and fn 8]. The SFC may add extra terms for these PDs [S:c79c4686c5e0, para 19 and fn 8].

## Status board

As of 25 Sep 2026.

| Instrument | Issuer | Date | Status (chip) | Applies to | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Circular on VA futures ETFs (22EC60) | SFC | 31 Oct 2022 | Superseded | Fund managers, distributors | [S:51dac2cabe78, p.1] |
| Circular on SFC-authorised funds with VA exposure (23EC65) | SFC | 22 Dec 2023 | Superseded | Funds, LCs, RIs | [S:5b6530666cc2, p.1] |
| Same circular, revised to add staking (25EC21) | SFC | 7 Apr 2025 | Superseded | Funds | [S:353535602a83, p.1] |
| Same circular, revised (26EC31) | SFC | 27 May 2026 | In force | Funds, managers, PDs, custodians | [S:c79c4686c5e0, p.1] |
| Tokenisation of SFC-authorised products (26EC22, revising 23EC53 of 2 Nov 2023) | SFC | 20 Apr 2026 | In force | Product providers, distributors | [S:58ea8520974d, p.1], [S:d422282a262d, p.1] |
| Secondary trading of tokenised SFC-authorised products (26EC23) | SFC | 20 Apr 2026 | In force | VATPs, LCs, RIs, product providers | [S:a64e364fd912, p.1] |
| Sale and distribution of tokenised products | HKMA | 20 Feb 2024 | In force | AIs | [S:b2719f3dcb37, p.1] |
| Joint circular (distribution rules) + Sep 2025 supplement | SFC + HKMA | 22 Dec 2023 / 30 Sep 2025 | In force | LCs, RIs | [S:8a016a912528, p.1], [S:d5ebca32c92b, p.1] |

## Key facts

- The first VA ETFs that the SFC allowed were based on futures [S:51dac2cabe78, paras 10, 12]. At first, the only futures allowed were bitcoin and ether futures traded on the Chicago Mercantile Exchange [S:51dac2cabe78, paras 10, 12]. The fund manager needed at least three years of experience managing ETFs [S:51dac2cabe78, paras 10, 12].
- The 2022 circular also capped each fund's net derivative exposure (its overall derivatives position after offsets) at 100% of NAV [S:51dac2cabe78, paras 14, 16]. It also required intermediaries to run a VA-knowledge test (a check that the client understands VAs) when serving clients in these ETFs [S:51dac2cabe78, paras 14, 16].
- Under the December 2023 circular, funds could invest directly in spot VAs [S:5b6530666cc2, para 5]. The first spot VA ETFs listed on the Hong Kong stock exchange on 30 April 2024 [S:e4236ed2600f, para 1].
- The current circular, 26EC31, covers public funds with more than 10% of NAV in VAs [S:c79c4686c5e0, paras 1, 3]. It replaced the April 2025 version [S:c79c4686c5e0, paras 1, 3].
- Circular 26EC31 does not cover a fund's exposure to Relevant Stablecoins or tokenised deposits [S:c79c4686c5e0, para 2 and fn 4]. Relevant Stablecoins are stablecoins tied to one or more official currencies and issued under a licence under the Stablecoins Ordinance [S:c79c4686c5e0, para 2 and fn 4]. Tokenised deposits are bank deposits recorded as digital tokens. For fund exposure to either of them, the SFC points to question 20G of its FAQs on the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds [S:c79c4686c5e0, para 2 and fn 4].
- Eligible VAs are limited to tokens that the Hong Kong public can trade on SFC-licensed VATPs [S:c79c4686c5e0, paras 11, 13, 15]. VA futures must trade on conventional regulated futures exchanges [S:c79c4686c5e0, paras 11, 13, 15]. Funds should not use leverage to increase their VA exposure at fund level [S:c79c4686c5e0, paras 11, 13, 15].
- Funds should buy and sell spot VAs through one of two routes [S:c79c4686c5e0, para 17 and fn 7]. The first is SFC-licensed VATPs, either on the platform or over the counter (a direct deal off the platform) [S:c79c4686c5e0, para 17 and fn 7]. The second is AIs, or subsidiaries of locally incorporated AIs, that comply with HKMA requirements [S:c79c4686c5e0, para 17 and fn 7].
- Spot VA ETFs may create and redeem units in cash or in kind (paying with the VAs themselves) [S:c79c4686c5e0, paras 17(b), 18]. For in-kind creations, PDs are expected to move VAs into the fund's custody accounts at VATPs or AIs [S:c79c4686c5e0, paras 17(b), 18]. The VAs may have been held in Hong Kong or overseas [S:c79c4686c5e0, paras 17(b), 18].
- PDs for spot VA ETFs should be LCs or RIs [S:c79c4686c5e0, para 19 and fn 8]. The SFC's Intermediaries Division may impose extra terms on them [S:c79c4686c5e0, para 19 and fn 8]. Appendix 6 of the joint circular sets out these terms [S:c79c4686c5e0, para 19 and fn 8].
- The trustee may delegate VA custody only to SFC-licensed VATPs, qualifying AIs, or other firms the SFC accepts [S:c79c4686c5e0, paras 20–21]. Qualifying AIs are AIs, or subsidiaries of locally incorporated AIs, that meet HKMA custody standards [S:c79c4686c5e0, paras 20–21]. Custodians should keep most VA holdings in cold wallets (storage kept offline) [S:c79c4686c5e0, paras 20–21]. They should store seeds and private keys (the secret codes that control the VAs) securely in Hong Kong [S:c79c4686c5e0, paras 20–21].
- The SFC may allow VA funds to stake through licensed VATPs or, where applicable, AIs [S:c79c4686c5e0, paras 28(d), 28(f), 31]. The conditions include disclosing how much of the fund may be staked, and reporting on staking in interim and annual reports [S:c79c4686c5e0, paras 28(d), 28(f), 31]. The fund also needs to consult the SFC and get its approval first [S:c79c4686c5e0, paras 28(d), 28(f), 31]. In April 2025, the SFC said it caps fund staking to manage liquidity risk (the risk of running short of cash for redemptions) [S:36753b22e10a, para 4].
- SFC-authorised VA funds are not restricted to professional investors (PIs) [S:8a016a912528, paras 9, 9.1–9.2 and fn 14]. For units listed on the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong (SEHK), an intermediary can execute on-exchange orders without a suitability check or warning statements [S:8a016a912528, paras 9, 9.1–9.2 and fn 14]. This applies only where the intermediary did not solicit or recommend the trade [S:8a016a912528, paras 9, 9.1–9.2 and fn 14]. A VA-knowledge test still applies [S:8a016a912528, paras 9, 9.1–9.2 and fn 14]. Unlisted classes, and trades off exchange, need a suitability check, warnings and the knowledge test [S:8a016a912528, paras 9, 9.1–9.2 and fn 14].
- The tokenisation circular looks through the token to the product underneath (a see-through approach) [S:58ea8520974d, paras 5, 13]. It permits primary dealing (buying units from, and selling them back to, the product provider) in tokenised authorised products [S:58ea8520974d, paras 5, 13]. Product providers should use public permissionless blockchains (open networks anyone can join) only if they add proper controls [S:58ea8520974d, paras 5, 13].
- Retail investors may be offered secondary trading (buying and selling between investors) in tokenised products [S:a64e364fd912, paras 8, 12(a)]. This trading runs through on-screen order matching on SFC-licensed VATPs [S:a64e364fd912, paras 8, 12(a)]. One control is an alert when the price moves away from the indicative NAV (a live estimate of the fund's value) [S:a64e364fd912, paras 8, 12(a)].
- In March 2026, the Hong Kong public could buy 13 tokenised products [S:bbd10edd41cf, paras 3, 6]. Their tokenised classes held about $10.7 billion in assets [S:bbd10edd41cf, paras 3, 6]. The SFC expects the first products offered for secondary trading to be mainly tokenised money market funds [S:bbd10edd41cf, paras 3, 6].

## What your bank must do

**Obligations**
- Apply the joint circular's selling rules when you sell any SFC-authorised VA fund [S:c79c4686c5e0, para 27; S:8a016a912528, paras 6.2, 9]. These rules include the VA-knowledge test for all clients except institutional and qualified corporate PIs [S:c79c4686c5e0, para 27; S:8a016a912528, paras 6.2, 9].
- Offer complex VA-related products (products whose terms and risks a retail investor is unlikely to understand) only to PIs [S:8a016a912528, paras 5, 6.1, 12.3]. VA funds not authorised by the SFC are one example [S:8a016a912528, paras 5, 6.1, 12.3]. Before offering such a fund, do the Appendix 4 due diligence on the fund and its manager [S:8a016a912528, appendices, Appendix 4]. Cover the firms the fund uses for trading and custody too [S:8a016a912528, appendices, Appendix 4].
- Be a licensed corporation or registered institution to distribute tokenised authorised products [S:58ea8520974d, para 18]. Apply the usual onboarding and suitability rules [S:58ea8520974d, para 18].
- Apply the underlying product's selling rules to tokenised products that the Securities and Futures Ordinance does not cover [S:b2719f3dcb37, pp.1–3 and fn 1]. The HKMA expects this, and expects the same for tokenised deposits placed by customers [S:b2719f3dcb37, pp.1–3 and fn 1]. The HKMA also expects AIs to understand and control the extra risks that tokenisation brings [S:b2719f3dcb37, pp.1–3 and fn 1]. RIs that sell tokenised products other than tokenised securities should follow this HKMA guidance [S:d5ebca32c92b, fn 2].

**Controls & monitoring**
- Show clients the price-deviation alert if the bank acts as a Connecting Broker [S:a64e364fd912, paras 13, 20(c) and fn 4]. A Connecting Broker is a licensed corporation or registered institution that routes clients' trades to VATPs [S:a64e364fd912, paras 13, 20(c) and fn 4]. Tell clients they can subscribe or redeem at NAV instead [S:a64e364fd912, paras 13, 20(c) and fn 4]. Get clients to confirm the risks before onboarding them [S:a64e364fd912, paras 13, 20(c) and fn 4].
- Keep an online screen that shows the indicative NAV and the last NAV [S:a64e364fd912, para 20(b)]. The indicative NAV is usually refreshed at least every 15 seconds while trading is open [S:a64e364fd912, para 20(b)].
- Build access rights and controls into any online platform that sells VA-related products, so the platform enforces selling restrictions [S:8a016a912528, para 11].

**Notify / consult HKMA or SFC**
- Give the SFC advance notice before first letting clients subscribe or redeem with VAs, including in-kind flows [S:d5ebca32c92b, paras 7(a), 10(d)]. Tell the HKMA too, where relevant [S:d5ebca32c92b, paras 7(a), 10(d)].
- Notify the SFC before first taking part in secondary trading of tokenised products [S:a64e364fd912, para 27 and fn 13]. The SFC reminds RIs to notify the HKMA too [S:a64e364fd912, para 27 and fn 13].
- Discuss with the HKMA before starting any activity covered by its tokenised-products circular [S:b2719f3dcb37, Implementation, p.6].

**Counterparty due diligence**
- Hold VAs for in-kind flows only in accounts with SFC-licensed platforms or AIs [S:d5ebca32c92b, para 7(b)]. For these VA transfers, the supplemental joint circular also points to the SFC's anti-money laundering (AML) guideline [S:d5ebca32c92b, para 7(c)]. The relevant part is Chapter 12 of the guideline for LCs and SFC-licensed VA service providers [S:d5ebca32c92b, para 7(c)].
- Do product due diligence on each VA-related product [S:8a016a912528, para 12.3]. Cover its risks and features, its target investors and selling restrictions, and its regulatory status [S:8a016a912528, para 12.3].
- Do due diligence on the issuer and its technology vendors for tokenised products under the HKMA circular [S:b2719f3dcb37, Section A, pp.3–4]. Cover smart-contract audits (independent reviews of the token's code) and private key management [S:b2719f3dcb37, Section A, pp.3–4]. Also cover contingency plans for the distributed ledger (the shared record behind the tokens) [S:b2719f3dcb37, Section A, pp.3–4].

## Talking points

**To the CCO**
- The VA fund circular is written for product providers [S:c79c4686c5e0, paras 8, 19, 27]. Our duties as distributor or participating dealer come from the joint circular and any extra SFC terms for PDs [S:c79c4686c5e0, paras 8, 19, 27].
- For secondary trading of tokenised products, intermediaries notify the SFC first [S:a64e364fd912, para 27 and fn 13]. RIs are reminded to notify the HKMA as well [S:a64e364fd912, para 27 and fn 13].

**To business heads**
- Retail clients can trade SEHK-listed VA ETFs on exchange without a suitability check if we did not solicit or recommend the trade [S:8a016a912528, paras 9.1–9.2, fn 14]. They still need a knowledge test [S:8a016a912528, paras 9.1–9.2, fn 14]. Unlisted classes of the same fund need a full suitability check [S:8a016a912528, paras 9.1–9.2, fn 14].
- In-kind creation is allowed, and the VAs may come from overseas holdings [S:c79c4686c5e0, paras 17(b), 18]. PDs are expected to move the VAs into custody at VATPs or AIs [S:c79c4686c5e0, paras 17(b), 18].

**To the CEO**
- Hong Kong allowed futures-only VA ETFs in 2022 and spot VA funds in 2023 [S:51dac2cabe78, para 12; S:5b6530666cc2, para 5]. Fund staking followed in 2025 [S:353535602a83, para 27]. In 2026 came a pilot of 24/7 secondary trading of tokenised funds [S:bbd10edd41cf, para 4].
- As of March 2026, 13 tokenised products held about $10.7 billion in their tokenised classes [S:bbd10edd41cf, para 3].

**To Risk / CRO**
- VA funds should not use leverage for VA exposure at fund level [S:c79c4686c5e0, paras 15, 20]. Custody can go only to VATPs, qualifying AIs, or firms the SFC accepts [S:c79c4686c5e0, paras 15, 20].
- Staking by funds needs SFC consultation and approval first [S:c79c4686c5e0, paras 28(f), 31]. Interim and annual reports should show staked holdings as a share of NAV, along with revenue and costs [S:c79c4686c5e0, paras 28(f), 31].

## Common mix-ups

- **Myth:** Hong Kong only has futures VA ETFs. **Fact:** Funds have been allowed to hold spot VAs directly since the December 2023 circular [S:5b6530666cc2, para 5].
- **Myth:** A fund holding licensed stablecoins is a VA fund. **Fact:** Circular 26EC31 excludes Relevant Stablecoins and tokenised deposits [S:c79c4686c5e0, para 2].
- **Myth:** The 2023 or 2025 fund circular still applies. **Fact:** Each was replaced, most recently by 26EC31 on 27 May 2026 [S:353535602a83, para 2; S:c79c4686c5e0, para 3].
- **Myth:** Tokenised funds only allow subscription and redemption. **Fact:** The 20 April 2026 revision allows secondary trading on VATPs [S:58ea8520974d, para 6]. The 2023 version had called for more caution [S:d422282a262d, para 6].
- **Myth:** In-kind subscription makes the bank a VA dealer. **Fact:** The regulators say in-kind subscription is not treated as VA dealing [S:d5ebca32c92b, para 7]. Notification, custody and AML conditions still apply [S:d5ebca32c92b, para 7].

## Read these first

1. **Circular on SFC-authorised funds with exposure to virtual assets (26EC31)**, SFC, revised 27 May 2026. Read paras 2, 11–22 and 27–31. They cover eligible VAs, PDs, custody, staking and SFC consultation. https://apps.sfc.hk/edistributionWeb/api/circular/openFile?lang=EN&refNo=26EC31
2. **Circular on secondary trading of tokenised SFC-authorised investment products (26EC23)**, SFC, 20 Apr 2026. Read paras 8–16, 19–27 and fn 13. They cover trading channels, Connecting Broker duties, and when RIs notify the HKMA. https://apps.sfc.hk/edistributionWeb/api/circular/openFile?lang=EN&refNo=26EC23
3. **Joint circular on intermediaries' VA-related activities**, SFC + HKMA, 22 Dec 2023. Read paras 5–15 and Appendix 4. They set out the selling rules for distributors and the due diligence on funds. https://apps.sfc.hk/edistributionWeb/api/circular/openFile?lang=EN&refNo=23EC66

## Open items

- Question 20F of the FAQs on the Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds holds the detailed staking requirements for VA funds [S:c79c4686c5e0, fn 4, fn 11]. Question 20G covers exposure to stablecoins and tokenised deposits [S:c79c4686c5e0, fn 4, fn 11]. Neither question is in the documents reviewed for this guide.
- For in-kind VA transfers, the supplemental joint circular cites the SFC's AML guideline for LCs and VA service providers [S:d5ebca32c92b, para 7(c)]. The circular does not say how this fits with the HKMA's own AML guideline for AIs.
- The SFC says it will review the first products offered for secondary trading [S:bbd10edd41cf, para 6]. It will then consider widening the product range in due course [S:bbd10edd41cf, para 6]. The SFC has given no timeline [S:bbd10edd41cf, para 6].
- The 2026 Policy Address (the Chief Executive's yearly policy speech) says the SFC will promote trading of regulated stablecoins on licensed VATPs [S:ef3648ff1610, para 49(iii)]. It will also promote their use in settling tokenised money market funds [S:ef3648ff1610, para 49(iii)].

## Related modules

[C1](#m-C1) (Selling, dealing and advising), [C3](#m-C3) (Custody and key management), [C4](#m-C4) (Stablecoins), plus the tokenisation and Project Ensemble modules.


**Business angle:** [Roles in virtual-asset ETFs](#b-va-etf-roles) and [Tokenised funds and money market fund settlement](#b-tokenised-funds) in the Business tab.

title: Custody of digital assets and key management
md:
This module is for the Head of Compliance at a bank that holds, or plans to hold, clients' crypto or tokenised assets. After reading it, you can explain what the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) expects in its May 2026 custody standards. You can also explain what changed from 2024 and how staking fits in. Finally, you can explain how rules from the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) and for stablecoins set the benchmark for counterparties.

## In 60 seconds

Custody means safekeeping assets for clients. In virtual asset (VA) custody, the core risk sits with whoever safekeeps the private keys, or similar tools, that can move the assets [S:f41a543388bc, para 7]. A private key is the secret code that authorises a transfer. So much of the rulebook is about key management [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 10–11]. The HKMA set custody standards for banks, which it calls authorized institutions (AIs), in February 2024 [S:ed61d7c335e7, Implementation, p.2]. On 27 May 2026 it replaced them with an updated annex (a set of detailed standards) of 26 paragraphs [S:ed61d7c335e7, Implementation, p.2; S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 1–26]. The new annex keeps the rule that 98% of client virtual assets (VAs) sit in cold storage, meaning their keys are kept offline [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(b), (l) and fn 8]. It also keeps the rule that keys stay in Hong Kong [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(b), (l) and fn 8]. It adds detailed controls on how wallets, the tools that hold keys, are run [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 10–11, fn 7, para 14(iii); S:86e064b2a8d0, fn 8]. It drops the fixed insurance percentages [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 10–11, fn 7, para 14(iii); S:86e064b2a8d0, fn 8]. With HKMA consent, a bank can now appoint a licensed stablecoin issuer to hold that issuer's own coins [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 10–11, fn 7, para 14(iii); S:86e064b2a8d0, fn 8]. A stablecoin is a token designed to keep a steady value against a currency. The SFC sets custody rules for licensed crypto exchanges, known as virtual asset trading platforms (VATPs) [S:f1bbafccd556, Part X]. These rules are in Part X of the SFC's guidelines for VATP operators, called the VATP Guidelines [S:f1bbafccd556, Part X]. The SFC says the standards in its August 2025 custody circular will also be core expectations for future VA custodians [S:562c0f8addce, p.2]. A circular is a formal notice to regulated firms. In December 2025, the Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau (FSTB) and the SFC published consultation conclusions on licensing custodians [S:f41a543388bc, Introduction, p.3]. Consultation conclusions are the final response to public comments. The conclusions stated an aim to put a bill, or draft law, before the Legislative Council (LegCo) in 2026 [S:f41a543388bc, Introduction, p.3].

## Status board

As of 25 Sep 2026.

| Instrument | Issuer | Date | Status (chip) | Applies to | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Provision of Custodial Services for Digital Assets + Annex | HKMA | 20 Feb 2024 | Superseded | AIs and subsidiaries of local AIs | [S:6bccca749ac2, p.1], [S:86e064b2a8d0, p.1] |
| Updated Guidance on Custodial Services + Annex | HKMA | 27 May 2026 | In force | AIs and subsidiaries of local AIs | [S:ed61d7c335e7, p.2], [S:ce05e67bcdce, p.1] |
| Staking services for VAs from custodial services | HKMA | 7 Apr 2025 | In force | AIs and subsidiaries of local AIs | [S:4641e6c404d2, p.1] |
| Staking services by VATPs + terms and conditions | SFC | 7 Apr 2025 | In force | VATPs and their associated entities | [S:50bf95ba3143, paras 1–2] |
| VATP Guidelines, Part X (custody) | SFC | Jun 2023 | In force | VATPs | [S:f1bbafccd556, paras 10.1–10.23] |
| Circular on custody of VAs (25EC44) | SFC | 15 Aug 2025 | In force | VATPs and associated entities | [S:562c0f8addce, p.1] |
| Guideline on Supervision of Licensed Stablecoin Issuers, para 6.5.7 (keys) | HKMA | Aug 2025 | In force | Licensed stablecoin issuers | [S:240be6833157, p.1] |
| VA custodian services licensing regime | FSTB + SFC | 24 Dec 2025 | Conclusions published | VA custodians, including banks that safekeep keys (licence or registration) | [S:f41a543388bc, paras 6, 35(b)] |

## Key facts

- The 2026 annex covers client digital assets held by AIs [S:ce05e67bcdce, preamble and fn 1–4]. It also covers those held by subsidiaries of locally incorporated AIs (AIs set up as companies in Hong Kong) [S:ce05e67bcdce, preamble and fn 1–4]. Digital assets here include VAs, tokenised securities and other tokenised assets [S:ce05e67bcdce, preamble and fn 1–4]. Tokenised means ownership is recorded on a blockchain or similar ledger. Two groups fall outside the annex: limited purpose digital tokens, and assets the bank or its group holds for itself [S:ce05e67bcdce, preamble and fn 1–4].
- The 2026 letter replaces the February 2024 circular [S:ed61d7c335e7, Implementation, p.2]. Banks already offering custody should review and revise their systems and controls to meet the latest standards [S:ed61d7c335e7, Implementation, p.2]. The 2024 circular set a six-month deadline to notify the HKMA and confirm compliance [S:6bccca749ac2, Implementation, p.2]. The 2026 letter sets no such deadline [S:ed61d7c335e7, Implementation, p.2].
- For client VAs, the annex's key controls are generally required [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11 chapeau]. For other digital assets, the bank may take a risk-based approach, matching controls to the risk [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11 chapeau]. Tokens on public permissionless chains, which anyone can join, call for extra caution [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11 chapeau].
- The rule to keep 98% of client VAs in cold storage has not changed [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(l) and fn 8; S:86e064b2a8d0, fn 6].
- **Compensation changed.** The 2024 annex asked banks for insurance or compensation cover [S:86e064b2a8d0, fn 8]. The cover was 50% of client VAs in cold storage and 100% in hot and other storage [S:86e064b2a8d0, fn 8]. The 2026 annex drops these figures [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(n)]. Instead, the HKMA expects the bank to be liable for losses from incidents attributable to the bank [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(n)]. Adequate financial resources, which may include insurance, back that liability [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(n)]. The 50%/100% figures still apply to VATPs under an SFC rule [S:f1bbafccd556, para 10.22]. For VATPs, the cover takes the form of a compensation arrangement the SFC approves [S:f1bbafccd556, para 10.22].
- **Key location.** Seeds and private keys should still be generated, stored and backed up in Hong Kong [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(b) and fn 7; para 14(iii)]. A seed is the master secret from which keys are made. There is one new exception [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(b) and fn 7; para 14(iii)]. With HKMA consent, a bank may appoint an HKMA-licensed stablecoin issuer to hold that issuer's own coins [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(b) and fn 7; para 14(iii)]. The issuer's keys can then be in Hong Kong or in another location the HKMA accepts [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(b) and fn 7; para 14(iii)].
- **New operating controls.** The annex adds cold-wallet whitelists, lists of approved addresses, with a system check on every transfer [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 10]. It also adds detection of intrusions into vaults, signing devices and code repositories, where software code is stored [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 10]. The annex also sets out these controls [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(a), (c), (f), (g), (i)]:
  - due diligence on hardware security module (HSM) vendors, who supply secure devices that store keys;
  - no smart contracts, or self-running blockchain programs, in cold wallets on public chains;
  - segregation of duties over wallet code, so no one person controls it alone;
  - dedicated devices for approving transactions;
  - integrity checks on critical transaction data, using devices kept off networks (air-gapped);
  - measures to prevent blind signing.
- Security monitoring should run 24/7 [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 23].
- **Anti-money laundering section removed.** The 2024 annex had a separate paragraph on anti-money laundering (AML) and counter-financing of terrorism (CFT), or AML/CFT [S:86e064b2a8d0, para 23]. The 2026 annex has none. The cover letter reminds AIs that every other law and rule that applies to them still applies [S:ed61d7c335e7, p.2].
- Transfers to third parties are now allowed if effective controls are in place [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(m) and fn 9]. They can support payment services or carry out client settlement instructions [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(m) and fn 9]. The definition of client now also covers clients of SFC-licensed VATPs [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(m) and fn 9].
- For staking from custody, the annex points to the HKMA's April 2025 staking guidance [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 26]. Staking means locking up tokens to help run a blockchain in return for rewards. The annex asks banks to have due regard to the SFC's staking terms for VATPs [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 26]. Under the HKMA guidance, the bank should keep control of everything needed to unstake, or withdraw staked tokens [S:4641e6c404d2, sections A–B, Implementation p.3]. It should disclose staking risks such as slashing, a penalty that takes away staked tokens [S:4641e6c404d2, sections A–B, Implementation p.3]. It should also discuss its plans with the HKMA before launch [S:4641e6c404d2, sections A–B, Implementation p.3]. VATPs may not use third-party custody for staked assets [S:50bf95ba3143, para 6].
- The SFC's August 2025 circular took effect immediately [S:562c0f8addce, pp.1–2, Way forward p.7]. It describes security incidents at overseas platforms. The SFC says these incidents point to potential weaknesses in any custody solution [S:562c0f8addce, pp.1–2, Way forward p.7]. That includes an HSM, multi-party computation (MPC) or multi-signature set-up [S:562c0f8addce, pp.1–2, Way forward p.7]. Its standards will also be core expectations for future VA custodians [S:562c0f8addce, pp.1–2, Way forward p.7].
- Under the custodian regime conclusions, the licence will cover custodians that safekeep private keys or similar tools that let VAs be transferred [S:f41a543388bc, paras 6–8, 12]. Custodians of tokenised securities that do not hold VAs fall outside the regime [S:f41a543388bc, paras 6–8, 12].
- The SFC will set a baseline of HK$10 million paid-up share capital, the money owners have put in [S:f41a543388bc, paras 41–42]. It will also set HK$3 million liquid capital, meaning assets that can quickly be turned into cash [S:f41a543388bc, paras 41–42]. Banks remain subject to HKMA capital requirements [S:f41a543388bc, paras 41–42].
- The FSTB and SFC do not plan to let existing providers carry on while they apply for a licence [S:f41a543388bc, paras 48, 51]. But banks already assessed by the HKMA and already providing VA custody get a faster licensing process [S:f41a543388bc, paras 48, 51].
- The consultation paper proposed that the SFC license and register VA custodians and set standards [S:30b60438f017, para 2.12(a)]. It also proposed that the HKMA act as frontline regulator, supervising banks' VA custodian activities [S:30b60438f017, para 2.12(a)]. The conclusions list banks that safekeep keys among those needing a licence or registration [S:f41a543388bc, para 35(b)]. The list also covers subsidiaries of locally incorporated banks that safekeep keys [S:f41a543388bc, para 35(b)].

**Key-management terms, as the documents use them**

- **Hot and cold wallets.** In a hot wallet the private keys sit online, which makes them easier to attack. In a cold wallet they are kept offline [S:8a016a912528, fn 19].
- **HSM (hardware security module).** A secure, tamper-resistant device that creates and stores seeds and keys. Banks should check that the vendor keeps up patching and re-certification [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(a)].
- **Key sharding and multi-signature.** Sharding splits a key among several authorised staff, so no one person holds all of it [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(i)]. A set number of shard-holders must act together to sign [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(i)]. Multi-signature uses several keys to approve one transaction. For stablecoin issuers, those keys should be stored in separate, isolated environments [S:240be6833157, para 6.5.7(iv)].
- **MPC (multi-party computation).** Another way to spread signing power across parties. For licensing, a key question is whether the provider can move client assets on its own [S:f41a543388bc, para 11].
- **Blind signing.** Approving a transaction without reviewing its contents. Banks should show signers every detail in human-readable form before they sign [S:562c0f8addce, fn 6; S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(i)].
- **Whitelisting.** Deposits and withdrawals go only to approved addresses shown to belong to the client [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 10, 11(m)]. The bank can check this, for example, by message signing or by a micropayment test (a tiny trial transfer) [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 10, 11(m)]. The third-party transfer exception still applies [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 10, 11(m)]. Changes to a cold-wallet whitelist are tightly controlled [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 10, 11(m)].
- **Air-gapped devices.** Devices kept off networks, stored in a cold vault and changed only with physical access. Banks should use them to check that critical transaction data is intact [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(g)]. Stablecoin issuers should generate, and use, their most significant keys in air-gapped environments [S:240be6833157, para 6.5.7(ii), (vii)].

## What your bank must do

**Obligations**
- Keep client assets and wallet addresses separate from the bank's own [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 6–7 and fn 6].
- Do not lend, pledge or otherwise use client assets as security [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 6–7 and fn 6]. Three exceptions apply: settling transactions or fees the client owes the bank, explicit written client consent given in advance, or where the law requires it [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 6–7 and fn 6].
- Be liable for losses attributable to the bank, and hold adequate financial resources to cover them [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(n)].
- Disclose the custody arrangements to clients fully and fairly [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 20]. Cover rights on insolvency, segregation, insurance or compensation, and commingling, which means mixing assets together [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 20]. Also explain how forks and airdrops are handled [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 20]. A fork splits a blockchain in two; an airdrop is a free token handout.

**Controls & monitoring**
- Keep 98% of client VAs in cold storage, and keep seeds, keys and backups in Hong Kong [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(b), (l) and fn 8].
- Train transaction signers in depth and run drills of the business continuity plan [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 3, 5].
- Reconcile, or match, each client's holdings regularly against both on-chain records (on the blockchain) and off-chain records (kept outside it) [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 21]. Escalate any discrepancies to senior management [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 21].
- Monitor security 24/7 [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 23–24]. Cover outside dependencies such as vendors, blockchain protocols, encryption methods and shared code libraries [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 23–24].

**Notify / consult HKMA or SFC**
- Discuss plans with the HKMA before launching custody, and show that the bank meets the standards [S:ed61d7c335e7, Implementation, p.2].
- Discuss staking plans with the HKMA before launch [S:4641e6c404d2, Implementation, p.3].
- Provide custody records to the HKMA promptly when asked [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 22].

**Counterparty due diligence**
- As a general principle, delegate VA custody only to one of three types of firm [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 14]:
  - another AI, or a subsidiary of a local AI;
  - an SFC-licensed VATP;
  - a licensed stablecoin issuer for the coins it issues, with HKMA consent.
- Before taking on a custodian, get independent reviews of its code [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 15]. Also understand how it builds and releases software [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 15].
- After taking on a custodian, check its security controls regularly [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 15]. Require it to report incidents promptly, and test its disaster recovery [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 15].
- For a VATP counterparty, the SFC's own custody standards are in the VATP Guidelines [S:f1bbafccd556, paras 10.6–10.8, 10.22; S:562c0f8addce, pp.1–2]. Paras 10.6–10.8 cover cold storage, approved addresses and key management [S:f1bbafccd556, paras 10.6–10.8, 10.22]. Para 10.22 covers the compensation arrangement [S:f1bbafccd556, paras 10.6–10.8, 10.22]. The SFC circular 25EC44 adds detail to these [S:562c0f8addce, pp.1–2]. The HKMA annex points to the VATP Guidelines for reference on delegation [S:ce05e67bcdce, fn 10].

## Talking points

**To the CCO (chief compliance officer)**
- The 2026 annex replaced the 2024 one. Existing services should review and revise their systems and controls to meet the latest standards. The letter sets no transition period [S:ed61d7c335e7, Implementation, p.2].
- The custody annex no longer has an AML/CFT section [S:ed61d7c335e7, p.2]. But the cover letter reminds AIs to comply with all applicable requirements [S:ed61d7c335e7, p.2]. The HKMA's AML/CFT Guideline sets the standards AIs should meet [S:7bfdad704174, para 1.3].

**To business heads**
- With HKMA consent, a bank may now delegate custody of a licensed stablecoin to its issuer [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 14(iii)].
- Transfers to third parties for payments and settlement are now allowed if effective controls are in place [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(m)].

**To the CEO**
- Fixed insurance percentages are gone [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(n); S:86e064b2a8d0, fn 8]. In their place, the bank is liable for losses attributable to it, backed by adequate financial resources [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(n); S:86e064b2a8d0, fn 8].
- The FSTB and SFC conclusions propose a custodian licence set by law [S:f41a543388bc, paras 48, 51]. The conclusions give existing providers no right to carry on while they apply. Banks the HKMA has already assessed get a faster process [S:f41a543388bc, paras 48, 51].

**To Risk / CRO (chief risk officer)**
- The SFC says weaknesses shown by overseas cybersecurity incidents can arise whichever custody solution is used: HSM, MPC or multi-signature [S:562c0f8addce, p.1].
- The HKMA lists slashing, lock-up periods and validator inactivity among staking risks to disclose [S:4641e6c404d2, sections A–B]. A validator is a node that checks blockchain transactions. The bank should keep control of the means to unstake [S:4641e6c404d2, sections A–B].

## Common mix-ups

- "Banks need 50%/100% insurance cover." That was the 2024 rule for banks [S:86e064b2a8d0, fn 8]. It remains the rule for VATPs [S:f1bbafccd556, para 10.22]. It is not the rule for banks from 2026 [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(n)].
- "The February 2024 annex is still current." It was superseded on 27 May 2026 [S:ed61d7c335e7, Implementation, p.2].
- "Keys may never leave Hong Kong." The general rule stands [S:ce05e67bcdce, fn 7]. But an issuer appointed to hold its own coins may keep keys elsewhere if the HKMA accepts the location [S:ce05e67bcdce, fn 7].
- "The custodian regime covers tokenised securities." It does not, because the legal definition of VA excludes securities [S:f41a543388bc, para 12].
- "MPC or HSM equals compliance." The SFC says weaknesses can exist in any custody solution [S:562c0f8addce, p.1].

## Read these first

1. **Updated Guidance on Expected Standards on Provision of Custodial Services for Digital Assets by Authorized Institutions (Annex)**, HKMA, 27 May 2026. Read paras 6–13 on segregation and safeguarding. Read paras 14–19 on delegation. Read paras 23–26 on monitoring and staking. These are the HKMA's current custody standards for AIs. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20260527-7-EN/20260527-7-EN.pdf
2. **Circular to licensed virtual asset trading platform operators on custody of virtual assets (25EC44)**, SFC, 15 Aug 2025. Read Sections I–VI (paras 1–28) and the good-practice boxes. The SFC says these standards will be core expectations for future VA custodians. https://apps.sfc.hk/edistributionWeb/api/circular/openFile?lang=EN&refNo=25EC44
3. **Consultation Conclusions: Legislative Proposal to Regulate Virtual Asset Custodian Services**, FSTB + SFC, December 2025. Read paras 5–16 on scope and paras 25–26 on individuals. Read para 35 on who needs a licence. Read paras 41–52 on capital and transition. https://www.fstb.gov.hk/fsb/en/publication/consult/doc/Custodian_consultation_conclusion_e.pdf

## Open items

- The FSTB and SFC stated an aim to put the custodian bill before LegCo in 2026 [S:f41a543388bc, Introduction, p.3]. The documents reviewed do not show that it has been introduced. No start date for the regime is set [S:f41a543388bc, para 49].
- The SFC said it would consult on custody for private funds, in a separate paper issued the same day [S:f41a543388bc, para 32]. The question is whether firms providing VA management services must use SFC-regulated custodians for private funds' VAs [S:f41a543388bc, para 32].
- The 2024 annex referred to AML/CFT guidance from the HKMA on custody of digital assets [S:86e064b2a8d0, para 23]. The documents reviewed do not show whether such separate guidance exists.

## Related modules

[C1](#m-C1) (Selling, dealing and advising), [C2](#m-C2) (VA funds and exchange-traded funds (ETFs)), [C4](#m-C4) (Stablecoins). Also see the cyber and technology risk module and the AML/CFT module.


**Business angle:** [Virtual-asset custody](#b-custody) and [Staking services](#b-staking) in the Business tab.

title: Stablecoins
md:
For the bank's Head of Compliance (digital assets). After this module you can explain Hong Kong's stablecoin law and what a licensed issuer must do. You can also explain each role a bank can play:

- issuer of its own coins;
- offeror (a firm that sells or offers coins to the public);
- dealer or adviser;
- custodian (a firm that keeps coins safe for clients);
- holder of coins on its own balance sheet.

## In 60 seconds

A stablecoin is a digital token designed to keep a steady value against a currency or other asset. The Stablecoins Ordinance (Cap. 656) took effect on 1 August 2025. [S:0df2de5234dc, para 1] It covers the fiat-referenced stablecoin (FRS), meaning a stablecoin tied to one or more official currencies. A business needs a licence from the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) to issue an FRS in Hong Kong. [S:ad1082eb2ea9, para 2] It also needs one to issue a Hong Kong dollar FRS, whether in or outside Hong Kong. [S:ad1082eb2ea9, para 2]

Licensed issuers must back each type of coin in full with reserves kept apart from their own assets. [S:240be6833157, paras 2.2.1, 2.5.1, 3.3.3, 6.5.7] They must not pay interest. [S:fe4baea8dd7d, para 3.13.1] The HKMA expects them to pay out valid redemptions at face value (par), normally within one business day. [S:240be6833157, paras 2.2.1, 2.5.1, 3.3.3, 6.5.7] Its expectations also cover strict control of private keys, the secret codes that move the coins.
