[S:240be6833157, paras 2.2.1, 2.5.1, 3.3.3, 6.5.7]

Only permitted offerors may offer these coins. [S:fe4baea8dd7d, para 2.10.1] Authorized institutions (AIs), the HKMA's term for banks and other deposit-takers, are permitted offerors. [S:fe4baea8dd7d, para 2.10.1] Retail investors may only be offered coins from licensed issuers. [S:7b6c8dc63140, reply (1), para 1]

The first two licences took effect on 10 April 2026. [S:270f1f7324ab, Register table] The HKMA says that if it grants more, the total will remain very limited. [S:193316443831, Follow-up work section, para 3]

On 27 May 2026 the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) eased some conduct rules for these coins. [S:a0bd48559762, pp.1-2, 9]; [S:19d52ade6849, p.1] The circulars call them Relevant Stablecoins. The eased rules are those for virtual asset (VA) services, such as dealing and advice. The HKMA circular covers registered institutions (RIs), meaning banks registered with the SFC for securities business. [S:a0bd48559762, pp.1-2, 9] Both regulators kept the duty to notify them in advance. [S:a0bd48559762, pp.1-2, 9]; [S:19d52ade6849, p.1]

For coins a bank holds itself, the bank sorts them into a risk group under CRP-1, the HKMA's capital module on cryptoassets. [S:b7d630146e6c, paras 1.3.1-1.3.2] It treats them under LM-1, the HKMA's liquidity module (rules on managing liquidity risk). [S:69600121310a, Annex 3, paras 6-7]

## Status board

As of 25 September 2026. Abbreviations used below:

- FSTB = Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau (the Government's policy bureau).
- LegCo = Legislative Council.
- AML/CFT = anti-money laundering (AML) and counter-financing of terrorism (CFT).
- RI = registered institution (a bank registered with the SFC).
- LCs = corporations licensed by the SFC.
- VATPs = virtual asset trading platforms licensed by the SFC.

| Instrument | Issuer | Date | Status (chip) | Applies to | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Discussion Paper on Crypto-assets and Stablecoins | HKMA | 12 Jan 2022 | Superseded | Public; AIs | [S:2b888e600616, Section 6] |
| Consultation paper on stablecoin issuer regime | FSTB + HKMA | 27 Dec 2023 | Superseded | Public | [S:167649d1bc28, para 3] |
| Consultation conclusions | FSTB + HKMA | 17 Jul 2024 | Superseded | Public | [S:54aa01e7396e, para 12.1] |
| Stablecoin issuer sandbox (a supervised testing scheme) | HKMA | 12 Mar 2024 | Superseded | Would-be issuers | [S:28616d929735, para 1] |
| Stablecoins Ordinance (Cap. 656) | LegCo / HKMA | 1 Aug 2025 | In force | Issuers; offerors incl. AIs | [S:0df2de5234dc, para 1] |
| Supervisory Guideline and AML/CFT Guideline for licensed issuers | HKMA | 1 Aug 2025 | In force | Licensed issuers, incl. an AI licensee | [S:6c3f349e4f90, para 1] |
| Explanatory Note on Licensing | HKMA | Jul 2025 | In force | Applicants | [S:fe4baea8dd7d, Chapter 3] |
| Stablecoin Review Tribunal (current membership) | FSTB | 1 Nov 2025 | In force | People aggrieved by HKMA decisions | [S:16699fe49364, paras 2-3] |
| Register of licensed issuers | HKMA | 10 Apr 2026 | In force | Public; counterparties | [S:270f1f7324ab, Register table] |
| Supervisory Policy Manual (SPM) CRP-1 and LM-1 (V.5) cryptoasset treatment | HKMA | 1 Jan 2026; 19 Dec 2025 | In force | All AIs | [S:b7d630146e6c, para 1.4.1]; [S:69600121310a, Annex 3] |
| RI circular and AI letter on Relevant Stablecoins | HKMA (with SFC) | 27 May 2026 | In force | RIs; all AIs | [S:a0bd48559762, p.1]; [S:1babdb609fc8, p.1] |
| SFC circular 26EC26 | SFC | 27 May 2026 | In force | VATPs; LCs | [S:19d52ade6849, p.1, opening paragraph] |

## Key facts

- History: the HKMA issued a discussion paper in January 2022. Its conclusions, in January 2023, reported 58 responses. [S:c72a4b732293, para 1.4] The FSTB and HKMA then consulted the public from 27 December 2023 to 29 February 2024. [S:167649d1bc28, para 3] They published consultation conclusions on 17 July 2024, after 108 responses. [S:54aa01e7396e, paras 1-2]
- The Government published the Bill in the Gazette on 6 December 2024. [S:a9a82f2b38ce, para 1] LegCo passed it on 21 May 2025. [S:35e1ac2b815a, para 1] The Ordinance took effect on 1 August 2025. [S:0df2de5234dc, para 1]
- A licence is required to issue an FRS in Hong Kong as a business. [S:ad1082eb2ea9, para 2] A licence is also needed to issue a Hong Kong dollar FRS, in or outside Hong Kong. [S:ad1082eb2ea9, para 2]
- For now, only FRS count as specified stablecoins (the coins the law covers). Bank deposits are outside the definition. So is stored value facility (SVF) float, the money customers hold in e-wallets. Securities are outside it too. [S:fe4baea8dd7d, paras 2.1.2, 2.2.1-2.2.2]
- Permitted offerors are licensed issuers, AIs and SVF licensees. [S:fe4baea8dd7d, para 2.10.1] Virtual asset trading platforms licensed by the SFC also qualify. [S:fe4baea8dd7d, para 2.10.1] So do corporations licensed by the SFC for Type 1 regulated activity (dealing in securities). [S:fe4baea8dd7d, para 2.10.1]
- Permitted offerors may offer licensed issuers' coins to anyone. They may offer other specified stablecoins only to professional investors (investors who meet legal wealth or institution tests). Over-the-counter virtual asset shops are not permitted offerors. [S:7b6c8dc63140, reply (1), paras 1-2]
- Only advertisements for licensed FRS issuance may be published. This rule also applied during the six-month grace period for existing issuers. [S:ad1082eb2ea9, para 3]
- An AI incorporated outside Hong Kong may apply without setting up a local subsidiary. The criteria on financial resources and business activity do not apply to AI applicants. No one needs HKMA consent to become an AI applicant's controller, chief executive or director. [S:fe4baea8dd7d, paras 3.2.1-3.2.3; fns 1, 6, 8]
- A licensed issuer must keep paid-up capital (money shareholders have paid in) of at least HK$25 million. An AI that holds a licence is exempt. The Banking Ordinance sets its capital instead. [S:240be6833157, paras 5.1.1, 5.1.3]
- Reserves must be worth at least the face value of all coins in circulation, at all times. Reserves must be kept segregated, meaning separate from the issuer's own assets. The HKMA expects an effective trust arrangement and a qualified custodian. Reserve deposits should have a term of three months or less. Debt securities should have one year or less left to run. [S:240be6833157, paras 2.2.1, 2.3.1, 2.5.1-2.5.4]
- Issuers must honour valid redemptions at face value. They cannot charge unreasonable fees or set unduly burdensome conditions. They should process each redemption within one business day, unless the HKMA approves otherwise. [S:240be6833157, paras 3.3.3, 3.3.5]
- Licensees may not pay interest or any yield linked to holding a coin. [S:fe4baea8dd7d, para 3.13.1]
- Private-key controls should cover every stage of a key's life. Significant keys should be created offline, on equipment never linked to a network (air-gapped). Keys should be stored in Hong Kong or another place the HKMA accepts. [S:240be6833157, para 6.5.7 and items (ii), (iv)]
- The issuer AML/CFT Guideline sets a HK$8,000 threshold for two things. One is customer due diligence (identity and risk checks) on one-off transactions. The other is the fuller data set sent with stablecoin transfers. [S:4d98c6a80b4d, paras 4.4, 6.5-6.6, 5.11]
- Each holder's identity should be verified. The licensee, a supervised institution or a reliable third party can do this. The exception is where a licensee shows the HKMA that its risk controls are effective. [S:4d98c6a80b4d, paras 4.4, 6.5-6.6, 5.11]
- An issuer already operating before the law had to apply by 31 October 2025 if it wanted a licence. If it applied, it could keep operating until 31 January 2026. The exception was an issuer that had entered a closing-down period. [S:6c3f349e4f90, Explanatory Note on Transitional Provisions, paras 3.3, 4.1]
- The HKMA received 36 applications in the first batch. [S:193316443831, paras 1, 3] It licensed two issuers, effective 10 April 2026 (register numbers in brackets): Anchorpoint Financial Limited (FRS01) and The Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation Limited (FRS02). [S:193316443831, paras 1, 3]; [S:270f1f7324ab, Register table]
- In June 2026 the Government said that if more licences are granted, the total will remain very limited. It expected the first regulated stablecoin launch as early as mid-2026. [S:3f0fcc104e61, Reply (1)-(2)]
- Complaints: the issuer should acknowledge a complaint within 7 calendar days. It should give a full or interim response within 30 calendar days. It should generally give a full response within 60 calendar days. [S:240be6833157, para 8.4.3] The HKMA may take up complaints the issuer has not handled properly. It generally does not order compensation. [S:d3e75db3ddb3, Lodging Complaint with the HKMA section]
- The current Stablecoin Review Tribunal panel serves a three-year term ending 31 October 2028. [S:16699fe49364, paras 2-3] A person aggrieved by (adversely affected by) an HKMA decision may refer it to the Tribunal in writing. The deadline is 30 days after the HKMA makes the decision, or another period the Tribunal permits. [S:16699fe49364, paras 2-3]
- On 28 April 2026 the HKMA warned about tokens using the tickers (trading symbols) HKDAP or HSBC. The HKMA said the licensed issuers did not issue these tokens and had no link to them. Both licensees had confirmed they had not yet issued any regulated stablecoins. [S:275e7319a841, paras 2-3]

## What your bank must do

**Obligations**
- [ ] Offer only licensed issuers' coins to retail clients when acting as an offeror. Offer other specified stablecoins only to professional investors. [S:7b6c8dc63140, reply (1), para 1]; [S:0df2de5234dc, para 4]
- [ ] Follow the RI standards when dealing, advising or managing portfolios in Relevant Stablecoins. Follow the terms in Appendices A1 and A2 too. The HKMA expects this of all AIs. [S:1babdb609fc8, p.1]
- [ ] Disclose material information on each Relevant Stablecoin when dealing or advising. Cover its stabilisation arrangements (how it keeps its value) and its redemption arrangements (how holders get money back). [S:a0bd48559762, para (5), p.5 and para (10), p.7]

**Controls & monitoring**
- [ ] Mark clearly the accounts of clients who trade only Relevant Stablecoins, to use the lighter rules for them. Deal in no other virtual assets for those clients. [S:a0bd48559762, para (3)(a) and fn 4, p.4] Dealing in other virtual assets for a client brings back the full virtual asset rules. These include the knowledge assessment, a check of the client's understanding of virtual assets. [S:a0bd48559762, para (3)(a) and fn 4, p.4]
- [ ] Base advice on the client's use case (what the client needs the coin for), not on commission rebates. [S:a0bd48559762, para (8), p.6]
- [ ] Classify stablecoin holdings under CRP-1. A coin is Group 1b (a lower-risk stablecoin group) only if it meets classification conditions 1-4. Here, full redeemability means redemption within five calendar days. [S:b7d630146e6c, paras 1.3.1-1.3.2, 2.3.2]
- [ ] Treat held stablecoins as debt securities outside high-quality liquid assets (HQLA), if your bank is a category 1 institution for liquidity. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3, paras 6-7] Under the liquidity coverage ratio (LCR), a short-term cash stress test, the usual inflow is 0%. The bank counts no cash coming in from them. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3, paras 6-7] Under the net stable funding ratio (NSFR), a longer-term funding test, the required stable funding factor is 85%. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3, paras 6-7] An issuing bank must apply a 100% LCR outflow if the coin is redeemable within the LCR period. In effect, it assumes holders cash in every such coin. Lower rates are possible where the backing assets qualify as HQLA. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3, paras 6-7]

**Notify / consult HKMA or SFC**
- [ ] RIs: notify the HKMA and SFC before any Relevant Stablecoin activity or material change. [S:a0bd48559762, Implementation, p.9]
- [ ] All AIs: discuss Relevant Stablecoin services with the HKMA first. [S:1babdb609fc8, Implementation, p.2]
- [ ] Notify the HKMA when you acquire a new type of cryptoasset. Treat it as Group 2b (the highest-risk group) until the HKMA agrees its classification. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2]

**Counterparty due diligence**
- [ ] Check any claimed issuer against the HKMA Register of licensed issuers. [S:270f1f7324ab, Register table] The HKMA points the public to the Register to verify licensees. [S:afb6cd0da6ff, paras 4-5]
- [ ] Hand custody (safekeeping) of stablecoins to a licensed issuer only for that issuer's own coins. An AI may do so only if the issuer has HKMA consent to provide that custody. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 14 and fn 7]

## Talking points

**To the Chief Compliance Officer (CCO)**
- Banks are permitted offerors. Only licensed issuers' coins may be offered to retail investors. [S:fe4baea8dd7d, para 2.10.1]; [S:7b6c8dc63140, reply (1), para 1]
- RIs notify the HKMA and SFC before Relevant Stablecoin activity. Other AIs discuss it with the HKMA first. [S:a0bd48559762, p.9]; [S:1babdb609fc8, p.2]

**To business heads**
- Two issuers hold licences, effective 10 April 2026. The HKMA says any further licences would keep the total very limited. [S:270f1f7324ab, Register table]; [S:193316443831, Follow-up work section, para 3]
- Relevant-Stablecoin-only dealing is not limited to RIs registered for Type 1 (dealing in securities). Clearly marked Relevant-Stablecoin-only accounts need no virtual asset knowledge test. The Appendix A1 conditions still apply. [S:a0bd48559762, paras (2), (3)(a)]

**To the Chief Executive Officer (CEO)**
- A bank can apply to issue stablecoins. The minimum criteria on financial resources and business activities do not apply to AI applicants. [S:fe4baea8dd7d, para 3.2.1; fns 1, 8]
- In June 2026 the Government expected the first regulated stablecoin launch as early as mid-2026. [S:3f0fcc104e61, Reply (1)]

**To Risk / Chief Risk Officer (CRO)**
- For liquidity, a held stablecoin counts as a debt security that is not HQLA. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3, para 7] An issuing bank must apply a 100% LCR outflow if the coin is redeemable within the LCR period. Lower rates are possible with HQLA-eligible backing. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3, para 7]
- HKMA-licensed coins can be treated as meeting CRP-1's extra measures for permissionless blockchains (public networks anyone can join). They still need conditions 1-4 to reach Group 1. [S:b7d630146e6c, paras 1.3.1, 2.6.3]

## Common mix-ups

- **Myth:** "A Relevant Stablecoin is an investment product." **Fact:** The HKMA letter says its guidance should not be read that way. [S:1babdb609fc8, p.1]
- **Myth:** "Sandbox firms are licensed." **Fact:** Joining the sandbox was not a licence. [S:28616d929735, Testing in the sandbox section, para 2] The HKMA later said the sandbox is neither a precondition nor a guarantee of a licence. [S:e0b249a7eb8c, Licensing regime section, para 5]
- **Myth:** "A licence means coins are live." **Fact:** On 28 April 2026 both licensees confirmed they had not yet issued any coins. [S:275e7319a841, para 3]
- **Myth:** "The SFC's circular 26EC26 governs our bank." **Fact:** It covers VATPs and LCs. [S:19d52ade6849, p.1, opening paragraph and fn 2] For RIs, it points to the HKMA RI circular. [S:a0bd48559762, p.1]
- **Myth:** "Only Hong Kong firms are caught." **Fact:** A business that issues Hong Kong dollar coins needs a licence wherever it issues them. [S:ad1082eb2ea9, para 2]
- **Myth:** "The HKMA will get my client compensated." **Fact:** The HKMA generally does not order issuers to pay compensation. [S:d3e75db3ddb3, Lodging Complaint with the HKMA section]

## Read these first

1. **Explanatory Note on Licensing of Stablecoin Issuers**, HKMA, July 2025. Read Chapter 2 and Chapter 3, especially 3.2-3.5 and 3.13. It covers scope, offerors, licensing criteria and the exceptions for AIs. https://www.hkma.gov.hk/media/eng/doc/key-functions/ifc/stablecoin-issuers/Explanatory_Notes_on_Licensing_of_Stablecoin_Issuers_eng.pdf
2. **Guideline on Supervision of Licensed Stablecoin Issuers**, HKMA, 1 August 2025. Read sections 2-3, 6.5 and 8.4. They cover reserves, redemption, keys and complaints. https://www.hkma.gov.hk/media/eng/doc/key-functions/ifc/stablecoin-issuers/Guideline_on_supervision_of_licensed_stablecoin_issuers_eng.pdf
3. **Circular on virtual asset activities involving Relevant Stablecoins (RI circular)**, HKMA, 27 May 2026. Read all nine pages. It shows how a bank deals, advises and distributes. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20260527-2-EN/20260527-2-EN.pdf

## Open items

- No document reviewed for this guide confirms that either licensee had launched a regulated stablecoin by 25 September 2026.
- The HKMA has told applicants it has no settled view on the direction and timing of further licensing. [S:3f0fcc104e61, Reply (2)]
- On 3 June 2026 the HKMA loosened CRP-1 para 2.6.4 for tokenised traditional assets, not stablecoins. [S:dca53ff0a62c, p.1] Tokenised traditional assets are ordinary assets, such as bonds, recorded as digital tokens. The change took effect at once. The HKMA said it will update the CRP-1 wording in due course. [S:dca53ff0a62c, p.1] No document reviewed for this guide has the updated CRP-1 text.
- The 2026 Policy Address says the SFC will promote the trading of regulated stablecoins on licensed trading platforms for virtual assets. It will also promote their use to settle tokenised money market funds. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 49(iii)] The documents reviewed for this guide contain no detailed measures.
- This guide has not reviewed the text of Cap. 656 on e-Legislation, the official online database of Hong Kong laws. Section numbers here come from HKMA documents.

## Related modules

[B2](#m-B2), [C1](#m-C1), [C3](#m-C3), [C5](#m-C5), [D3](#m-D3)


**Business angle:** [Stablecoin roles for banks](#b-stablecoin-roles) and [Tokenised deposits and payments](#b-tokenised-deposits) in the Business tab.

title: Tokenisation: tokenised products, deposits and bonds
md:
This module is for a bank's Head of Compliance (digital assets). After reading it, you can explain which tokenisation rules bind the bank today. You can also explain which Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) projects the bank may join, and what is still only a stated plan.

## In 60 seconds

Tokenisation records a claim on an asset, such as a bond, fund unit, gold or a bank deposit. [S:a9aa06fbcc12, paras 2, 5; S:b2719f3dcb37, p.1 and fn 1] The claim is recorded on distributed ledger technology (DLT) or similar technology. [S:a9aa06fbcc12, paras 2, 5; S:b2719f3dcb37, p.1 and fn 1] A distributed ledger is a shared digital record kept in step across many computers.

Hong Kong regulators apply the rules for the underlying product to its tokenised form. They also add expectations on technology, ownership and custody risks. [S:b2719f3dcb37, pp.2-3; S:a9aa06fbcc12, paras 7-8]

For authorized institutions (AIs), meaning banks, the HKMA set these expectations in a February 2024 circular. [S:b2719f3dcb37, p.1] A circular is a formal notice a regulator sends to the firms it supervises.

The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) has circulars on tokenised securities. It also has circulars on tokenised SFC-authorised investment products, such as funds the SFC has authorised for sale to the public. [S:a9aa06fbcc12, para 35 and fn 8; S:58ea8520974d, para 18] These circulars reach SFC licensed corporations (LCs). They also reach banks acting as registered institutions (RIs), meaning banks registered with the SFC for securities business. [S:a9aa06fbcc12, para 35 and fn 8; S:58ea8520974d, para 18]

The HKMA's Project Ensemble entered a real-value pilot, EnsembleTX (live transactions with real money), in November 2025. [S:8b67e8dc510f, paras 1-3; S:d193f12a5f78, Annex A] Seven named Tokenised Deposit Banks are to offer tokenised deposits through it. They are also to settle payments between banks through it. [S:8b67e8dc510f, paras 1-3; S:d193f12a5f78, Annex A]

The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR) Government has made three tokenised bond issues, in 2023, 2024 and 2025. [S:fc3eb72031c6, para 5] The Hong Kong Mortgage Corporation (HKMC) priced its first digital bond in June 2026. [S:6aa27ee8b400, para 1]

The 2026 Policy Address, the Chief Executive's yearly policy speech, lists these next steps. They are stated targets, not rules. [S:ef3648ff1610, paras 35(ii)-(iv), 37(i), 50]
- Settlement in central bank digital currency (CBDC) for EnsembleTX, and round-the-clock (24/7) operation.
- A digital asset platform at CMU OmniClear, the operator of the Central Moneymarkets Unit (CMU). The CMU is Hong Kong's central system for holding and settling bonds.
- Tests of tokenised Exchange Fund Bills (short-term debt papers the HKMA issues).
- A second-phase legal review with the Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau (FSTB). [S:ef3648ff1610, paras 35(ii)-(iv), 37(i), 50]

## Key facts

- The HKMA circular covers tokenised real-world assets. Examples are spot precious metal and structured investment products outside the Securities and Futures Ordinance (SFO). [S:b2719f3dcb37, p.1 and fn 1; Sections A-D; p.6] It excludes stablecoins (tokens built to hold a steady value) and products covered by the SFO. [S:b2719f3dcb37, p.1 and fn 1; Sections A-D; p.6] AIs should also meet its standards when customers place tokenised deposits. [S:b2719f3dcb37, p.1 and fn 1; Sections A-D; p.6] The circular expects: [S:b2719f3dcb37, p.1 and fn 1; Sections A-D; p.6]
  - checks on issuers and vendors (due diligence)
  - plain-language risk disclosure
  - HKMA custody standards, where relevant
  - discussion with the HKMA in advance.
- Existing selling and investor-protection rules for a product also apply to its tokenised form. [S:b2719f3dcb37, p.2] AIs should still assess whether tokenisation changes what the product is. [S:b2719f3dcb37, p.2] For example, selling small fractions of an asset could turn it into a collective investment scheme (a pooled investment, like a fund). [S:b2719f3dcb37, p.2]
- The SFC treats tokenised securities as traditional securities in a tokenisation wrapper. [S:a9aa06fbcc12, paras 7, 21, 24, 26-27] Whether one is a complex product is judged by looking at the underlying security. This holds as long as the technology risks are well managed. [S:a9aa06fbcc12, paras 7, 21, 24, 26-27] A complex product is one whose risks are hard for retail investors to understand. The SFC no longer imposes its mandatory 2019 restriction that tokenised securities go to professional investors only. Public-offering rules still apply. [S:a9aa06fbcc12, paras 7, 21, 24, 26-27]
- RIs that plan activity in digital securities should notify the SFC and the HKMA in advance. [S:a9aa06fbcc12, para 35 and fn 8]
- The SFC allows primary dealing (buying new units and cashing them in) in tokenised SFC-authorised investment products. [S:58ea8520974d, paras 5, 10, 13] Product providers stay responsible for the tokenisation arrangement. [S:58ea8520974d, paras 5, 10, 13] They should not use public-permissionless chains (open networks anyone can join) without extra controls. One such control is a permissioned token, which only approved holders can hold. [S:58ea8520974d, paras 5, 10, 13]
- Since 20 April 2026, the SFC allows secondary trading of these products on SFC-licensed VATPs. Secondary trading means investors buying and selling among themselves after issue. [S:a64e364fd912, paras 4, 8, 12, 27 and fn 13] The trading is subject to fair-pricing and other controls. RIs taking part should also notify the HKMA. [S:a64e364fd912, paras 4, 8, 12, 27 and fn 13]
- Project Ensemble first focused on tokenised deposits, meaning commercial bank deposits held in digital token form. [S:5a9cad53f2be, para 2] EnsembleTX moved Ensemble from proof-of-concept (a trial to show an idea works) to real-value transactions. [S:8b67e8dc510f, paras 1-3] It starts with tokenised money market funds and treasury (cash management) uses. [S:8b67e8dc510f, paras 1-3] Payments between banks first settle on the Hong Kong dollar Real Time Gross Settlement system. That system settles each payment in full, one by one, as it happens. [S:8b67e8dc510f, paras 1-3]
- The HKMA lists seven Tokenised Deposit Banks for EnsembleTX: [S:d193f12a5f78, Annex A]
  - Bank of China (Hong Kong)
  - China Construction Bank (Asia)
  - Fubon Bank (Hong Kong)
  - Fusion Bank
  - Standard Chartered Bank (Hong Kong)
  - The Bank of East Asia
  - The Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation
- The HKMA's liquidity guideline LM-1 (V.5, Dec 2025) covers tokenised deposits that a bank issues. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3 para 4] Here, a tokenised deposit is a legally binding claim on the bank, redeemable at face value (par) in ordinary currency (fiat). [S:69600121310a, Annex 3 para 4] A category 1 bank may treat them as deposits or unsecured funding for the liquidity coverage ratio (LCR). [S:69600121310a, Annex 3 para 4] The LCR tests whether a bank holds enough easy-to-sell assets to meet cash outflows under stress. The deposits get no stable-deposit or stable-funding treatment, even when retail or small business customers hold them. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3 para 4] That treatment is for money the rules assume is less likely to leave the bank.
- The DBGS pays 50% of eligible expenses, up to a cap. [S:5a0563de8142, s.1] The cap is HK$1.25m for a Half Grant and HK$2.5m for a Full Grant. [S:5a0563de8142, s.1] An issuer and its associates (related companies) can get grants for at most two issuances. [S:5a0563de8142, s.1]
- For a Full Grant, all of these conditions must hold: [S:5a0563de8142, s.3]
  - The DLT platform provider is not an associate of the issuer.
  - The issue is at least HK$1bn.
  - The issue goes to five or more investors not associated with the issuer or platform provider.
  - The issue is listed on the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong or on one of the SFC-licensed VATPs.
- The FSTB and HKMA phase-1 review found Hong Kong's legal and regulatory framework already flexible enough for tokenised bond issues. [S:279f10054c6e, opening para and 'Issuing clarifications' section] A debenture is a company's written promise to repay a debt, such as a bond. The Companies Registry's FAQs confirm that a DLT register of debenture holders can be treated as meeting the record-keeping rules of the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622). [S:279f10054c6e, opening para and 'Issuing clarifications' section]

## What your bank must do

**Obligations**
- Apply existing product-selling rules to tokenised products. Add the HKMA's tokenisation-specific expectations on top. [S:b2719f3dcb37, pp.2-3]
- Apply the circular's standards when customers place tokenised deposits. [S:b2719f3dcb37, fn 1]
- As a distributor of tokenised SFC-authorised products, the bank should be a regulated intermediary, such as a registered institution (RI). [S:58ea8520974d, para 18] It should also follow existing onboarding and suitability rules (checking a product fits the customer). [S:58ea8520974d, para 18]

**Controls & monitoring**
- Carry out due diligence on the product, its issuer and third-party vendors. Do it before offering the product and at intervals after. [S:b2719f3dcb37, Section A, pp.3-4] Cover key management (how the keys that control tokens are kept safe) and audits. [S:b2719f3dcb37, Section A, pp.3-4]
- Give customers plain-language disclosures on tokenisation risks. [S:b2719f3dcb37, Section B, pp.4-5]
- Meet the HKMA's digital asset custody standards if the bank holds tokenised products for customers (custody). [S:b2719f3dcb37, Section D, p.6]

**Notify / consult HKMA or SFC**
- Discuss plans for tokenised products with the HKMA in advance. [S:b2719f3dcb37, 'Implementation', p.6]
- Notify the SFC and the HKMA before starting digital-securities activity as an RI. [S:a9aa06fbcc12, para 35 and fn 8]
- Notify the HKMA as well when taking part, as an RI, in secondary trading of tokenised SFC-authorised products. [S:a64e364fd912, para 27 and fn 13]
- Consider the HKMA's Supervisory Incubator for DLT (optional). Banks can use it to reaffirm their risk controls before a full launch. [S:1b1a0de5de5a, para 3]

**Counterparty due diligence**
- Assess the track record of the issuer and the tokenisation platform. Also assess their controls over keys and ownership records. [S:b2719f3dcb37, Section A, pp.3-4]
- Consider, for tokenised bonds, the product's legal status and whether settlement is final. [S:b2719f3dcb37, Section A, p.4; Section B, p.5] Final settlement means a completed transfer is legally fixed and stays in place. For example, the HKMA states that a law protects the finality of CMU settlement for the Government digital green bonds. [S:4290ec1111e3, fn 2]

## Talking points

**To the CCO**
- Existing product rules apply to tokenised products. The HKMA adds expectations on due diligence, disclosure and early discussion with it. [S:b2719f3dcb37, pp.2-6]
- As an RI, the bank should tell the SFC and the HKMA before digital-securities work. [S:a9aa06fbcc12, fn 8] It should also notify the HKMA before secondary trading of tokenised SFC-authorised products. [S:a64e364fd912, fn 13]

**To business heads**
- EnsembleTX is to run throughout 2026 with real-value tokenised-deposit settlement. [S:8b67e8dc510f, para 3 and CE remarks] The HKMA invites parties with real-value tokenised-deposit use cases to take part. [S:8b67e8dc510f, para 3 and CE remarks]
- The DBGS Full Grant pays up to HK$2.5m per issue. It is not available if the DLT platform provider is an associate of the issuer. [S:5a0563de8142, ss.1, 3] A Half Grant of up to HK$1.25m may still apply. [S:5a0563de8142, ss.1, 3]

**To the CEO**
- The Government has made three tokenised bond issues. [S:fc3eb72031c6, para 5] The latest raised about HK$10bn. [S:ac6cd085a325, para 1] The HKMC priced a digital bond of about HK$12bn in June 2026. [S:6aa27ee8b400, para 1]
- The Policy Address targets CBDC settlement and 24/7 operation for EnsembleTX around end-2026. It also targets a CMU OmniClear digital asset platform this year. [S:ef3648ff1610, paras 35(iv), 50]

**To Risk / CRO**
- Tokenised deposits the bank issues cannot get stable-deposit treatment in the LCR. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3 para 4] If the bank cannot always identify the holders, it must treat them as "other unsecured wholesale funding". [S:69600121310a, Annex 3 para 4]
- The HKMA's April 2024 DLT risk considerations are not binding. They cover network choice, smart contracts (code that runs by itself on a ledger), legal risks such as settlement finality, and third parties. They also cover interoperability (systems working together), cybersecurity and private-key security. [S:1884530ff235, Introduction and items 2-8]

## Common mix-ups

- **Myth:** Tokenised securities are automatically complex or for professional investors only. **Fact:** The SFC looks through to the underlying security. It no longer imposes a mandatory professional-investor-only restriction. [S:a9aa06fbcc12, paras 24, 26]
- **Myth:** The HKMA tokenised-products circular covers stablecoins. **Fact:** The circular expressly excludes them. [S:b2719f3dcb37, fn 1]
- **Myth:** Secondary trading of tokenised SFC-authorised products is still barred. **Fact:** That was the 2023 position. [S:d422282a262d, paras 6-7] The revised April 2026 framework allows it on SFC-licensed VATPs, subject to conditions. [S:58ea8520974d, para 6]
- **Myth:** EnsembleTX is not an official name. **Fact:** The HKMA uses the name in its own November 2025 announcement and annex. [S:8b67e8dc510f, para 1]; [S:d193f12a5f78, Annex A]

## Read these first

1. **Sale and distribution of tokenised products**, HKMA, 20 Feb 2024. Read the whole circular (6 pages), especially Sections A-D and 'Implementation'. It is the bank's baseline for tokenised products. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20240220-10-EN/20240220-10-EN.pdf
2. **Circular on secondary trading of tokenised SFC-authorised investment products**, SFC, 20 Apr 2026. Read paragraphs 8-27 and footnotes 13-14. They set out duties for connecting brokers, distributors and RIs. https://apps.sfc.hk/edistributionWeb/api/circular/openFile?lang=EN&refNo=26EC23
3. **EnsembleTX announcement and Annexes A/B**, HKMA, 13 Nov 2025. Read the full release and both annexes. They show the pilot's scope and participants. https://www.hkma.gov.hk/eng/news-and-media/press-releases/2025/11/20251113-3/ and https://www.hkma.gov.hk/media/eng/doc/key-information/press-release/2025/20251113e3a1.pdf

## Open items

- The sources reviewed contain no dedicated HKMA framework for issuing tokenised deposits. For now, the anchors are the February 2024 circular and the LM-1 liquidity treatment. [S:b2719f3dcb37, fn 1; S:69600121310a, Annex 3 para 4] A third anchor is the Supervisory Incubator, which has tokenised deposits as a core focus. [S:1b1a0de5de5a, para 2]
- The HKMA said it would soon publish an Ensemble Use Case Report and an Ensemble Taxonomy (a shared set of terms). Neither appears in the sources reviewed as of 25 Sep 2026. [S:3e5e256be485, Project Ensemble passage and 'The Road Ahead' section]
- The findings of the phase-2 legal review are not yet published. That review covers electronic signing, and holding and transferring tokenised instruments. [S:279f10054c6e, 'Next phase']

## Related modules

[C6](#m-C6), [C7](#m-C7), [D1](#m-D1), [D2](#m-D2)


**Business angle:** [Digital bonds: arranging and custody](#b-digital-bonds) and [Tokenised funds and money market fund settlement](#b-tokenised-funds) in the Business tab.

title: Financing, shared order books and client withdrawals
md:
For a bank's Head of Compliance (digital assets) whose bank is a registered institution (RI). An RI is a bank registered with the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) to do securities business. This module suits RIs that offer, or plan to offer, virtual asset (VA) dealing. VA dealing means buying and selling virtual assets (VAs), such as bitcoin, for clients. The module explains what the SFC changed in February 2026. It shows how the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) applied the change to banks in May 2026. It also sets out which controls the regulators expect.

## In 60 seconds

An omnibus account holds many clients' assets together in one account at a trading platform. SFC-licensed firms are called licensed corporations (LCs). Under the omnibus-account terms and conditions, LCs and RIs that dealt in VAs for clients could not lend clients money to buy VAs. [S:e64b7b0267b2, Background, p.1] On 11 February 2026 the SFC changed this for VA brokers that already offer securities margin financing. Margin financing means lending clients money to buy assets, secured on their holdings. Those brokers can now lend to their securities margin clients to buy VAs. [S:73dac3a5a832, paras 3, 5] If a broker relies on VA collateral, the SFC expects only bitcoin and ether to count. [S:73dac3a5a832, para 7] The broker should apply a haircut (a cut to the value it counts) of 60% or more. [S:73dac3a5a832, para 7] On 27 May 2026 the HKMA let RIs offer VA financing if they observe similar standards. [S:e64b7b0267b2, p.2] The HKMA also accepts stablecoins from HKMA-licensed issuers as collateral. [S:e64b7b0267b2, items (4), (9)] It says loans secured only by VA must be treated as clean (unsecured) loans when the bank works out its capital. [S:e64b7b0267b2, items (4), (9)] The same circulars let brokers and RIs trade for clients on a shared order book. A shared order book lets a virtual asset trading platform (VATP) pool its orders with affiliated platforms abroad. [S:73dac3a5a832, paras 15-17]; [S:e64b7b0267b2, p.6] Retail clients get access only after a clear risk explanation and after they expressly opt in. [S:73dac3a5a832, paras 15-17]; [S:e64b7b0267b2, p.6] The circulars also set anti-fraud standards for firms that let clients withdraw VAs. [S:73dac3a5a832, paras 18-20] The SFC circular is addressed to LCs. [S:73dac3a5a832, para 1] The HKMA applies the standards to RIs. [S:e64b7b0267b2, pp.2, 6]

## Status board

As of 25 September 2026.

| Instrument | Issuer | Date | Status (chip) | Applies to | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Circular on shared liquidity by virtual asset trading platforms (VATPs) (25EC56), plus the Shared Order Book terms and conditions | SFC | 3 November 2025 | In force | SFC-licensed VATPs (they need written SFC approval first) | [S:f009f1a6d615, paras 3, 26]; [S:fda3c03f239d, para 3] |
| Circular on VA brokers: financing, shared order book, client VA withdrawals (26EC5) | SFC | 11 February 2026 | In force | LCs that deal in VA through omnibus accounts | [S:73dac3a5a832, para 1] |
| Circular letting VATPs accept affiliated market makers (26EC6) | SFC | 11 February 2026 | In force | SFC-licensed VATPs | [S:84b3c1a0cee1, paras 7, 9] |
| Guidance on offering of financing for VA dealing, shared order book and client VA withdrawals | HKMA | 27 May 2026 | In force | All RIs; the financing part covers RIs that provide VA dealing | [S:e64b7b0267b2, pp.1-2] |
| Circular on VA-related activities involving relevant stablecoins (with revised terms and conditions, Appendices A1 and A2) | HKMA (written jointly with the SFC) | 27 May 2026 | In force | RIs | [S:553c7d718bec, landing page]; [S:a0bd48559762, p.1] |
| SFC consultation on capital requirements for VA activities, including VA financing | SFC | not dated | Stated target ('in due course') | LCs | [S:73dac3a5a832, para 14] |

## Key facts

- Before the SFC's circular of 11 February 2026, LCs and RIs could not give clients credit to buy VA. [S:e64b7b0267b2, Background, p.1] The omnibus-account terms and conditions set this ban. [S:e64b7b0267b2, Background, p.1]
- The revised terms of 27 May 2026 keep the ban, with one exception. [S:31b4f67e0233, Part I para 4.3, p.10] A licensed corporation or RI may give such financing only if it does securities margin financing. [S:31b4f67e0233, Part I para 4.3, p.10] It also needs a Type 1 licence or registration (dealing in securities) with these terms attached as conditions. [S:31b4f67e0233, Part I para 4.3, p.10]
- The SFC calls VA financing a first step under Pillar P (Product) of ASPIRe — the SFC's roadmap for the VA market. [S:73dac3a5a832, paras 3-5] Only VA brokers that already provide securities margin financing can offer it. [S:73dac3a5a832, paras 3-5]
- The HKMA allows RIs that provide VA dealing to offer VA financing if they observe standards similar to the SFC's. [S:e64b7b0267b2, 'HKMA's guidance for RIs', p.2] The HKMA lists the standards for RIs as items (1)-(9). [S:e64b7b0267b2, 'HKMA's guidance for RIs', p.2]
- Only the RI's securities margin financing clients can borrow. [S:e64b7b0267b2, items (2)-(3), p.2] The HKMA does not expect an RI to raise a client's credit limit just because VA financing is available. [S:e64b7b0267b2, items (2)-(3), p.2]
- An RI may take a client's VA holdings into account when it judges the client's financial capability. If it does, its assessment should cover seven risk factors. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (3)(a)-(g), p.3] These include price-gap risk (sudden jumps in price), too much exposure to the digital-asset sector, and shares and digital assets falling together in a crisis. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (3)(a)-(g), p.3]
- An RI can choose to rely on VA collateral. If it does, only bitcoin, ether and stablecoins from HKMA-licensed issuers ('Relevant Stablecoins') should count as eligible collateral, with a prudent haircut. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (4), pp.3-4]
- The haircut for bitcoin and ether should be 60% or more. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (4) and footnote 5, p.4] The HKMA may revise the haircut after giving advance notice. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (4) and footnote 5, p.4] The HKMA sets no numeric haircut for Relevant Stablecoins. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (4) and footnote 5, p.4]
- The HKMA generally expects an RI to value VA collateral at prices on the VATP where the client's orders are carried out. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (6) and footnote 6, p.4] For Relevant Stablecoins, the RI may use the licensed issuer's prices instead. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (6) and footnote 6, p.4] RIs should keep a contingency plan for when the VATP goes down. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (6) and footnote 6, p.4]
- VA financing counts as part of the client's margin loan. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (7)(a)-(c), pp.4-5] Concentration controls (limits on holding too much of one kind of collateral) should cover VA collateral too. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (7)(a)-(c), pp.4-5] The RI should not repledge (pledge again to someone else) or reuse VA collateral. The only exception is enforcing it when a client defaults. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (7)(a)-(c), pp.4-5]
- Two cases call for action. One is when the loan is larger than the collateral value. The other is when a client has an unpaid margin call and a poor record of meeting margin calls. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (8), p.5] In either case the RI should stop new advances, stop VA purchases on margin, and review the client's credit and trading limits. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (8), p.5]
- The Banking (Capital) Rules do not recognise VA as collateral. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (9), p.5] So loans secured solely by VA must be treated as clean loans to the client. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (9), p.5]
- Until the SFC revises capital requirements, LCs follow the Securities and Futures (Financial Resources) Rules (FRR). [S:73dac3a5a832, para 14] The FRR apply a 100% haircut to VA collateral that LCs hold. In effect, that collateral counts for nothing in the capital sums. [S:73dac3a5a832, para 14]
- The HKMA circular does not cover tokenised products, because the financing ban does not apply to buying them. [S:e64b7b0267b2, footnote 4, p.2] For selling and distributing tokenised products, RIs should refer to HKMA guidance. One example is its circular of 20 February 2024 on tokenised products. [S:e64b7b0267b2, footnote 4, p.2]
- A shared order book lets an SFC-licensed VATP combine its order book (its list of buy and sell orders) with those of affiliated platforms abroad. [S:f009f1a6d615, paras 1, 3, 7] The overseas platform should be in a member jurisdiction of the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) or of a FATF-style regional body. [S:f009f1a6d615, paras 1, 3, 7] Its regulation should be substantially aligned with international standards. [S:f009f1a6d615, paras 1, 3, 7]
- A shared order book should accept only fully pre-funded orders, where the client has the cash or assets before trading. [S:f009f1a6d615, paras 10, 13, 15, 17] Delivery-versus-payment is central to settlement: both sides' assets change hands at the same time. [S:f009f1a6d615, paras 10, 13, 15, 17] The VATP is required to hold a client-compensation reserve on trust in Hong Kong. The reserve must be no smaller than the Unsettled Trade Limit (a set cap on trades not yet settled). [S:f009f1a6d615, paras 10, 13, 15, 17]
- Some RIs trade for clients (as their agent) on a shared order book and also give retail clients access to it. Such RIs should follow SFC circular 26EC5, paras 15-17. [S:e64b7b0267b2, 'Shared Order Book', p.6] Before trading, a broker should assess these points: [S:73dac3a5a832, paras 16-17]
  - conflicts of interest
  - settlement
  - default handling
  - reserve funds and insurance
  - client recourse (how clients can claim if something goes wrong).

  Retail access needs a prominent risk explanation and the client's express choice to take part. [S:73dac3a5a832, paras 16-17]
- Client VAs sometimes stay in custody (safekeeping) at the VATP. In that case, a broker's withdrawal function adds cyber and operational risk. [S:73dac3a5a832, para 19] If a broker's system is hacked, an impostor could send fake withdrawal instructions. [S:73dac3a5a832, para 19]
- SFC 26EC5 paras 18-20 also apply to RIs that let clients withdraw VAs. [S:e64b7b0267b2, 'Client VA withdrawals', p.6] They apply on top of HKMA requirements, such as those on e-banking and technology risk management. [S:e64b7b0267b2, 'Client VA withdrawals', p.6] The paragraphs expect: [S:73dac3a5a832, para 20]
  - robust authentication (checking who gives an instruction)
  - continuous monitoring
  - the power to suspend withdrawals inside and outside office hours
  - working with VATPs on withdrawal limits.
- SFC circular 26EC6 lets a VATP accept an affiliated market maker, subject to conditions. A market maker is a firm that keeps quoting prices to buy and sell. [S:84b3c1a0cee1, paras 7, 9-10] The conditions include: [S:84b3c1a0cee1, paras 7, 9-10]
  - the market maker works independently of the platform
  - client orders at the same price go first
  - the market maker's trades are identified after execution
  - disclosure.

  The VATP must notify the SFC first, with a report from an independent firm. [S:84b3c1a0cee1, paras 7, 9-10]

## What your bank must do

**Obligations**
- Offer VA financing only to securities margin financing clients. [S:e64b7b0267b2, items (1)-(2), p.2] Base it on the client's financial capability and the collateral the client posts. [S:e64b7b0267b2, items (1)-(2), p.2]
- Treat loans secured solely by VA as clean (unsecured) loans for capital. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (9), p.5]
- Do not repledge, reuse or pledge VA collateral as security for anything else. The only exception is enforcing it when a client defaults. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (7)(c), p.5]

**Controls & monitoring**
- If relying on VA collateral, write down in the margin lending policy how the bank assesses VA risks. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (5)(a), p.4] Monitor vulnerable VA exposures on an ongoing basis. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (5)(a), p.4]
- If relying on VA collateral, keep the ability to watch its price swings in real time and act promptly. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (5)(b), p.4]
- Set prudent triggers for margin calls and for stopping new advances. Act on them. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (8), p.5]
- Monitor withdrawals continuously. Be able to escalate and suspend withdrawals outside office hours too. [S:e64b7b0267b2, p.6]; [S:73dac3a5a832, para 20(b)]

**Notify / consult HKMA or SFC**
- The HKMA circular sets no separate notification step. For new digital-asset activity, the HKMA's existing expectation is that banks discuss plans with it before launch. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body para 5, p.2]
- The circular names contacts for queries, by topic. [S:e64b7b0267b2, p.6]

**Counterparty due diligence**
- Before trading on a shared order book, assess these points about the platform operators: [S:e64b7b0267b2, p.6]; [S:73dac3a5a832, para 16]
  - conflicts of interest
  - the settlement mechanism
  - failure and default processes
  - reserve fund and insurance
  - client recourse.
- Work with the partner VATP as needed on withdrawal limits and on blocking suspicious withdrawals. [S:e64b7b0267b2, p.6]; [S:73dac3a5a832, para 20(c)]
- Keep a contingency plan for outages at the VATP whose prices the bank uses to value collateral. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (6), p.4]

## Talking points

**To the Chief Compliance Officer (CCO)**
- Under the HKMA's circular of 27 May 2026, our bank, as an RI, can offer VA margin financing. The condition is that we observe standards similar to the SFC's. [S:e64b7b0267b2, items (1)-(4), pp.2-4] If we rely on VA collateral, it should be only bitcoin, ether or stablecoins from HKMA-licensed issuers. [S:e64b7b0267b2, items (1)-(4), pp.2-4]
- The withdrawal and shared-order-book standards come from SFC circular 26EC5, paras 15-20. The HKMA applies them to RIs. [S:e64b7b0267b2, p.6]

**To business heads**
- Only securities margin financing clients qualify. Their limits are not expected to rise just because VA financing exists. [S:e64b7b0267b2, items (2)-(3), p.2]
- Retail clients can use a shared order book only after a prominent explanation of the overseas risks and their express opt-in. [S:e64b7b0267b2, p.6]; [S:73dac3a5a832, para 17]

**To the Chief Executive Officer (CEO)**
- The SFC calls this a first step to bring margin trading into VA. The aim is more liquidity in a risk-controlled setting. [S:73dac3a5a832, para 3]
- The Banking (Capital) Rules give VA collateral no recognition. So loans secured solely by VA are treated as clean loans. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (9), p.5]

**To Risk / Chief Risk Officer (CRO)**
- Bitcoin and ether collateral should get a haircut of 60% or more. For stablecoins, the HKMA asks only for a prudent haircut. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (4), footnote 5, pp.3-4]
- The HKMA notes that VAs have a short track record in major market-wide shocks. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (3), closing paragraph, p.3] Even the most traded VA has fallen sharply within a day and over several days. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (3), closing paragraph, p.3]

## Common mix-ups

- **Myth:** The SFC circular binds banks directly. **Fact:** It is addressed to LCs. [S:73dac3a5a832, para 1] The HKMA's circular of 27 May 2026 brings in banks, as RIs. [S:e64b7b0267b2, p.2]
- **Myth:** Bank collateral rules are the same as the SFC's. **Fact:** The HKMA adds Relevant Stablecoins as eligible collateral. [S:e64b7b0267b2, items (4), (9)] Banks treat VA-only loans as clean loans under the Banking (Capital) Rules. [S:e64b7b0267b2, items (4), (9)] LCs instead apply the FRR 100% haircut. [S:73dac3a5a832, paras 7, 14]
- **Myth:** The financing ban covered tokenised products. **Fact:** The HKMA says the ban does not apply to buying tokenised products. [S:e64b7b0267b2, footnote 4, p.2]
- **Myth:** A shared order book can link to any overseas exchange. **Fact:** As a first step, it is limited to platforms in the same group. [S:f009f1a6d615, para 3]

## Read these first

1. **Guidance on Offering of Financing for VA Dealing, Shared Order Book, and Client VA Withdrawals**, HKMA, 27 May 2026. Read all six pages, especially items (1)-(9) and page 6. This is the text addressed to RIs. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20260527-1-EN/20260527-1-EN.pdf
2. **Circular on licensed corporations providing VA dealing services (26EC5)**, SFC, 11 February 2026. Read paras 4-11, which the HKMA restates. Read paras 15-20, which the HKMA applies to RIs. https://apps.sfc.hk/edistributionWeb/api/circular/openFile?lang=EN&refNo=26EC5
3. **Circular on shared liquidity by VATPs (25EC56)**, SFC, 3 November 2025. Read paras 3-18 and 25-26 to understand the partner platform's settlement risk. https://apps.sfc.hk/edistributionWeb/api/circular/openFile?lang=EN&refNo=25EC56

## Open items

- Paragraph numbers differ. SFC 26EC5 cites the financing ban as para 4.4 of the omnibus terms and conditions. [S:73dac3a5a832, para 2] The HKMA cites para 4.3 'as renumbered on 30 September 2025'. [S:e64b7b0267b2, p.1 footnote 3] The revised terms of 27 May 2026 also number it 4.3. [S:31b4f67e0233, Part I para 4.3, p.10]
- Dates differ. The HKMA's footnote 4 dates the joint circular 23 December 2023. [S:e64b7b0267b2, footnote 4] The SFC's version gives 22 December 2023. [S:8a016a912528, p.1] So does the HKMA's own stablecoin circular of 27 May 2026. [S:a0bd48559762, p.1]
- The SFC has not published a date for its consultation on capital requirements for VA activities. [S:73dac3a5a832, para 14]
- The revised terms and conditions are Appendices A1 and A2 to the HKMA's stablecoin circular of 27 May 2026. [S:553c7d718bec, landing page] This module reviewed only para 4.3 of Appendix A1. [S:553c7d718bec, landing page]
- The HKMA specifies no numeric haircut for Relevant Stablecoin collateral. [S:e64b7b0267b2, item (4) and footnote 5, p.4]

## Related modules

[C5](#m-C5), [C7](#m-C7), [D1](#m-D1), [D2](#m-D2)


**Business angle:** [Virtual-asset dealing](#b-va-dealing) and [Virtual-asset financing and margin](#b-va-financing) in the Business tab.

title: VATP counterparties and the SFC platform regime
md:
VATP stands for virtual asset trading platform. SFC stands for the Securities and Futures Commission. This module is for the bank's Head of Compliance (digital assets). After it, you can explain how the SFC licenses these platforms and what its rulebook requires of them. You can also use that rulebook to check a platform that is your bank's partner, customer or counterparty.

## In 60 seconds

Since 1 June 2023, a platform needs an SFC licence to run a virtual asset (VA) exchange in Hong Kong. [S:2e5c35b38cc3, para 1] A VA is a digital token, such as a cryptocurrency. The same applies to a platform that actively markets such an exchange to Hong Kong investors. [S:2e5c35b38cc3, para 1] The licence comes under the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (AMLO), a Hong Kong law. [S:2e5c35b38cc3, para 1] Before that date, licensing was opt-in. The SFC could only license platforms that offered at least one security token (a token that counts as a security). [S:024089b01825, paras 4, 32] The SFC's Guidelines for VATP Operators (the Guidelines) are the platforms' rulebook. They cover which tokens a platform lists and which tokens retail clients can buy. They also cover 98% cold storage (keys kept offline), compensation cover and key bans. The Guidelines apply to platform operators, not to banks. [S:f1bbafccd556, paras 1.2, 7.1, 7.8, 10.6(c), 10.22] But the SFC and the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) require banks and other intermediaries to partner only with SFC-licensed platforms for VA dealing. [S:8a016a912528, para 17] So the Guidelines become your benchmark for due diligence (the checks you run on a partner). [S:8a016a912528, para 17] Since November 2025, the SFC has widened what licensed platforms may do. [S:e9cab4f52431, para 3; S:f009f1a6d615, para 3] In May 2026, the HKMA told registered institutions (RIs) which of these SFC standards it expects them to follow. [S:e64b7b0267b2, pp.1, 6] RIs are banks registered with the SFC to carry on securities business.

## Status board

As of 25 September 2026.

| Instrument | Issuer | Date | Status (chip) | Applies to | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Position paper: opt-in regulation of VA trading platforms | SFC | 6 Nov 2019 | Superseded | Platforms listing a security token | [S:024089b01825, paras 32, 82] |
| AMLO licensing regime for VA trading platforms | AMLO (statute); SFC licenses | 1 Jun 2023 | In force | All VA trading platforms in or marketing to Hong Kong | [S:2e5c35b38cc3, para 1] |
| Guidelines for VATP Operators | SFC | Jun 2023 | In force | Licensed platforms; bank uses as benchmark | [S:f1bbafccd556, para 1.2] |
| Lists of VA trading platforms (licensed, applicants, removed, closing down) | SFC | live; update 29 May 2026 | In force | Public; counterparty checks | [S:b14be2203d39, Licensed platforms table] |
| Inspection findings on applicants treated as licensed (circular 25EC3) | SFC | 16 Jan 2025 | In force | Platform operators and applicants | [S:0c93d9a066e6, p.1] |
| Custody circular for licensed platforms | SFC | 15 Aug 2025 | In force | Licensed platforms | [S:562c0f8addce, 'Way forward', p.7] |
| More products and services; shared liquidity | SFC | 3 Nov 2025 | In force | Licensed platforms | [S:e9cab4f52431, para 5]; [S:f009f1a6d615, para 26] |
| Affiliated market makers (AFMM) | SFC | 11 Feb 2026 | In force | Licensed platforms | [S:84b3c1a0cee1, paras 7, 9] |
| High-level framework for perpetual contracts | SFC | 11 Feb 2026 | Issued (initial framework; SFC invites proposals) | Licensed platforms; professional investors only | [S:49f642bdee28, 'Eligible investors' and 'Way forward' sections] |
| HKMA guidance to RIs on VA financing, shared order book and VA withdrawals | HKMA | 27 May 2026 | In force | RIs (banks) | [S:e64b7b0267b2, pp.1-2, 6] |
| Circular on phishing-resistant login | SFC | 9 Jul 2026 | Issued; phishing-resistant authentication due by 8 Jul 2027 | Internet brokers and SFC-licensed virtual asset service providers (VASPs) | [S:724f4d9f786e, paras 1, 21] |

## Key facts

- In 2018, the SFC chose to watch selected platforms in its Regulatory Sandbox (a supervised test setting). [S:e7f89463ceae, Section II] The SFC would then decide whether to license any of them. [S:e7f89463ceae, Section II]
- Under its 2019 position paper, the SFC could only license a centralised Hong Kong platform. [S:024089b01825, paras 4, 32] Centralised means the platform trades, clears and settles for clients and controls their assets. That platform also had to trade at least one security token. [S:024089b01825, paras 4, 32] Platforms that traded only non-security tokens were outside the SFC's powers. [S:024089b01825, paras 4, 32]
- The SFC granted the first VATP licence in December 2020. [S:60682e9fd7fa, main text and Note 1] The licence covered Type 1 (dealing in securities) and Type 7 (automated trading services) regulated activities. [S:60682e9fd7fa, main text and Note 1] The platform could serve professional investors only. [S:60682e9fd7fa, main text and Note 1]
- The AMLO licensing regime started on 1 June 2023. [S:2e5c35b38cc3, para 1] The AMLO requires every platform that runs a VA exchange in Hong Kong to hold an SFC licence. [S:2e5c35b38cc3, para 1] This also covers platforms that actively market a VA exchange to Hong Kong investors. [S:2e5c35b38cc3, para 1]
- Platforms already operating before the regime could carry on until 31 May 2024. [S:2e5c35b38cc3, paras 6, 12] A platform that applied by 29 February 2024 and met set conditions could be treated as licensed from 1 June 2024. [S:2e5c35b38cc3, paras 6, 12] This let existing platforms keep operating while they waited for a licence decision. [S:2e5c35b38cc3, paras 6, 12]
- Being treated as licensed is not the same as holding a licence. [S:c787f990209d, 'Reminder for investors' and 'Reminder for deemed-to-be-licensed VATP applicants'] The SFC warns investors that such platforms are not formally licensed. [S:c787f990209d, 'Reminder for investors' and 'Reminder for deemed-to-be-licensed VATP applicants'] The SFC does not expect them to take on new retail clients until they prove their controls work and are formally licensed. [S:c787f990209d, 'Reminder for investors' and 'Reminder for deemed-to-be-licensed VATP applicants']
- The SFC publishes lists of licensed platforms and of applicants. [S:b14be2203d39, Licensed platforms table and note] It also lists removed applicants and platforms that are closing down. [S:b14be2203d39, Licensed platforms table and note] At 29 May 2026, the licensed list showed 13 platforms. [S:b14be2203d39, Licensed platforms table and note] Being on a list does not mean a platform is creditworthy. [S:b14be2203d39, Licensed platforms table and note]
- Token admission: a platform should have a token admission and review committee. [S:f1bbafccd556, paras 7.1, 7.6] The platform should also do documented due diligence before listing any token. [S:f1bbafccd556, paras 7.1, 7.6]
- Retail access: a token offered to retail clients should be highly liquid (easy to buy and sell). [S:f1bbafccd556, paras 7.7-7.8] At a minimum, it should be in at least two acceptable indices from at least two different index providers. [S:f1bbafccd556, paras 7.7-7.8]
- Custody: a platform and its Associated Entity (the group company that holds client assets) should keep 98% of client virtual assets in cold storage. [S:f1bbafccd556, paras 10.6(c), 10.22] They should also hold an SFC-approved compensation arrangement (cover that pays clients if assets are lost). [S:f1bbafccd556, paras 10.6(c), 10.22] That cover is 50% of client virtual assets in cold storage. [S:f1bbafccd556, paras 10.6(c), 10.22] It is 100% of those in hot storage (keys kept online) and other storage. [S:f1bbafccd556, paras 10.6(c), 10.22]
- Prohibitions: outside narrow exceptions, the June 2023 Guidelines say platforms should not do six things. [S:f1bbafccd556, paras 7.23-7.26, 13.2-13.4] Three are lending clients money to buy virtual assets, dealing in VA futures or derivatives, and offering clients algorithmic (computer-run) trading. [S:f1bbafccd556, paras 7.23-7.26, 13.2-13.4] The other three are earning returns on client virtual assets, trading for their own account, and market making (quoting prices) with their own money. [S:f1bbafccd556, paras 7.23-7.26, 13.2-13.4] Two later SFC documents open limited routes. [S:49f642bdee28, 'Background'; S:84b3c1a0cee1, paras 4, 7] The February 2026 perpetuals framework invites platforms to propose perpetual contracts (futures-style contracts with no end date). [S:49f642bdee28, 'Background'] A February 2026 circular lets a company in the platform's group make markets on the platform, under conditions. [S:84b3c1a0cee1, paras 4, 7]
- The SFC inspected all applicants treated as licensed. [S:0c93d9a066e6, p.1] It checked three areas: cybersecurity, the safety of client assets, and know-your-client (KYC) checks on client identity. [S:0c93d9a066e6, p.1] The SFC then told every platform operator to review its systems and fix gaps at once. [S:0c93d9a066e6, p.1]
- In November 2025, the SFC dropped the 12-month track record rule for some tokens. [S:e9cab4f52431, para 5] Under that rule, a token needed a 12-month history before a platform offered it. [S:e9cab4f52431, para 5] The rule no longer covers tokens offered to professional investors. [S:e9cab4f52431, para 5] Nor does it cover stablecoins (tokens meant to hold a steady value) from licensed issuers offered to retail clients. [S:e9cab4f52431, para 5] It still applies to other tokens offered to retail clients. [S:e9cab4f52431, para 5]
- Shared liquidity: licensed platforms may share an order book (the list of waiting buy and sell orders) with affiliated overseas platforms. [S:f009f1a6d615, paras 1, 3, 26] They need prior written SFC approval. [S:f009f1a6d615, paras 1, 3, 26] The first step allows only liquidity from within the same group. [S:f009f1a6d615, paras 1, 3, 26]
- Since February 2026, a platform may let an affiliated market maker (a group company that quotes buy and sell prices) trade on it. [S:84b3c1a0cee1, paras 7, 9] The platform first notifies the SFC and files a report from an independent firm. [S:84b3c1a0cee1, paras 7, 9] Client orders keep priority over the market maker's orders at the same price. [S:84b3c1a0cee1, paras 7, 9]
- The SFC's perpetual contracts framework says these products should go to professional investors only. [S:49f642bdee28, 'Eligible investors and reference assets' and 'Margin arrangements' sections] It says margin collateral (assets posted to back a trade) should take one of three forms. [S:49f642bdee28, 'Eligible investors and reference assets' and 'Margin arrangements' sections] These are fiat money (ordinary currency), or stablecoins or tokenised deposits (bank deposits recorded as tokens) regulated by the HKMA. [S:49f642bdee28, 'Eligible investors and reference assets' and 'Margin arrangements' sections]
- The SFC said JPEX (which presented itself as a VA trading platform) was unregulated. [S:c8dcca119dab, main text, paras 3, 5-6] The SFC said it put JPEX on its Alert List (a public warning list) in July 2022. [S:c8dcca119dab, main text, paras 3, 5-6] It said JPEX never applied for a licence. [S:c8dcca119dab, main text, paras 3, 5-6] The SFC referred the matter to the Police on suspicion of fraud. [S:c8dcca119dab, main text, paras 3, 5-6]
- The SFC expects SFC-licensed VASPs to adopt phishing-resistant login by 8 July 2027. [S:724f4d9f786e, paras 7, 21(c)] Phishing-resistant means fake websites cannot trick users into handing over login details. The same deadline covers device binding (tying an account to a trusted device). [S:724f4d9f786e, paras 7, 21(c)] The SFC does not treat a one-time password (OTP) as phishing-resistant. [S:724f4d9f786e, paras 7, 21(c)]

## What your bank must do

**Obligations**
- [ ] Partner only with SFC-licensed platforms if the bank offers VA dealing. [S:8a016a912528, para 17] Either introduce clients to the platform, or trade through an omnibus account (one account that pools many clients' orders). [S:8a016a912528, para 17]
- [ ] Offer VA dealing only to clients of the bank's Type 1 (dealing in securities) business. [S:8a016a912528, para 18]
- [ ] Follow the SFC's guidance for VA brokers if the bank trades for clients on a shared order book and also gives retail clients access to it. [S:e64b7b0267b2, 'Shared Order Book', p.6] The HKMA expects this of RIs. [S:e64b7b0267b2, 'Shared Order Book', p.6]
- [ ] Apply the SFC's safeguards for client VA withdrawals if the bank, as an RI, lets clients withdraw virtual assets. [S:e64b7b0267b2, 'Client VA withdrawals', p.6] These safeguards apply on top of the HKMA's e-banking and technology rules for RIs. [S:e64b7b0267b2, 'Client VA withdrawals', p.6]

**Controls & monitoring**
- [ ] Re-check a platform's status on the live SFC lists before onboarding it and at each review. The lists can lag between updates. [S:dddd919625e9, Note 1]; [S:b14be2203d39, applicant section Note 1]

**Notify / consult HKMA or SFC**
- [ ] Tell the SFC in advance before the bank starts or changes VA activities. [S:8a016a912528, para 31] Tell the HKMA too, where relevant. [S:8a016a912528, para 31]

**Counterparty due diligence**
- [ ] Run a risk-based anti-money laundering (AML) and counter-financing of terrorism (CFT) assessment when the bank takes VASPs as customers. [S:642680fa4467, section (b) 'Banking relationships with VASPs', p.4] The HKMA says extra checks may be needed, depending on the relationship. [S:642680fa4467, section (b) 'Banking relationships with VASPs', p.4] These are like the checks used in correspondent banking (where one bank provides accounts to another). [S:642680fa4467, section (b) 'Banking relationships with VASPs', p.4] They include understanding the customer's business, licensing status and AML/CFT controls. [S:642680fa4467, section (b) 'Banking relationships with VASPs', p.4]
- [ ] Find out, for VASPs based outside Hong Kong, whether each account is for the firm's own use or for its clients. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 11.23-11.24] If the account serves clients, apply the correspondent-banking measures. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 11.23-11.24]
- [ ] Benchmark a partner platform against the VATP Guidelines. [S:f1bbafccd556, paras 7.1, 7.8, 10.6(c), 10.22] Check its token committee and its retail index test. [S:f1bbafccd556, paras 7.1, 7.8, 10.6(c), 10.22] Check its 98% cold storage and its compensation cover. [S:f1bbafccd556, paras 7.1, 7.8, 10.6(c), 10.22]
- [ ] Ask whether the platform has fixed the gaps listed in the SFC's inspection findings. [S:0c93d9a066e6, p.1 and Appendix 2]

## Talking points

**To the chief compliance officer (CCO)**
- The VATP Guidelines bind platforms, not the bank. [S:f1bbafccd556, para 1.2] We use them as a due diligence benchmark, because our VA dealing must run through SFC-licensed platforms. [S:8a016a912528, para 17]
- For customers that are VASPs, we follow the HKMA's AML/CFT Guideline. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 11.23-11.24] That includes correspondent-banking-style checks on overseas VASPs. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 11.23-11.24]

**To business heads**
- Platforms can now share order books with SFC approval. [S:f009f1a6d615, para 26] They can also use affiliated market makers after notifying the SFC. [S:84b3c1a0cee1, para 9] The SFC's framework says perpetual contracts should go to professional investors only. [S:49f642bdee28, 'Eligible investors and reference assets']
- If we trade for clients on a platform's shared order book and give retail clients access to it, the HKMA expects us to follow the SFC's broker guidance. [S:e64b7b0267b2, 'Shared Order Book', p.6]

**To the CEO**
- From 2019 to 2020, Hong Kong platform licensing was opt-in and for professional investors only. [S:024089b01825, para 32]; [S:60682e9fd7fa, Note 1] Since June 2023, every platform in or marketing to Hong Kong has needed a licence. [S:2e5c35b38cc3, para 1]
- The SFC's licensed list showed 13 platforms at 29 May 2026. [S:b14be2203d39, Licensed platforms table]

**To Risk / chief risk officer (CRO)**
- The Guidelines say licensed platforms should keep 98% of client virtual assets in cold storage. [S:f1bbafccd556, paras 10.6(c), 10.22] Their compensation cover should equal 50% of cold-stored and 100% of hot-stored client assets. [S:f1bbafccd556, paras 10.6(c), 10.22]
- The SFC's inspections of applicants treated as licensed covered cybersecurity, client assets and KYC. [S:0c93d9a066e6, p.1] The SFC said platforms should fix gaps at once. [S:0c93d9a066e6, p.1]

## Common mix-ups

- **Myth:** A platform treated as licensed has been vetted.
  **Fact:** In 2023, the SFC said it had not vetted whether these platforms were fit and proper (suitable to hold a licence). [S:dddd919625e9, Note 4] The SFC also said they may never get a licence. [S:dddd919625e9, Note 4]
- **Myth:** The 50%/100% compensation rule applies to our custody.
  **Fact:** That rule is for licensed trading platforms. [S:f1bbafccd556, para 10.22] The HKMA's May 2026 custody guidance for banks takes a different approach. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(n)] It expects the bank to be liable for losses caused by the bank, and to hold enough financial resources. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(n)]
- **Myth:** A one-time password sent by text message (SMS) is enough.
  **Fact:** The SFC does not treat an OTP as phishing-resistant for login or device binding. [S:724f4d9f786e, para 7]

## Read these first

1. **Guidelines for Virtual Asset Trading Platform Operators** — SFC, June 2023. Read paragraphs 7.1-7.8 (token admission and the retail test). Also read 7.24-7.26, 10.6, 10.11, 10.22 and 13.2-13.4. Use this as your benchmark for any platform counterparty. https://www.sfc.hk/-/media/EN/assets/components/codes/files-current/web/guidelines/Guidelines-for-Virtual-Asset-Trading-Platform-Operators/Guidelines-for-Virtual-Asset-Trading-Platform-Operators.pdf
2. **Joint circular on intermediaries' VA-related activities** — SFC and HKMA, 22 December 2023. Read paragraphs 17-18 and 31. The circular explains why a bank's VA dealing must go through licensed platforms. https://apps.sfc.hk/edistributionWeb/api/circular/openFile?lang=EN&refNo=23EC66
3. **Lists of virtual asset trading platforms** — SFC, live page (29 May 2026 update reviewed). Read the licensed table and the notes on the applicant list. This page is the SFC's own record of each platform's status. https://www.sfc.hk/en/Welcome-to-the-Fintech-Contact-Point/Virtual-assets/Virtual-asset-trading-platforms-operators/Lists-of-virtual-asset-trading-platforms

## Open items

- The SFC calls its perpetuals framework an initial approach that may be refined. [S:49f642bdee28, 'Way forward'] The documents reviewed for this guide show no approvals of specific perpetual products. [S:49f642bdee28, 'Way forward']
- The SFC press release on the first licence is dated 16 December 2020. [S:60682e9fd7fa, dateline] The SFC's licensed list gives 15 December 2020 as the earliest platform's licence date. [S:b14be2203d39, Licensed platforms table] The documents reviewed do not explain the one-day gap.
- The SFC's VATP lists are a live page. The counts here are a snapshot from 29 May 2026.

## Related modules

[A1](#m-A1), [B1](#m-B1), [C1](#m-C1), [C2](#m-C2), [C5](#m-C5), [C6](#m-C6), [D1](#m-D1)


**Business angle:** [Banking the digital-asset industry](#b-banking-da-industry) and [Virtual-asset dealing](#b-va-dealing) in the Business tab.

title: Capital and prudential treatment of cryptoassets
md:
This module is for the bank's Head of Compliance (digital assets). After it, you can explain three things. First, how Hong Kong turned the global Basel standard on cryptoassets into binding rules on capital, liquidity and exposure limits. Second, how a cryptoasset gets sorted into a group. Third, what the bank must tell the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA).

## In 60 seconds

The Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) sets global standards for banks. It published a standard on banks' cryptoasset exposures in December 2022. It amended that standard in July 2024. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 1.1.1] The HKMA consulted on the standard in February 2024, in consultation paper (CP) 24.01. [S:27f8bc2f6b2a, paras 1-2] In January 2025, the HKMA sent draft rules to the banking industry associations. [S:ebc5f9b5ee0d, p.1] In July 2025, the government published three sets of amendment rules in the Gazette (the government's official record). [S:277820235891, para 1] These rules took effect on 1 January 2026. [S:277820235891, closing para] On the same date, the HKMA brought in a new guidance module, CRP-1 (Classification of Cryptoassets). It also revised nine modules of its Supervisory Policy Manual (SPM), the HKMA's set of guidance modules for banks. [S:30b686db29f9, pp.1-2] Every cryptoasset a bank is exposed to falls into one of four groups. [S:b7d630146e6c, paras 1.3.2-1.3.3, 2.1.8] Group 1a is tokenised traditional assets, such as bonds recorded as digital tokens. [S:b7d630146e6c, paras 1.3.2-1.3.3, 2.1.8] Group 1b is stablecoins (tokens built to hold a steady value) with an effective stabilisation mechanism. [S:b7d630146e6c, paras 1.3.2-1.3.3, 2.1.8] Group 2a is Group 2 assets that meet hedging criteria, so limited hedging (offsetting one position with another) is recognised. [S:b7d630146e6c, paras 1.3.2-1.3.3, 2.1.8] Group 2b is everything else, at a 1,250% risk weight. [S:9e8d84c87168, Part XII CAE1 explanatory note, column (c), pp.214-215] A risk weight scales how much capital a bank holds against an asset. At 1,250%, the bank in effect holds capital equal to the whole exposure. A bank must tell the HKMA before acquiring each new type of cryptoasset. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2] The asset stays in Group 2b until the HKMA agrees with the bank's assessment. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2] In June 2026, the HKMA clarified one Group 1 condition. It covers tokenised traditional assets on permissionless blockchains (open networks anyone can join). A bank can also meet that condition another way. [S:dca53ff0a62c, p.1]

## Status board

As of 25 September 2026.

| Instrument | Issuer | Date | Status (chip) | Applies to | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BCBS standard (December 2022) and amendments (July 2024) | BCBS, put into effect by the HKMA | December 2022; July 2024 | Implemented in Hong Kong rules | All authorized institutions (AIs: banks and deposit-taking companies authorized by the HKMA) from 1 January 2026 | [S:b7d630146e6c, paras 1.1.1-1.1.2] |
| CP 24.01 Cryptoasset Exposures | HKMA | 7 February 2024 | Superseded | AIs | [S:27f8bc2f6b2a, paras 2, 11] |
| Informal industry consultation ("soft consultation") on draft rule amendments | HKMA | 13 January 2025 | Closed (comments were due 20 February 2025; rules since published in the Gazette) | AIs, through the Hong Kong Association of Banks and The DTC Association (DTC = deposit-taking company) | [S:ebc5f9b5ee0d, pp.1-2] |
| Banking (Capital), (Disclosure) and (Exposure Limits) (Amendment) Rules 2025 | Government; laid before the Legislative Council | Published in the Gazette 11 July 2025 | In force (from 1 Jan 2026) | All AIs | [S:277820235891, paras 1-2 and closing para] |
| SPM CRP-1 plus nine revised modules and a code of practice | HKMA | Finalised 27 November 2025. Eight revised modules and the code published in the Gazette 19 December 2025 | In force (from 1 Jan 2026) | All AIs | [S:30b686db29f9, pp.1-2]; [S:54e0a69bd91f, pp.1-2] |
| CRP-1 para 2.6.4 clarification | HKMA | 3 June 2026 | In force | All AIs | [S:dca53ff0a62c, p.1] |
| Guidance for registered institutions (RIs) on virtual asset financing (clean-loan treatment, meaning unsecured). RIs are banks registered with the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) for securities business. | HKMA | 27 May 2026 | In force | RIs | [S:e64b7b0267b2, para (9), p.5] |
| Proposed Banking (Capital) Rules amendments | HKMA | 30 April 2026 | Consultation closed 1 Jun 2026; no final rules seen | AIs | [S:f6b5ade120fe, landing page]; [S:1e9b351e81e7, p.1] |

## Key facts

- CP 24.01 proposed bringing the December 2022 Basel standard into Hong Kong rules no earlier than 1 July 2025. Comments were due by 6 May 2024. [S:27f8bc2f6b2a, paras 2, 4, 11]
- In January 2025, the HKMA sent draft rule amendments to the industry. It asked for comments by 20 February 2025. It aimed for a 1 January 2026 start, in line with the Basel timetable. [S:ebc5f9b5ee0d, p.1]
- The government published the three amendment rules in the Gazette on 11 July 2025. They were due to be laid before the Legislative Council on 16 July 2025. They took effect on 1 January 2026. [S:277820235891, paras 1-2 and closing para]
- On 27 November 2025, the HKMA finalised CRP-1. It also finalised changes to nine other modules and a code of practice. All took effect on 1 January 2026. [S:30b686db29f9, pp.1-2]
- CRP-1 is guidance. The binding classification rules sit in Part 12 of the Banking (Capital) Rules (BCR). If the two differ, the BCR prevails. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 1.1.4]
- A cryptoasset reaches Group 1 only if it meets all four classification conditions. [S:b7d630146e6c, paras 2.2.1, 2.3.1, 2.4.1, 2.5.1] Condition 1: the token carries the same rights and risks as the traditional asset, or has an effective stabilisation mechanism. [S:b7d630146e6c, paras 2.2.1, 2.3.1, 2.4.1, 2.5.1] Condition 2: its rights are clearly defined and legally enforceable, and settlement is final. [S:b7d630146e6c, paras 2.2.1, 2.3.1, 2.4.1, 2.5.1] Condition 3: its network risks are sufficiently reduced and managed. [S:b7d630146e6c, paras 2.2.1, 2.3.1, 2.4.1, 2.5.1] Condition 4: the entities doing key functions are regulated and supervised, or follow suitable risk management standards. [S:b7d630146e6c, paras 2.2.1, 2.3.1, 2.4.1, 2.5.1]
- Group 1a is tokenised traditional assets. Group 1b is stablecoins with an effective stabilisation mechanism. Anything else is Group 2. [S:b7d630146e6c, paras 1.3.1-1.3.2]
- A Group 2 asset reaches Group 2a only if it meets three hedging criteria. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 3.1.1] One is an average market capitalisation (total market value) of at least HK$78 billion. Another is 100 or more real price observations. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 3.1.1]
- Group 2b exposures take a 1,250% risk weight. [S:9e8d84c87168, Part XII CAE1 explanatory note, column (c), pp.214-215] It also covers their credit valuation adjustment risk (the risk that a derivative loses value as the other party's credit weakens). [S:5d845665ba83, para 4.3.2]
- Before acquiring a new type of cryptoasset, a bank must notify the HKMA. The bank then treats the asset as Group 2b until the HKMA agrees with the bank's own classification. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2]
- Exposures held before 1 January 2026 must sit in Group 2b until the HKMA agrees the bank's assessment. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 1.4.2]
- If the HKMA disagrees with a bank's classification, the HKMA will override it. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.6]
- Stablecoins issued under the HKMA's licensing regime can be treated as meeting the extra safeguards for permissionless blockchains. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.6.3] Other stablecoins on those blockchains must be under a regime the HKMA considers comparable to the Stablecoins Ordinance. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.6.3]
- The June 2026 letter covers the approval condition for tokenised traditional assets on permissionless blockchains. [S:dca53ff0a62c, p.1] That condition calls for approval of the tokenised instrument by a financial market regulator. [S:dca53ff0a62c, p.1] A bank can also meet it where a financial market regulator supervises the tokenisation business. The letter took effect immediately. [S:dca53ff0a62c, p.1]
- CA-G-1 section 8.7 covers the banking book (positions a bank holds rather than trades). [S:5d0c13e09312, paras 8.7.1-8.7.2] Group 1a exposures there generally follow the rules for the underlying asset. [S:5d0c13e09312, paras 8.7.1-8.7.2] For Group 1b, the bank calculates capital separately for the reference asset and for the redeemer (the party that pays holders back). [S:5d0c13e09312, paras 8.7.1-8.7.2]
