- Group 2 exposure limit: this applies to a systemically important bank. That is a global or domestic bank whose failure could harm the wider system. [S:5d0c13e09312, para 8.7.4(d)] Such a bank faces a capital add-on (extra capital charge) if its Group 2 exposure exceeds 1% of Tier 1 capital. [S:5d0c13e09312, para 8.7.4(d)] Tier 1 capital is a bank's core capital, such as ordinary shares and retained earnings. Above 2%, a different and heavier treatment applies. [S:9e8d84c87168, Part XII CAE1 explanatory note, rows 8-10, p.215]
- LM-1 Annex 3 covers liquidity. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3 paras 1, 7] High-quality liquid assets (HQLA) are assets a bank can turn into cash quickly in a crisis. The liquidity coverage ratio (LCR) checks that a bank holds enough HQLA to cover 30 days of stressed cash outflows. A category 1 institution is a bank the HKMA has designated to follow the LCR. Such an institution may count a cryptoasset as HQLA only if it passes two tests. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3 paras 1, 7] It is a Group 1a token of an asset class that qualifies as HQLA, and it meets the HQLA requirements. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3 paras 1, 7] The issuer of a stablecoin that holders can redeem within the LCR period must generally apply a 100% outflow. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3 paras 1, 7] In other words, it assumes all such stablecoins are paid out.
- Market risk rules change in three ways. [S:b8d2d2a0f9c8, footnote 80, paras 6.1.9, 6.2.8] Any cryptoasset exposure removes the small-amount exception from market risk capital rules. [S:b8d2d2a0f9c8, footnote 80, paras 6.1.9, 6.2.8] The internal models approach (a bank's own approved risk models) cannot be used for instruments referencing Group 2 cryptoassets. [S:b8d2d2a0f9c8, footnote 80, paras 6.1.9, 6.2.8] For Group 2a, position risk (capital for price risk on a holding) is 100% of the net position. [S:b8d2d2a0f9c8, footnote 80, paras 6.1.9, 6.2.8]
- CR-G-8 values crypto exposures under new Division 5A of the Banking (Exposure Limits) Rules. [S:0cd3c1a74e5e, paras 2.8.8-2.8.9 and footnote 13] Some exposures are not linked to a counterparty's credit or default risk. The bank leaves those out when measuring large exposures (big concentrations of risk) to that counterparty or its group. [S:0cd3c1a74e5e, paras 2.8.8-2.8.9 and footnote 13]
- CR-L-5 covers the rules on HKMA consent for major acquisitions. Under it, a token that carries the economics of equity (the returns and risks of owning shares) counts as share capital. [S:13365a31e794, footnote 1]
- CA-G-5 says the HKMA may respond to crypto-related weaknesses in several ways. These include capital add-ons, provisions (money set aside for losses) and limits. [S:349a543ae2f0, para 3.6.6]

## What your bank must do

**Obligations**
- [ ] Classify every cryptoasset exposure under BCR Part 12 and CRP-1. Keep reassessing it on an ongoing basis. [S:b7d630146e6c, paras 1.1.4, 2.1.1]
- [ ] Move an asset to Group 2b at once if it stops meeting its conditions or criteria. This covers any asset the HKMA agreed as Group 1a, 1b or 2a. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.3]
- [ ] As a registered institution (RI), treat loans secured only by virtual asset collateral as clean (unsecured) loans for capital purposes. [S:e64b7b0267b2, para (9), p.5]

**Controls & monitoring**
- [ ] Keep policies, staff and technology systems able to assess cryptoasset risk. Document the evidence behind each classification. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.1]
- [ ] For stablecoins, keep a monitoring framework that checks the stabilisation mechanism works as intended. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.2.4]
- [ ] If the bank is systemically important, track its Group 2 exposure ratio. Compare it with the 1% and 2% thresholds used in disclosure. [S:9e8d84c87168, Part XII CAE1 explanatory note, rows 8-10, p.215]

**Notify / consult HKMA or SFC**
- [ ] Notify the HKMA before acquiring any new type of cryptoasset. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2]
- [ ] Give the HKMA classification evidence when it asks. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.1]

**Counterparty due diligence**
- [ ] For Group 1 assets, check each entity with a key role. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.5.1] These roles are redemption, transfer, storage or settlement of the asset, and management of its reserves. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.5.1] Confirm each entity is regulated and supervised, or meets suitable risk standards. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.5.1] Confirm it also discloses a governance framework (its rules for oversight and decisions). [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.5.1]

## Talking points

**To the CCO**
- The capital rules are law from 1 January 2026. CRP-1 is guidance, and the BCR wins if they differ. [S:b7d630146e6c, paras 1.1.4, 1.4.1]
- We need to tell the HKMA before we acquire any new type of cryptoasset. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2]

**To business heads**
- A new cryptoasset sits in Group 2b until the HKMA agrees its classification. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2] That means a 1,250% risk weight, so capital equal to the whole exposure. [S:9e8d84c87168, Part XII CAE1 explanatory note, column (c), pp.214-215]
- Stablecoins under the HKMA licensing regime can be treated as meeting the permissionless-blockchain safeguards. The four classification conditions still apply. [S:b7d630146e6c, paras 1.3.1, 2.6.3]

**To the CEO**
- Hong Kong's rules started on 1 January 2026, matching the Basel timetable. [S:277820235891, closing para]
- The HKMA can override our classifications. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.6] It can also add capital or limits if it sees weaknesses. [S:349a543ae2f0, para 3.6.6]

**To Risk / CRO**
- Any crypto exposure ends our small-amount exception from the market risk capital rules. [S:b8d2d2a0f9c8, footnote 80]
- For a category 1 institution, a stablecoin it holds is generally not HQLA. It counts as a 0% inflow under the LCR. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3 para 7] The net stable funding ratio tests that long-term assets have stable funding. Under it, the stablecoin has an 85% required stable funding factor. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3 para 7]

## Common mix-ups

- **Myth:** The June 2026 CRP-1 letter tightened the rules. **Fact:** The letter clarified the approval condition in para 2.6.4. A bank can also meet it where a financial market regulator supervises the tokenisation business. [S:dca53ff0a62c, p.1]
- **Myth:** Internal models are barred only for Group 2a. **Fact:** Market risk module MR-1 bars them for all instruments referencing Group 2 cryptoassets. [S:b8d2d2a0f9c8, para 6.1.9]
- **Myth:** The 1%/2% Group 2 limit applies to every bank. **Fact:** Only systemically important banks face the add-on. [S:5d0c13e09312, para 8.7.4(d)] The HKMA's instructions for its regulatory return (a report banks file) have all Hong Kong-incorporated AIs report the ratio. [S:d1fbf6c0736a, paras 11-12]
- **Myth:** Legacy holdings keep their old treatment. **Fact:** Holdings from before 1 January 2026 sit in Group 2b until the HKMA agrees the assessment. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 1.4.2]
- **Myth:** Central bank digital currencies are cryptoassets. **Fact:** They sit outside the standard. They are generally treated like the central bank's ordinary currency. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 1.2.3 and footnote 4]

## Read these first

1. **SPM CRP-1 Classification of Cryptoassets** — HKMA, version 1, in effect from 1 January 2026. Read paras 1.1.4, 1.4, 2.1, 2.6 and 3.1.1. It sets out how each cryptoasset is grouped. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20251125-15-EN/CRP-1.pdf
2. **SPM CRP-1: update on cryptoassets classification conditions** — HKMA, 3 June 2026. Read page 1. It adds another way to meet para 2.6.4. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20260603-1-EN/20260603-1-EN.pdf
3. **Cryptoassets standard: SPM modules, code of practice, disclosure templates and returns** — HKMA, 27 November 2025. Read pages 1-4. It lists every changed module and the move to the new reporting returns. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20251127-1-EN/20251127-1-EN.pdf

## Open items

- The April 2026 BCR proposals closed for comment on 1 June 2026. [S:f6b5ade120fe, landing page] One of these proposals is to remove cryptoassets from the Part 6 "cash item" definition. [S:1e9b351e81e7, Items 19, 45] Another is a set of new rules on hedging counterparty credit risk (the risk the other side of a deal defaults). [S:1e9b351e81e7, Items 19, 45] Those rules cover netting sets (groups of trades that can be offset) holding Group 2b cryptoasset derivatives. [S:1e9b351e81e7, Items 19, 45] The documents reviewed for this guide hold no final rules. [S:f6b5ade120fe, landing page]
- The June 2026 letter says CRP-1's wording will reflect the clarification in due course. The documents reviewed hold no updated CRP-1 text. [S:dca53ff0a62c, p.1]
- The documents reviewed for this guide do not include the Gazette text of Banking (Capital) Rules Part 12. Section references come from HKMA modules and templates.
- For two sets of HKMA letters, only catalogue pages were reviewed. One is the December 2022 letter passing on the BCBS standard. The others are the July and August 2025 letters on the Gazette publication.

## Related modules

[A1](#m-A1), [C7](#m-C7), [D2](#m-D2), [D3](#m-D3), [D4](#m-D4)

title: Regulatory reporting and disclosure
md:
For the bank's Head of Compliance (digital assets). After this module, you can name the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) reports that now carry cryptoasset data. You can say when each change applied. You can also say which banks could use the six-month transition.

## In 60 seconds

New amendment rules bring the Basel cryptoasset standard into Hong Kong law. The Basel standard is the global rule set for how banks treat cryptoassets. The new rules took effect on 1 January 2026. [S:277820235891, paras 1, 6]

For reporting, the HKMA changed seven returns. A return is a regular data report that a bank files with the HKMA. Each return got new or revised templates (the forms) and completion instructions (the guide to filling them in). [S:30b686db29f9, p.3; S:d1fbf6c0736a, para 1] The HKMA names its returns with codes such as MA(BS)3. The seven returns are:
- MA(BS)1E: liquidity (whether the bank has enough cash and easy-to-sell assets).
- MA(BS)1F: compliance certificate.
- MA(BS)3: capital. It has a new Part IIIf (a form for extra crypto risk-weighted amounts). A risk-weighted amount is an exposure scaled up or down for its risk. It drives how much capital the bank holds.
- MA(BS)3A: capital for market risk and credit valuation adjustment (CVA) risk. CVA risk is the risk of loss when a trading counterparty's credit quality worsens.
- MA(BS)26: stable funding.
- MA(BS)27: leverage (capital against total exposures, without risk weights).
- MA(BS)28: large exposures (big exposures to a single counterparty).

[S:30b686db29f9, p.3; S:d1fbf6c0736a, para 1]

Authorized institutions (AIs) are banks and other deposit-takers authorized by the HKMA. Some AIs had no cryptoasset exposure on 1 January 2026. The HKMA calls these 'Transition AIs'. They could keep using the old templates for four of the seven returns until 30 June 2026. [S:30b686db29f9, p.3]

For disclosure, Pillar 3 is the public report in which a bank publishes data on its capital and risks. A new Part XII (the crypto section) adds four items to the Pillar 3 package. [S:9e8d84c87168, Part XII, pp.210-218] They are:
- Table CAEA (a written description of crypto activities and risks).
- Template CAE1 (crypto exposures and risk-weighted amounts).
- Template CAE2 (accounting classification).
- Template CAE3 (liquidity).

[S:9e8d84c87168, Part XII, pp.210-218] These items apply to AIs with cryptoasset exposures. [S:9e8d84c87168, Part XII, pp.210-218] CAE1 needs extra rows for each material single holding. [S:9e8d84c87168, Part XII, pp.210-218]

The Supervisory Policy Manual (SPM) is the HKMA's book of supervisory guidance. SPM module CA-D-1 (the disclosure guideline) helps AIs understand the HKMA's approach to applying the Banking (Disclosure) Rules (BDR). [S:e10295e5fe20, para 2.1]

## Status board

As of 25 September 2026.

| Instrument | Issuer | Date | Status (chip) | Applies to | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Banking (Disclosure) (Amendment) Rules 2025 | Government / Legislative Council | Gazetted 11 July 2025. In effect 1 January 2026. | In force | All AIs | [S:277820235891, paras 1, 2, 6] |
| Consultation on return templates | HKMA | 13 June 2025 (closed 11 July 2025) | Closed; finalised 27 Nov 2025 | AIs | [S:64b1dc490633, landing page, Issue Date and Consultation Status]; [S:30b686db29f9, p.3] |
| Consultation on revised completion instructions | HKMA | 4 September 2025 (closed 3 October 2025) | Closed; finalised 27 Nov 2025 | AIs | [S:fc9efbf504f8, landing page, Issue Date and Consultation Status]; [S:30b686db29f9, p.3] |
| Final returns package and transition for Transition AIs | HKMA | 27 November 2025 | In force | All AIs. Transition AIs could use old templates until 30 June 2026. | [S:30b686db29f9, p.3-4] |
| Standard disclosure templates, new Part XII (CAEA, CAE1-CAE3) | HKMA | 27 November 2025 | In force | AIs with cryptoasset exposures | [S:9e8d84c87168, Part XII, pp.210-219]; [S:30b686db29f9, p.3] |
| SPM CA-D-1 (version 5) | HKMA | 1 January 2026 | In force | All AIs | [S:e10295e5fe20, para 12.2.4] |

Chip meanings: In force means it applies now. Closed means the consultation has ended. Gazetted means published in the official Government Gazette.

## Key facts

- The HKMA listed seven returns with new templates or instructions. [S:30b686db29f9, p.3, 'Banking returns' list (a)-(g)] The list covers MA(BS)1E, MA(BS)1F(a) and (b), MA(BS)3, 3A, 26, 27 and 28. [S:30b686db29f9, p.3, 'Banking returns' list (a)-(g)]
- The HKMA said the final templates would not differ materially from the consultation versions. The only exceptions were wording, formatting and changes agreed with the industry. [S:30b686db29f9, p.3]
- A Transition AI is an AI with no cryptoasset exposure on 1 January 2026. [S:30b686db29f9, p.3] It could keep filing four returns on the old templates until 30 June 2026. These are MA(BS)26, MA(BS)1E, MA(BS)3 and MA(BS)3A. [S:30b686db29f9, p.3]
- Even Transition AIs were expected to use some revised MA(BS)3 instructions from 1 January 2026. [S:30b686db29f9, p.3, footnote 4] These cover Part II (capital base) and paragraph 6 of Part I. They deal with other changes unrelated to crypto. [S:30b686db29f9, p.3, footnote 4]
- A bank with crypto exposure could agree a temporary alternative arrangement with the HKMA if its systems were not ready. [S:30b686db29f9, p.4] So could a Transition AI that later acquired crypto exposure. The arrangement covered positions from 31 January to 30 June 2026. [S:30b686db29f9, p.4]
- The points below come from the September 2025 consultation versions of the completion instructions. [S:30b686db29f9, p.3] The final versions went to AIs for download in December 2025. The HKMA said they would not differ materially. [S:30b686db29f9, p.3]
- MA(BS)3 Part IIIf is new. [S:d1fbf6c0736a, para 1] Its instructions say every Hong Kong-incorporated AI should complete it. The form works out extra risk-weighted amounts for cryptoassets. [S:d1fbf6c0736a, para 1]
- The Basel standard sorts cryptoassets into groups. Group 1 assets meet four classification conditions. Group 1b is the stablecoin part of Group 1. Group 2 assets do not meet the conditions. Group 2a assets also meet certain hedging criteria. Group 2b is the rest of Group 2. Part IIIf covers four items: [S:d1fbf6c0736a, paras 3-12]
  - An infrastructure add-on for Group 1 exposures in the banking book (assets not held for trading). The add-on is extra capital for risks in the underlying blockchain infrastructure. The HKMA sets it by written notice. [S:d1fbf6c0736a, paras 3-12]
  - Redemption-related credit risk. This is the risk that whoever redeems the tokens fails to pay. It covers Group 1b exposures in the trading book (assets held for trading) and Group 2a stablecoins. [S:d1fbf6c0736a, paras 3-12]
  - Each Group 2b cryptoasset. [S:d1fbf6c0736a, paras 3-12]
  - The Group 2 exposure ratio (Group 2 exposures measured against the bank's capital). All Hong Kong-incorporated AIs report it. Only global and domestic systemically important banks report its add-on. [S:d1fbf6c0736a, paras 3-12]
- The consultation version of the Part IIIf instructions carries a March 2026 version stamp (03/2026). [S:d1fbf6c0736a, header p.1]
- Part IIIa (basic approach) and Part IIIb (standardized approach) are credit-risk forms. Each gains a separate Division A2 for cryptoasset exposures. [S:2195417bfd31, para 4 and Section C.3, para 47; S:df1dbac9c51a, para 4 and Section C.3, para 60] Both also ask for the top five Group 1 cryptoassets by risk-weighted amount. [S:2195417bfd31, para 4 and Section C.3, para 47; S:df1dbac9c51a, para 4 and Section C.3, para 60]
- Part IIIc (a credit-risk form) covers the internal ratings-based approach (where a bank uses its own approved models for credit risk). [S:4b2b2befa66f, Section C.6] It adds a memorandum form, IRB_CRYPTO, for Group 1 exposures in the banking book. [S:4b2b2befa66f, Section C.6]
- MA(BS)1E is due no later than 14 days after each month-end. [S:f4e64fda4011, paras 5, 13.14] Category 1 institutions are AIs the HKMA designates to meet its main liquidity ratio. They report new memo items 1.7(a)-(b). One covers cryptoassets counted as high-quality liquid assets (assets easy to sell for cash in stress). The other covers tokenised claims on customers or counterparties. [S:f4e64fda4011, paras 5, 13.14]
- Tokenised deposits are bank deposits recorded as digital tokens. In MA(BS)1E, some tokenised deposits may be treated like ordinary deposits. [S:f4e64fda4011, para 31] This covers those that meet the criteria in SPM LM-1 (the liquidity risk module). [S:f4e64fda4011, para 31] But they do not get the 3% or 5% stable-deposit outflow rate. That rate is the low run-off assumed for stable deposits in a stress. [S:f4e64fda4011, para 31]
- MA(BS)26 is quarterly and due within one month. [S:767a346fbcaa, paras 4, 14] Category 1 institutions add items 3(a)-(b) on tokenised claims and cryptoassets. These feed the net stable funding ratio. This ratio checks that long-term assets have stable funding. [S:767a346fbcaa, paras 4, 14]
- MA(BS)27 includes cryptoassets in the leverage exposure measure. It values them at their financial-reporting value (the value in the bank's accounts). [S:3955600d53f0, attached completion instructions, para 6.5, pp.10-11]
- MA(BS)28 is quarterly and due within one month of quarter-end. [S:527c897d3eed, paras 4, 12] Some crypto exposures are not tied to a counterparty's credit or default risk. A bank need not include them when it reports exempted exposures. [S:527c897d3eed, paras 4, 12]
- Pillar 3: the revised disclosure package applies to any reporting period ending after 1 January 2026. [S:30b686db29f9, p.3]
- Table CAEA is annual. It covers crypto activities and risks. [S:9e8d84c87168, Table CAEA, pp.210-211] It also covers how the bank assessed each Group 1 classification condition. The bank includes public information it used, but not confidential or proprietary information. [S:9e8d84c87168, Table CAEA, pp.210-211]
- Hong Kong-incorporated banks with crypto exposures publish two templates twice a year. [S:9e8d84c87168, Templates CAE1 p.212, CAE2 p.216] CAE1 shows exposures and risk-weighted amounts by Group. CAE2 shows accounting classification. [S:9e8d84c87168, Templates CAE1 p.212, CAE2 p.216]
- CAE1 needs extra rows for each material stablecoin or unbacked cryptoasset. [S:9e8d84c87168, CAE1 points to note (iii), p.214] A Group 2 exposure is material if two tests are met. The Group 2 ratio is at least 0.3%, and the single asset exceeds 5% of total Group 2 exposure. [S:9e8d84c87168, CAE1 points to note (iii), p.214]
- The CAE1 narrative must state the market value of cryptoassets the bank holds in custody for clients, split by type. [S:9e8d84c87168, CAE1 accompanying narrative, p.212]
- CAE3 (liquidity) is published twice a year in a fixed format. [S:9e8d84c87168, Template CAE3, p.218; S:e10295e5fe20, Annex A, p.61-62] It applies to category 1 institutions with crypto exposures, whether incorporated locally or overseas. [S:9e8d84c87168, Template CAE3, p.218; S:e10295e5fe20, Annex A, p.61-62]

## What your bank must do

**Obligations**
- [ ] File the revised crypto items in MA(BS)1E, 3, 3A, 26, 27 and 28 on the stated schedules. [S:30b686db29f9, p.3]; [S:f4e64fda4011, para 5]; [S:767a346fbcaa, para 4]; [S:527c897d3eed, para 4]
- [ ] Complete MA(BS)3 Part IIIf if the bank is incorporated in Hong Kong. Include the Group 2 exposure ratio. [S:d1fbf6c0736a, paras 1, 11]
- [ ] Publish Table CAEA and Templates CAE1-CAE3 as they apply to the bank. [S:e10295e5fe20, Annex A, pp.61-62]; [S:9e8d84c87168, Part XII, pp.210-218]

**Controls & monitoring**
- [ ] Use daily averages over the period for certain CAE1 columns. [S:9e8d84c87168, CAE1 points to note (i), p.213] These are the Group 2a long and short columns, and the Group 2b total, long and short columns. [S:9e8d84c87168, CAE1 points to note (i), p.213]
- [ ] Run the 0.3% / 5% materiality test at each period end. The test decides which Group 2 assets need their own CAE1 row. [S:9e8d84c87168, CAE1 points to note (iii), p.214]
- [ ] Use the HKMA's explanatory notes, alongside the BDR, when filling in each standard template and table. [S:e10295e5fe20, para 2.1]

**Notify / consult HKMA or SFC**
- [ ] Agree a temporary arrangement with the HKMA if your systems are not ready for the revised returns. [S:30b686db29f9, p.4]

**Counterparty due diligence**
- [ ] Be ready to describe, for each Group 1 asset, how the bank assessed the four classification conditions. Include the public information used. Table CAEA asks for this. [S:9e8d84c87168, Table CAEA point (f), p.211]

## Talking points

**To the CCO**
- Crypto reporting started on 1 January 2026. The transition window for banks with no crypto ended on 30 June 2026. [S:30b686db29f9, p.3]
- CA-D-1 is general guidance on the HKMA's approach. If it conflicts with the Disclosure Rules, the Rules prevail. [S:e10295e5fe20, para 2.1]

**To business heads**
- A Transition AI that picked up crypto exposure after 1 January 2026 was grouped with exposed banks. [S:30b686db29f9, p.3-4] If its systems were not ready, it could agree a temporary arrangement with the HKMA. [S:30b686db29f9, p.3-4]
- The public CAE1 narrative shows the total market value of crypto we hold in custody for clients, split by type. [S:9e8d84c87168, CAE1 accompanying narrative, p.212]

**To the CEO**
- If we have crypto exposures, our public Pillar 3 report has a crypto section. It has a yearly narrative plus numbers twice a year. [S:e10295e5fe20, Annex A, pp.61-62]
- Seven HKMA returns changed at once for the cryptoasset standard. [S:30b686db29f9, p.3]

**To Risk / CRO**
- Every Hong Kong-incorporated AI reports its Group 2 exposure ratio in Part IIIf. Only global and domestic systemically important banks report the add-on. [S:d1fbf6c0736a, paras 11-12]
- Tokenised deposits do not get stable-deposit outflow rates in the liquidity return. [S:f4e64fda4011, para 31]

## Common mix-ups

- **Myth:** "No crypto, no reporting change." **Fact:** Transition AIs were still expected to apply some revised MA(BS)3 instructions. [S:30b686db29f9, p.3, footnote 4] These cover non-crypto items and applied from 1 January 2026. [S:30b686db29f9, p.3, footnote 4]
- **Myth:** "The transition covered all seven returns." **Fact:** It covered only four: MA(BS)26, 1E, 3 and 3A. [S:30b686db29f9, p.3]
- **Myth:** "Part IIIf redemption risk is a banking-book item." **Fact:** It sits in the trading book. [S:d1fbf6c0736a, para 5] The instructions place Group 1b redemption-related credit risk on trading-book exposures. [S:d1fbf6c0736a, para 5] The legal basis is section 376 of the Banking (Capital) Rules. [S:5d0c13e09312, para 8.7.4(a)]
- **Myth:** "Banks incorporated overseas disclose nothing." **Fact:** Two items apply to them too. [S:9e8d84c87168, Table CAEA scope, p.210; CAE3 scope, p.218] CAEA covers their crypto activities that create liquidity risk. CAE3 applies if they are category 1. [S:9e8d84c87168, Table CAEA scope, p.210; CAE3 scope, p.218]
- **Myth:** "Every stablecoin needs its own row." **Fact:** Group 2 rows follow the 0.3% / 5% test. [S:9e8d84c87168, CAE1 points to note (iii), p.214-215] Group 1b follows the general materiality test in the Disclosure Rules. [S:9e8d84c87168, CAE1 points to note (iii), p.214-215]

## Read these first

1. **Cryptoassets standard: SPM modules, code of practice, disclosure templates and tables, and banking returns** — HKMA, 27 Nov 2025. Read pp.3-4. It gives the returns list and the transition rules. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20251127-1-EN/20251127-1-EN.pdf
2. **Standard Disclosure Templates and Tables (Annex 4), Part XII** — HKMA, 27 Nov 2025. Read pp.210-219. It holds the crypto Pillar 3 templates and their notes. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20251027-8-EN/20251027-8-EN.pdf
3. **Completion Instructions, MA(BS)3 Part IIIf** — HKMA, consultation version stamped March 2026. Read paras 1-12. It explains the new crypto capital add-on form. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20250903-22-EN/20250903-22-EN.pdf

## Open items

- The documents reviewed hold the consultation versions of the completion instructions. They do not hold the December 2025 finals. The HKMA said there would be no material changes. [S:30b686db29f9, p.3]
- The documents reviewed for this guide do not include the gazetted text of the BDR amendment. BDR section numbers (such as 16ZQH-16ZQK) come from the templates and CA-D-1. [S:9e8d84c87168, Part XII; S:e10295e5fe20, para 12.2.4]
- No HKMA statement in the documents reviewed for this guide says whether any bank used the temporary alternative reporting arrangement.

title: AML/CFT for digital assets at a bank
md:
AML (anti-money laundering) and CFT (countering the financing of terrorism) rules exist to stop criminals using a bank to move or hide money. This module is for the Head of Compliance (digital assets) at a Hong Kong bank. After it, you can name the AML and CFT texts that actually bind the bank for virtual asset (VA) business. A virtual asset is a digital token such as a cryptocurrency. You can also point to where the rules written for virtual assets (VAs) sit. And you can tell which Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) material is only background. The same goes for Financial Action Task Force (FATF) material. Some of this material only sets expectations for the bank's counterparties. The FATF is the global standard-setter for anti-money laundering.

## In 60 seconds

The bank's AML rulebook for digital assets is the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) AML/CFT Guideline for Authorized Institutions (AIs). [S:7bfdad704174, para 1.3; S:16fd7cfab136, Part III para 1] Authorized institutions are the banks and deposit-takers the HKMA supervises. The HKMA revised the Guideline in May 2023, and it took effect on 1 June 2023. [S:7bfdad704174, para 1.3; S:16fd7cfab136, Part III para 1] The bank follows this HKMA Guideline, not the SFC's guideline. [S:7bfdad704174, para 1.3; S:16fd7cfab136, Part III para 1]

The Guideline says little about VAs. It covers four points: [S:7bfdad704174, paras 4.2.1 fn 15, 8.4, 11.23]

- A HK$8,000 trigger for customer due diligence (CDD) on one-off VA transfers. CDD means checking who a customer is and what they do. The trigger applies to people with no business relationship with the bank. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 4.2.1 fn 15, 8.4, 11.23]
- A footnote pointing to Schedule 2, section 13A of the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (AMLO). [S:7bfdad704174, paras 4.2.1 fn 15, 8.4, 11.23]
- Record keeping for five years. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 4.2.1 fn 15, 8.4, 11.23]
- Correspondent-style checks on virtual asset service providers (VASPs) located outside Hong Kong. A VASP (such as a crypto exchange) offers VA services to others. Correspondent-style checks are the due diligence a bank does before serving another financial firm. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 4.2.1 fn 15, 8.4, 11.23]

Other HKMA and SFC guidance calls the section 13A requirements the travel rule. [S:4d98c6a80b4d, paras 6.1–6.2; S:08a762f7233e, paras 12.11.1–12.11.2] The travel rule means sender and recipient details go along with each VA transfer.

The HKMA's January 2022 circular sets further expectations. [S:642680fa4467, pp.3–5] It asks banks to:

- watch customers' flows to and from VA platforms; [S:642680fa4467, pp.3–5]
- assess the risk of each VASP customer; [S:642680fa4467, pp.3–5]
- talk to the HKMA before launching VA products or services. [S:642680fa4467, pp.3–5]

The SFC's AML guideline applies to licensed corporations (LCs) and SFC-licensed VASPs. [S:08a762f7233e, para 12.1.2] LCs are firms licensed by the SFC. Chapter 12 of that guideline covers VAs. [S:08a762f7233e, para 12.1.2] The bank's SFC-registered business is a registered institution (RI). An RI is a bank registered with the SFC to do securities business. The RI must take the SFC guideline into account. [S:7bfdad704174, fn 1] The RI must comply with Chapter 12 when it handles client VA deposits or withdrawals. [S:8a016a912528, para 20(b)]

Recent SFC circulars describe current money laundering patterns. [S:be46918f8aa2, paras 7–8; S:cfc4a0d9f1be, paras 1, 11] One is scam money layered through brokers and platforms. [S:be46918f8aa2, paras 7–8] Layering means moving money through many transactions to hide where it came from. Another is misuse of simplified Electronic Direct Debit Authorisation (eDDA) deposits. [S:cfc4a0d9f1be, paras 1, 11] eDDA lets a customer approve direct debits from a bank account online. The SFC also passed on a March 2026 FATF report on stablecoins and unhosted wallets. [S:00c9fbd119bf, p.3] A stablecoin is a token designed to keep a steady value, for example against a currency. An unhosted wallet is a crypto wallet the owner controls directly, not through a service provider.

## Status board

As of 25 September 2026. Registered institutions (RIs) are banks registered with the SFC. The Legislative Council (LegCo) is Hong Kong's law-making body.
