## Key facts

- The HKMA Guideline is the AML rulebook for every AI, including AIs registered with the SFC. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 1.3, 1.6] The Guideline treats both "must" and "should" as signalling a mandatory requirement. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 1.3, 1.6]
- One-off VA transfers: an AI should complete CDD before carrying out an occasional VA transfer worth HK$8,000 or more. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 4.2.1(b)(iii), 4.2.4] It should also watch for linked smaller transfers that together reach that amount, and carry out CDD if they do. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 4.2.1(b)(iii), 4.2.4]
- For VA transfers, the Guideline points readers to AMLO Schedule 2, section 13A (footnote 15). [S:7bfdad704174, para 4.2.1 fn 15; Chapter 10] Chapter 10 of the Guideline, on wire transfers, does not mention VAs. [S:7bfdad704174, para 4.2.1 fn 15; Chapter 10]
- The HKMA has stated that the AMLO does not stop AIs making VA transfers for customers if they meet the section 13A requirements. [S:16fd7cfab136, Part II para 4.3]
- The bank should keep records of occasional VA transfers of HK$8,000 or more for at least five years after the transaction. [S:7bfdad704174, para 8.4] For relationship records, the period is the life of the relationship plus at least five years after it ends. [S:7bfdad704174, para 8.4]
- This point covers a bank that gives correspondent-like services to financial institutions (FIs) or VASPs located outside Hong Kong. [S:7bfdad704174, para 11.23, fn 78–79] That bank should apply the cross-border correspondent measures in paras 11.6 and 11.13 (where they apply). [S:7bfdad704174, para 11.23, fn 78–79] FIs as defined in the AMLO are left out of this rule. [S:7bfdad704174, para 11.23, fn 78–79]
- For an overseas VASP customer, the bank should find out whether the account is for the VASP's own use or for serving its clients. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 11.24–11.25] The bank could consider encouraging or requiring separate accounts for the two. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 11.24–11.25]
- RIs are required to take the SFC's AML Guideline into account, including Chapter 12 on VAs. [S:7bfdad704174, fn 1 to para 1.3; S:8934af8cc884, para 4.16.1] The same applies to AIs that are associated entities of SFC licensees. An associated entity is a company linked to an SFC licensee that holds client assets for it. [S:7bfdad704174, fn 1 to para 1.3; S:8934af8cc884, para 4.16.1]
- The HKMA expects AIs to watch for customers who often send money to or receive money from VA platforms. [S:642680fa4467, AML/CFT section (a), pp.3–4] AIs should understand those flows and, where there are grounds, file suspicious transaction reports (STRs). [S:642680fa4467, AML/CFT section (a), pp.3–4]
- For VASP customers, the bank's risk assessments should tell individual VASPs apart. [S:642680fa4467, AML/CFT section (b), p.4] Depending on the relationship, extra CDD may be needed. [S:642680fa4467, AML/CFT section (b), p.4] Examples: [S:642680fa4467, AML/CFT section (b), p.4]
  - understand the VASP's business model;
  - check its licensing, and whether the overseas rules are comparable;
  - assess the VASP's own AML controls.
- An AI planning VA activity should discuss it with the HKMA before launch. [S:642680fa4467, 'AIs' VA-related proposals', p.5] It should also get the HKMA's feedback on its risk controls before launch. [S:642680fa4467, 'AIs' VA-related proposals', p.5]
- Intermediaries are LCs and RIs. Those that let clients deposit or withdraw VAs should comply with SFC Chapter 12 for those movements. [S:8a016a912528, para 20(b); S:b79266f3da51, para 7(c)] The same applies when clients use VAs to subscribe for or redeem investment products. [S:8a016a912528, para 20(b); S:b79266f3da51, para 7(c)]
- SFC Chapter 12 requires the ordering firm to get, record and pass on sender (originator) and recipient details for VA transfers. [S:08a762f7233e, paras 12.11.5–12.11.10, 12.14.2] The ordering firm is the one that sends the transfer for its customer. The full set of details applies at HK$8,000 or more, and a shorter set below that. [S:08a762f7233e, paras 12.11.5–12.11.10, 12.14.2] For unhosted wallets, the firm should collect similar details from its own customer. [S:08a762f7233e, paras 12.11.5–12.11.10, 12.14.2]
- Licensed stablecoin issuers that send transfers must collect full sender and recipient details for transfers of HK$8,000 or more. Fewer details apply below that. [S:4d98c6a80b4d, paras 6.5–6.6, 5.11] The HKMA expects every holder's identity to be checked, unless an issuer shows the HKMA its controls work. [S:4d98c6a80b4d, paras 6.5–6.6, 5.11]
- The SFC, citing police intelligence, reports scam money being layered through licensed firms. [S:be46918f8aa2, para 8] Some of it was turned into VAs and withdrawn to unhosted wallets. [S:be46918f8aa2, para 8]
- A Government reply to LegCo on 21 Feb 2024 gave the number of VA-related criminal cases: [S:4bd22ccf481d, reply (1)–(2)]
  - 2021: 1,397 cases, with HK$824 million involved;
  - 2022: 2,336 cases, with HK$1,704 million involved;
  - 2023: 3,415 cases, with HK$4,398 million involved.
- An HKMA speaker said Hong Kong recorded over 44,000 deception cases in 2024. That was a rise of close to 12% on the year before. [S:165d354a94bc, remarks on fraud and scams]

## What your bank must do

**Obligations**
- Complete CDD before any occasional VA transfer of HK$8,000 or more. Watch for linked transfers. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 4.2.1(b)(iii), 4.2.4–4.2.5]
- Meet AMLO Schedule 2, section 13A for VA transfers the bank carries out. [S:7bfdad704174, fn 15; S:16fd7cfab136, Part II para 4.3]
- Assess money laundering and terrorist financing risk before launching any VA-related product, service or new technology. Put controls in place to reduce that risk. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 2.10–2.11; S:642680fa4467, pp.2–3]
- Keep VA transfer and relationship records for the periods in para 8.4. [S:7bfdad704174, para 8.4]

**Controls & monitoring**
- Monitor customers' flows to and from VA platforms, and look into what they are for. [S:642680fa4467, AML/CFT section (a), pp.3–4]
- Write down the settings and thresholds that trigger transaction-monitoring alerts. Review them regularly and have them checked independently. [S:7bfdad704174, para 5.8]
- In the RI business, apply SFC Chapter 12 when handling client VA deposits and withdrawals. [S:8a016a912528, para 20(b)]

**Notify / consult HKMA or SFC**
- Discuss any planned VA activity with the HKMA before launch. [S:642680fa4467, 'AIs' VA-related proposals', p.5]
- For the RI: tell the SFC and HKMA before it starts VA activities or changes them. [S:8934af8cc884, para 5.6] This covers dealing, advice and asset management, and changes to the type of clients served. [S:8934af8cc884, para 5.6]
- File STRs with the Joint Financial Intelligence Unit (JFIU) where the bank finds grounds for suspicion. The JFIU is the unit that receives these reports. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 5.10–5.12]

**Counterparty due diligence**
- For overseas VASPs that get correspondent-like services, do the following: [S:7bfdad704174, paras 11.6, 11.23–11.24]
  - understand the business;
  - check its reputation and how it is supervised;
  - assess its AML controls;
  - get senior management approval.
- Confirm with each VASP customer that its operations do not break the laws that apply in Hong Kong or elsewhere. [S:642680fa4467, AML/CFT section (b), p.4]
- Note that the SFC expects licensed firms to register the client bank accounts used for deposits and withdrawals. [S:be46918f8aa2, para 20] It also expects them to whitelist client wallet addresses, meaning they keep a list of approved addresses. [S:be46918f8aa2, para 20]

## Talking points

**To the CCO**
- Our main AML text for VAs is the HKMA Guideline for AIs. [S:7bfdad704174, para 1.3, fn 1] Our RI business must take SFC Chapter 12 into account, and comply with it for client VA deposits or withdrawals. [S:7bfdad704174, para 1.3, fn 1; S:8a016a912528, para 20(b)]
- For our own VA transfers, the Guideline points to AMLO Schedule 2, section 13A, not the wire-transfer chapter. [S:7bfdad704174, fn 15]

**To business heads**
- Any VA product needs a written money laundering and terrorist financing risk assessment. [S:7bfdad704174, para 2.11] It also needs a conversation with the HKMA before launch. [S:642680fa4467, p.5]
- If we serve an overseas VASP like a correspondent bank, we need correspondent-style checks and senior management approval. [S:7bfdad704174, paras 11.6, 11.23–11.24]

**To the CEO**
- The HKMA has said the AMLO does not prohibit AIs from making VA transfers for customers if they meet the section 13A requirements. [S:16fd7cfab136, Part II para 4.3]
- The Government told LegCo that money involved in VA-related crime reached HK$4,398 million in 2023. That was up from HK$824 million in 2021. [S:4bd22ccf481d, reply (1)–(2)]

**To Risk / CRO**
- The SFC's red flags for licensed firms include deposits and withdrawals with little or no trading. [S:be46918f8aa2, para 7] Another is a new eDDA setup followed by whitelisting a new wallet address. [S:cfc4a0d9f1be, para 11]
- An SFC circular notes that the FATF published a report on stablecoin and unhosted wallet risks on 3 March 2026. [S:00c9fbd119bf, p.3 item (3)(c)]

## Common mix-ups

- **Myth:** SFC Chapter 12 binds the bank. **Fact:** It applies to LCs and SFC-licensed VASPs. [S:08a762f7233e, para 12.1.2] The HKMA said AIs, including RIs, should keep complying with its own Guideline. RIs take the SFC text into account. [S:16fd7cfab136, Part II para 4.2]
- **Myth:** Chapter 10 of the HKMA Guideline is our crypto travel rule. **Fact:** Chapter 10 covers wire transfers. The link to VA transfers is footnote 15, which points to section 13A. [S:7bfdad704174, fn 15, Chapter 10]
- **Myth:** All VASP customers need correspondent banking measures. **Fact:** Para 11.23 targets VASPs located outside Hong Kong. [S:7bfdad704174, para 11.23] For other VASP customers, the HKMA expects a risk-based assessment, with extra CDD depending on the relationship. [S:642680fa4467, AML/CFT section (b), p.4]
- **Myth:** VASPs are automatically high-risk. **Fact:** The HKMA asks banks to assess each VASP's risks separately. There is no single approach. [S:642680fa4467, AML/CFT section (b), p.4]
- **Myth:** The 2026 custody guidance removed AML duties. **Fact:** The 2024 annex had its own AML paragraph, and the 2026 text does not. [S:86e064b2a8d0, para 23; S:ce05e67bcdce, sections (A)–(H)] But the AML Guideline still applies to all AIs. [S:7bfdad704174, para 1.3]

## Read these first

1. **Guideline on AML/CFT (For Authorized Institutions), revised May 2023** — HKMA, 25 May 2023. Read footnote 1 (printed p.1) and paras 2.10–2.11. Then read paras 4.2.1–4.2.5 with footnotes 14–15. Then read paras 8.4, 11.6 and 11.23–11.25. Why: this is the text that binds the bank. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20230525-4-EN/AML-2.pdf
2. **Regulatory approaches to AIs' interface with VAs and VASPs** — HKMA, 28 Jan 2022. Read pp.3–5. Why: it sets out what the HKMA expects on VA flows, VASP customers and talks before launch. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/20220128-1-EN
3. **AML/CFT Guideline for LCs and SFC-licensed VASPs, Chapter 12** — SFC, 1 Jun 2023. Read 12.1, 12.11, 12.13–12.14. Why: it shows what the RI business must take into account, and what counterparties must do. https://www.sfc.hk/-/media/EN/assets/components/codes/files-current/web/guidelines/guideline-on-anti-money-laundering-and-counter-financing-of-terrorism-for-licensed-corporations/AML-Guideline-for-LCs-and-SFC-licensed-VASPs_Eng_1-Jun-2023.pdf

## Open items

- The 2023 consultation conclusions cite an HKMA circular of 27 April 2023. [S:16fd7cfab136, Part II para 4.3] That circular is not in the documents reviewed for this guide, so its content is unverified here.
- The text of AMLO Schedule 2, section 13A is not in the documents reviewed. So this guide does not restate the data fields it sets for banks.
- In May 2025, the HKMA said it was writing an extra AML/CFT guideline for digital asset activities. [S:0d6e6d0253ff, para 4.1] It was to cover AIs and stablecoin licensees. The HKMA said it would consult later in 2025. [S:0d6e6d0253ff, para 4.1] No consultation or final version appears in the documents reviewed.
- The HKMA's document page still lists the 16 Dec 2019 circular as current. [S:2b4123d71a07, landing page] The AML guidance in the 28 Jan 2022 circular follows it, updated for the FATF guidance of October 2021. [S:642680fa4467, p.3 fn 4]
- The documents reviewed contain no official VA crime statistics after 2023. The FATF report on stablecoins and unhosted wallets is also not among them.
- The SFC eDDA and layering circulars go to LCs, SFC-licensed VASPs and associated entities. The documents reviewed contain no matching HKMA circular for banks as payer banks. A payer bank is the bank that holds the customer's account being debited.

## Related modules

B-series (HKMA supervision of VA activity), C-series (RI conduct and custody), [D4](#m-D4), [D5](#m-D5), [E1](#m-E1), [E3](#m-E3).

title: Cyber, fraud and technology risk
md:
This module is for the Head of Compliance (digital assets) at a Hong Kong bank. After it, you can:
- Name the technology-risk expectations the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) sets for the bank.
- Tell them apart from the rules the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) sets for the bank's platform and broker counterparties.
- Name the dated SFC deadlines.
- Describe the scam patterns that regulators have flagged.

## In 60 seconds

For a bank, the technology-risk texts on digital assets come from the HKMA. [S:1884530ff235, Annex; S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 10–11] The first is an April 2024 list of risk points for authorized institutions (AIs). AIs are banks and other deposit-takers that the HKMA authorizes. [S:1884530ff235, Annex] It covers AIs that use distributed ledger technology (DLT), the shared record-keeping technology behind blockchains. [S:1884530ff235, Annex] The second is the HKMA custody standards. In May 2026 the HKMA added detailed controls for wallets and for managing the secret keys that control digital assets. [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 10–11]

The SFC has a parallel, more detailed set of rules. It covers licensed virtual asset trading platform (VATP) operators and internet brokers. Four SFC circulars stand out:
- An August 2025 custody circular, prompted by incidents at overseas platforms. [S:562c0f8addce, p.1]
- A January 2025 circular on what SFC inspections found. [S:0c93d9a066e6, p.1]
- A June 2026 circular on cyberattacks that use artificial intelligence. [S:a4929c8f9f3e, para 1]
- A July 2026 circular on client login. It expects firms to stop relying on one-time passwords (OTPs) when clients log in or bind (register) a device. [S:724f4d9f786e, paras 7, 21(c)] Firms are to move to phishing-resistant methods by 8 July 2027. [S:724f4d9f786e, paras 7, 21(c)] Phishing means fake messages or websites that trick people into giving away login details. Phishing-resistant methods are logins that a fake website is unable to capture and reuse.

These SFC circulars are addressed to SFC-licensed firms, not to the bank. [S:724f4d9f786e, para 1] But they show what the bank's VATP and broker counterparties are expected to have. [S:724f4d9f786e, para 1] Also, many controls in the HKMA's 2026 custody update use the same wording as the SFC's 2025 custody circular. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(c), (f), (i); S:562c0f8addce, paras 5, 14, 28]

On fraud, the HKMA has warned the public about three things:
- Crypto firms that call themselves 'banks'. [S:19c8611c621a, para 1]
- Tokens falsely linked to licensed stablecoin issuers. [S:275e7319a841, para 2]
- Entities that falsely claim to be part of its e-HKD (digital Hong Kong dollar) Pilot Programme. [S:5f67b02549b0, para 1]

## Status board

As of 25 Sep 2026.

| Instrument | Issuer | Date | Status (chip) | Applies to | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Risk management considerations related to the use of DLT | HKMA | 16 Apr 2024 | In force | AIs | [S:1884530ff235, Annex] |
| Updated custody expected standards (key management, wallet controls) | HKMA | 27 May 2026 | In force | AIs and subsidiaries of locally incorporated AIs | [S:ce05e67bcdce, opening para; paras 10–11] |
| Inspection findings on platforms treated as licensed while applying (25EC3) | SFC | 16 Jan 2025 | In force | VATP operators | [S:0c93d9a066e6, p.1] |
| Cybersecurity webinar materials (25EC11) | SFC | 20 Feb 2025 | Superseded | Licensed corporations (LCs), licensed virtual asset service providers (VASPs), associated entities | [S:0fcb48929954, p.1] |
| Custody of virtual assets (25EC44) | SFC | 15 Aug 2025 | In force | VATP operators | [S:562c0f8addce, 'Way forward', p.7] |
| Cyberattacks enabled by artificial intelligence (26EC32) | SFC | 2 Jun 2026 | In force | LCs, VASPs, associated entities | [S:a4929c8f9f3e, para 1] |
| Phishing-resistant authentication and surveillance (26EC35) | SFC | 9 Jul 2026 | Issued, effective 8 Jul 2027 (authentication deadline; other sections immediate or as soon as practicable) | Internet brokers, SFC-licensed VASPs | [S:724f4d9f786e, para 21] |
| Alert: crypto firms misusing 'bank' | HKMA | 15 Nov 2024 (updating 15 Sep 2023 alert) | In force | Public | [S:19c8611c621a, para 1; S:fcbcbb5d9d99, para 1] |
| Alert: tokens using licensed issuers' names | HKMA | 28 Apr 2026 | In force | Public | [S:275e7319a841, para 2] |

Note: the SFC's own record lists 25EC11 as historical webinar material. 'Superseded' is the closest status chip. HKMA alerts are one-off public notices, recorded as historical. 'In force' is shown only because it is the closest chip.

## Key facts

- The HKMA says an AI's board and senior management carry full responsibility for using DLT and for its risks. [S:1884530ff235, Annex item 1] The HKMA also says the AI should update its policies on technology risk, business continuity and outsourcing for DLT as needed. [S:1884530ff235, Annex item 1]
- The HKMA expects banks to understand the types of DLT network and pick one that suits the application's risks. [S:1884530ff235, Annex items 2, 5] Anyone can join a permissionless network. The HKMA sees such networks as likely unsuitable for highly critical or sensitive functions. [S:1884530ff235, Annex items 2, 5] The exception is where adequate compensating controls (extra safeguards that offset the risk) exist. [S:1884530ff235, Annex items 2, 5]
- A bank acting as custodian (holding assets for clients) would generally be expected to have stricter procedures for private keys. [S:1884530ff235, Annex item 8] A private key is the secret code that controls a digital asset. The procedures cover creating, storing and backing up keys securely. [S:1884530ff235, Annex item 8] Examples include limited access, cold storage (keys kept offline) and offsite backups. [S:1884530ff235, Annex item 8]
- The HKMA's May 2026 custody update includes three controls: [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 10, 11(c), 11(i)]
  - System-based whitelists (lists of pre-approved addresses) for transfers out of cold wallets. A cold wallet is one whose keys are kept offline.
  - No smart contracts in cold wallets on public blockchains. A smart contract is code on a blockchain that runs by itself.
  - Measures to prevent 'blind signing', which means approving a transaction without seeing its details.
- Keys and seeds should be created and stored in tamper-resistant devices, such as hardware security modules (HSMs). [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(a)–(b)] A seed is a master secret from which keys can be rebuilt. HSMs are sealed devices built to protect keys. Keys and seeds should also be created, stored and backed up in Hong Kong. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(a)–(b)]
- Where the assets in custody are virtual assets (VAs), a bank custodian should hold 98% of client VAs in cold storage. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(l), fn 8]
- Wallet software code must be managed with strictly enforced segregation of duties, so no single person controls the whole process. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(f)] Administrator access should follow least privilege, meaning staff get only the access their job needs. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(f)] The segregation line is the annex's only 'must'. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(f)]
- Custody security monitoring should run 24/7, including holidays. [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 23–24] It should also cover outside dependencies, such as vendors, blockchain protocols and encryption algorithms. [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 23–24]
- The SFC's August 2025 custody circular took effect immediately for VATP operators. [S:562c0f8addce, p.1; 'Way forward', p.7] The SFC says overseas incidents showed potential critical weaknesses, whatever custody solution was used. [S:562c0f8addce, p.1; 'Way forward', p.7] Examples of such solutions are HSMs, multi-signature wallets and multi-party computation (MPC). A multi-signature wallet needs several approvers to sign a transfer. MPC splits a key into shares held by different parties or devices.
- The SFC inspected platforms that were treated as licensed while their applications were pending. [S:0c93d9a066e6, Appendix 2 paras 6, 18, 22] It found four problems: [S:0c93d9a066e6, Appendix 2 paras 6, 18, 22]
  - Keys for one hot wallet (a wallet connected to the internet) were kept partly outside Hong Kong.
  - One cold wallet was built as a multi-signature smart contract.
  - Some encryption algorithms were outdated.
  - Hot-wallet calculations under the 98/2 rule had errors. The rule keeps 98% of client assets in cold storage and at most 2% in hot wallets.
- The SFC's June 2026 circular reminds firms that senior managers bear ultimate responsibility for cybersecurity risk. [S:a4929c8f9f3e, paras 3, 9–15] These managers include the Manager-in-Charge of information technology. [S:a4929c8f9f3e, paras 3, 9–15] The circular asks firms to review five areas: [S:a4929c8f9f3e, paras 3, 9–15]
  - patching (installing security fixes);
  - access controls;
  - detection of attacks;
  - supply chain;
  - incident response.
- The Hong Kong Computer Emergency Response Team Coordination Centre (HKCERT) recorded 15,877 cybersecurity incidents in 2025. [S:a4929c8f9f3e, fn 1] That was up from 12,536 in 2024, as cited by the SFC. [S:a4929c8f9f3e, fn 1]
- The SFC does not consider OTPs sent by text message (SMS) or email to be phishing-resistant. [S:724f4d9f786e, paras 7–8, 21(c)] Internet brokers and VASPs are expected to adopt robust login methods no later than 8 July 2027. [S:724f4d9f786e, paras 7–8, 21(c)] Examples include passkeys and bound devices. [S:724f4d9f786e, paras 7–8, 21(c)] A passkey is a password-free login stored on the client's device. A bound device is a phone or computer linked to the client's account. Large internet brokers are expected to act immediately. [S:724f4d9f786e, paras 7–8, 21(c)]
- This point is about large-scale unauthorised transactions through client accounts after hacking incidents. [S:724f4d9f786e, para 25] If a firm lacks adequate measures to prevent, detect and halt them, the SFC will hold it accountable for clients' losses. [S:724f4d9f786e, para 25]
- In February 2025 the SFC only strongly urged licensed corporations to drop OTPs for login and device binding. [S:4ce7d53d6956, Note 4] The July 2026 circular goes further. [S:4ce7d53d6956, Note 4]
- Under the Banking Ordinance, only AIs may take deposits. [S:fcbcbb5d9d99, para 3, Notes 1–2] A business that is not a bank commits an offence if it uses the word 'bank' in its business name. [S:fcbcbb5d9d99, para 3, Notes 1–2] The exception is where the Monetary Authority has given written consent (section 97). [S:fcbcbb5d9d99, para 3, Notes 1–2]
- In April 2026 the HKMA warned about tokens with the tickers (trading symbols) 'HKDAP' and 'HSBC'. [S:275e7319a841, paras 2–3] These tokens were not issued by, or linked to, licensed stablecoin issuers. [S:275e7319a841, paras 2–3] Both licensed issuers had confirmed they had not issued any regulated stablecoins. [S:275e7319a841, paras 2–3]
- An HKMA presentation of 25 September 2026 gives the sector's first Quantum Preparedness Index score as 2.3 out of 10. [S:a50e9dc16dc7, slide 11] The index tracks how ready the sector is for risks from quantum computing. The objective is full readiness across the sector by 2030. [S:a50e9dc16dc7, slide 11]

## What your bank must do

**Obligations**
- Keep the board and senior management in charge of DLT risk. [S:1884530ff235, Annex item 1] Update technology-risk, continuity and outsourcing policies. [S:1884530ff235, Annex item 1]
- For custody, run a full risk assessment before launch. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 1] Make sure the board and senior management oversee the activity before and during it. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 1]
- For client VAs, meet the key-management controls in para 11 of the custody annex: [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11, fn 8]
  - use HSMs;
  - keep keys in Hong Kong;
  - keep smart contracts out of cold wallets on public blockchains;
  - prevent blind signing;
  - hold 98% in cold storage.

**Controls & monitoring**
- Use system controls and whitelists to stop unauthorised transfers out of cold wallets. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 10] Check each transaction through a systematic process. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 10]
- Run security monitoring 24/7. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 23] Test system changes thoroughly before they go live. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 23]
- Add DLT-specific scenarios to continuity plans for critical functions. [S:1884530ff235, Annex item 10] Examples are cyberattacks, loss or theft of keys, and forks (a split of a blockchain into two versions). [S:1884530ff235, Annex item 10]
- An HKMA speech says banks should secure their own cyber basics and those of critical service providers. [S:a50e9dc16dc7, slide 10] It also says the risks of frontier artificial intelligence (the most advanced models) should not be underestimated. [S:a50e9dc16dc7, slide 10]

**Notify / consult HKMA or SFC**
- Discuss virtual asset activity with the HKMA before launch, and get its feedback on risk controls. [S:642680fa4467, p.5]
- SFC-licensed firms in the bank's group should promptly report material cyber incidents to the SFC. [S:a4929c8f9f3e, para 18]
- Internet brokers or VASPs should tell their SFC case officer at once if they expect trouble meeting the July 2027 login deadline. [S:724f4d9f786e, para 23]

**Counterparty due diligence**
- Before relying on a DLT network, check that its node operators are trustworthy, reliable and diverse. [S:1884530ff235, Annex item 5] Node operators are the parties that run the computers that keep the network going.
- For custody delegates (firms the bank hands custody to), check for: [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 15]
  - independent code reviews;
  - an understanding of how software releases are made;
  - regular evaluation of security controls and disaster-recovery testing.
- A bank may delegate custody of VAs to an SFC-licensed VATP operator after due diligence. [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 14–15] The SFC's own custody standards for VATP operators show what such a platform is expected to have. [S:562c0f8addce, paras 2, 7, 10, 18, 24] They include: [S:562c0f8addce, paras 2, 7, 10, 18, 24]
  - HSMs;
  - air-gapped signing devices (devices never connected to a network);
  - a security operations centre (a team that watches for attacks);
  - 24/7 monitoring.

## Talking points

**To the chief compliance officer (CCO)**
- The SFC circular on OTPs is addressed to internet brokers and VASPs, not the bank. [S:724f4d9f786e, para 1] Our own custody baseline is the HKMA custody annex. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11]
- Several wallet controls in the HKMA's 2026 custody annex use the same wording as the SFC's 2025 custody circular. [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 10–11; S:562c0f8addce, Sections II–III]

**To business heads**
- Custody keys are to be kept in Hong Kong, in tamper-resistant devices such as HSMs. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(a)–(c)] Smart contracts are ruled out for cold wallets on public blockchains. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(a)–(c)]
- Counterparty platforms and internet brokers are expected to move client login and device binding off OTPs by 8 July 2027. [S:724f4d9f786e, paras 7, 21(c)]

**To the CEO**
- The HKMA places responsibility for DLT adoption and its risks with the board and senior management. [S:1884530ff235, Annex item 1]
- Phishing made up 57% of security incidents reported to HKCERT in 2025, as cited by the SFC. [S:724f4d9f786e, fn 5]

**To Risk / chief risk officer (CRO)**
- The HKMA's first quantum readiness score for the sector is 2.3 out of 10. [S:a50e9dc16dc7, slide 11] The objective is full readiness by 2030. [S:a50e9dc16dc7, slide 11]
- The HKMA has warned about crypto firms presenting themselves as 'banks'. [S:19c8611c621a, para 2] It has also warned about tokens falsely linked to licensed stablecoin issuers. [S:275e7319a841, para 2]

## Common mix-ups

- **Myth:** "MPC or multi-signature makes custody safe." **Fact:** The SFC says overseas incidents pointed to potential critical weaknesses, whatever the custody solution. [S:562c0f8addce, p.1]
- **Myth:** "The 50%/100% compensation cover applies to bank custodians." **Fact:** That cover is an SFC requirement for VATP operators. [S:0c93d9a066e6, Appendix 2 para 33] It covers potential loss of 50% of client VAs in cold wallets and 100% in hot wallets (VATP Guidelines para 10.22). [S:0c93d9a066e6, Appendix 2 para 33] The 2026 HKMA annex takes a different approach. It makes the bank liable for losses from incidents attributable to the bank. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(n)] It also requires adequate financial resources, which may include insurance. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(n)]
- **Myth:** "OTPs are fine for client login." **Fact:** Not for SFC-licensed internet brokers and VASPs. They are expected to stop using OTPs for login and device binding by 8 July 2027. [S:724f4d9f786e, paras 7, 21(c)]
- **Myth:** "The HKMA DLT considerations are hard rules." **Fact:** The HKMA calls them non-binding and not a complete list. It discusses detailed expectations with each bank one to one. [S:1884530ff235, Annex, Introduction]
- **Myth:** "A licensed issuer's name on a token means it is regulated." **Fact:** The HKMA warned these tokens were not issued by, or linked to, the licensed issuers. [S:275e7319a841, paras 2–3]

## Read these first

1. **Updated Guidance on Expected Standards on Provision of Custodial Services for Digital Assets by AIs** — HKMA, 27 May 2026. Read paras 10–11, 14–15, 23–25. Why: it sets the bank's own baseline for key and wallet controls. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20260527-7-EN/20260527-7-EN.pdf
2. **Risk management considerations related to the use of DLT** — HKMA, 16 Apr 2024. Read all ten items. Why: it shows how the HKMA reviews bank DLT projects. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20240416-2-EN/20240416-2-EN.pdf
3. **Circular 26EC35 on robust authentication and surveillance** — SFC, 9 Jul 2026. Read paras 5–13, 21–25. Why: it sets the counterparty deadline and the line on liability for losses. https://apps.sfc.hk/edistributionWeb/api/circular/openFile?lang=EN&refNo=26EC35

## Open items

- The documents reviewed for this guide include no HKMA circular on phishing-resistant authentication for banks. The 2026 Policy Address says the HKMA is driving the use of 'iAM Smart' step-up authentication in banks. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 51(i)] The iAM Smart app is the government's digital identity tool. Step-up authentication means an extra identity check for riskier actions. First-phase testing on remote account opening is under way. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 51(i)]
- The SFC cybersecurity circular of 6 February 2025 is referred to, but it is not among the documents reviewed for this guide. [S:4ce7d53d6956, Note 4]
- Two items are outside this module. One is the staking guidance that the HKMA custody annex cross-refers to. Staking means locking up tokens to help run a blockchain in return for rewards. The other is the SFC's November 2024 circular on generative artificial intelligence.

## Related modules

[D3](#m-D3), [D5](#m-D5), [E1](#m-E1), [E2](#m-E2), [E3](#m-E3).

title: Tax and information reporting
md:
For the bank's Head of Compliance (digital assets). After this module you can explain three things:
- what the Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF) bill would require;
- where CARF overlaps with the bank's existing Common Reporting Standard (CRS) duties;
- what the government has said about tax concessions (tax breaks) for digital-asset funds.

CRS is the global standard under which banks and other financial institutions report accounts held by foreign tax residents to the tax authority.

## In 60 seconds

CARF is a global tax standard from the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD). [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, Overview] Under CARF, tax authorities exchange tax data on crypto-asset transactions once a year. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, Overview] Hong Kong committed to CARF in December 2024. [S:ea81f92ea327, para 1] The government consulted on it in December 2025. [S:252a7f86684e, para 1]

The bill is the Inland Revenue (Amendment) (CARF and Amended CRS) Bill 2026. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, Overview] The bill appeared in the Gazette (the government's official journal) on 22 May 2026. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, Overview] It had its First Reading in the Legislative Council (LegCo) on 3 June 2026. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, Overview] The documents reviewed do not show the bill passing as of 25 September 2026. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, Overview]

If passed, CARF duties would start on 1 January 2027, and amended CRS duties on 1 January 2028. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, Clause 1(3)-(4)]

The bill calls a business that carries out crypto exchange transactions for customers a reporting crypto-asset service provider (RCASP). [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, ss.50M, 50O-50Q, 80R] An RCASP with a Hong Kong link would have to register, check its customers (due diligence), report and keep records. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, ss.50M, 50O-50Q, 80R] Failures could lead to fines. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, ss.50M, 50O-50Q, 80R]

CRS already covers bank accounts. [S:275d5cc93a88, paras 4.3-4.5] The amended CRS adds crypto-linked assets and digital money products. [S:275d5cc93a88, paras 4.3-4.5]

Separately, the government said it would extend fund and family-office tax breaks to digital assets. [S:a29b51bffc6b, para 15]; [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 98] It is aiming at the 2025/26 tax year (year of assessment). [S:a29b51bffc6b, para 15]; [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 98]

## Status board

As of 25 September 2026.

Abbreviations in this table:
- FSTB = Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau
- IRD = Inland Revenue Department (Hong Kong's tax authority)
- HKMA = Hong Kong Monetary Authority
- SFC = Securities and Futures Commission
- RCASPs = reporting crypto-asset service providers

| Instrument | Issuer | Date | Status (chip) | Applies to | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Commitment to implement CARF (first exchanges from 2028) | FSTB | 13 Dec 2024 | Stated target | Hong Kong government | [S:ea81f92ea327, para 4] |
| CARF and amended CRS consultation paper | FSTB + IRD | 9 Dec 2025 | Consultation closed 6 Feb 2026; followed by the bill | Proposed RCASPs; CRS financial institutions | [S:275d5cc93a88, para 8 and Chapter 6, PDF p.8, 48-49]; [S:252a7f86684e, para 7] |
| Inland Revenue (Amendment) (CARF and Amended CRS) Bill 2026 | LegCo / FSTB / IRD | Gazetted 22 May 2026; First Reading 3 Jun 2026 | Bill before LegCo | Hong Kong RCASPs (Part 2); reporting financial institutions (Part 3) | [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, Clause 1(2)-(4)]; [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, Overview]; [S:d5097f447cf9, para 1] |
| IRD CARF web guidance | IRD | Undated (reflects bill) | Bill before LegCo | RCASPs | [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, Overview] |
| Tax concessions for funds and family-owned investment holding vehicles (FIHVs) to cover digital assets | FSTB / Financial Secretary | 26 Jun 2025; 25 Feb 2026 | Stated target | Privately offered funds; FIHVs; single-family offices | [S:a29b51bffc6b, para 15]; [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 98] |

## Key facts

- On 13 December 2024, the government told the OECD's Global Forum on tax transparency that it would implement CARF. [S:ea81f92ea327, paras 1, 4] It aimed to have local law in place by 2026 and first data exchanges from 2028. [S:ea81f92ea327, paras 1, 4] It committed to two-way exchanges, and only with partners that protect data. [S:ea81f92ea327, paras 1, 4]
- The December 2025 consultation paper proposed amending Hong Kong's main tax law, the Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112). [S:252a7f86684e, paras 4, 7] The changes covered both CARF and the amended CRS. [S:252a7f86684e, paras 4, 7] Comments closed on 6 February 2026. [S:252a7f86684e, paras 4, 7]
- The consultation described CARF and the amended CRS as finalised global standards. [S:275d5cc93a88, para 8, PDF p.8 (printed p.4)] It asked for views only on choices for putting them in place locally. [S:275d5cc93a88, para 8, PDF p.8 (printed p.4)]
- The bill appeared in the Gazette on 22 May 2026. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, Overview] It went to LegCo for its First Reading (the formal first step in LegCo) on 3 June 2026. [S:d5097f447cf9, para 1] LegCo's notice for that sitting said the Second Reading debate would be adjourned (put off to a later date). [S:d5097f447cf9, para 1]
- If passed, Part 2 of the bill (CARF) would start on 1 January 2027, and Part 3 (amended CRS) on 1 January 2028. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, Clause 1(2)-(4)] The rest would start on the day the new law is published in the Gazette. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, Clause 1(2)-(4)]
- The bill defines an RCASP as any individual or entity that, as a business, carries out crypto exchange transactions for customers. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.50M "reporting crypto-asset service provider"] This covers acting as the other side of the trade, acting as a broker, or running a trading venue. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.50M "reporting crypto-asset service provider"]
- Under the bill, an RCASP with any of the following Hong Kong links would be a Hong Kong RCASP (HKRCASP): [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.50N(1)-(2)]
  - it is tax resident in Hong Kong;
  - it is set up under Hong Kong law, and is either a legal person or a tax-return filer with the IRD;
  - it is managed from Hong Kong;
  - it has a regular place of business in Hong Kong;
  - it carries out the relevant transactions through a Hong Kong branch.
- The bill would require an HKRCASP to register with the Commissioner of Inland Revenue (the head of the IRD). [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.50O(1)-(2)] The deadline is 31 January of the year after it first meets a Hong Kong link test (a "nexus" test). [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.50O(1)-(2)]
- CARF covers three kinds of reportable transaction: crypto-to-fiat exchanges (crypto for ordinary money), crypto-to-crypto exchanges, and transfers. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, 'Scope of crypto-assets covered' and 'Transactions subject to reporting'] Central bank digital currencies (CBDCs) and specified electronic money products (certain digital forms of ordinary money) are outside CARF. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, 'Scope of crypto-assets covered' and 'Transactions subject to reporting']
- RCASPs would have to get a tax-residence self-certification from each new customer and check that it is reasonable. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, 'Due diligence requirements'] A self-certification is the customer's own statement of where they are tax resident. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, 'Due diligence requirements'] For existing users, they would have 12 months after the rules start. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, 'Due diligence requirements']
- The bill proposes that records be kept for six years after the related return's due date. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, 'Record keeping requirements'] If a former RCASP entity is dissolved (closed down), its last directors would have to make sure the records are still kept. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, 'Record keeping requirements']
- An HKRCASP would commit an offence if it failed, without reasonable excuse, to register, do due diligence or file a return. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.80R(1)-(3)] On conviction, the fine would be at level 3 (a band on Hong Kong's standard scale of fines). [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.80R(1)-(3)] Using a service provider would not, on its own, be a reasonable excuse. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.80R(1)-(3)]
- Extra fines would apply. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.80R(4)-(5)] A registration, return or notice failure would cost a further HK$500 a day while it continues after conviction. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.80R(4)-(5)] A due-diligence breach could instead bring a fine of HK$1,000 per affected user or controlling person. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.80R(4)-(5)] This applies if that total is higher than the level 3 fine. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.80R(4)-(5)] A controlling person is someone who controls a customer that is an entity.
- The bill also proposes a financial penalty, set by the Commissioner, in place of prosecution. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, 'Penalty provisions'] The firm could make its case in writing and appeal to the Board of Review (an independent tax appeals body). [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, 'Penalty provisions']; [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, ss.82E-82F]
- Under the amended CRS, CBDCs and specified electronic money products join the "depository account" category (the CRS term for deposit-type accounts). [S:275d5cc93a88, paras 4.3-4.5] Derivatives that reference crypto-assets become financial assets. [S:275d5cc93a88, paras 4.3-4.5] Crypto-assets become eligible investments for investment entities, such as funds. [S:275d5cc93a88, paras 4.3-4.5]
- The consultation covered entities that are both a CRS reporting financial institution and an RCASP. [S:275d5cc93a88, paras 4.14-4.17] It proposed that they report crypto sale or redemption proceeds under both regimes, not once. [S:275d5cc93a88, paras 4.14-4.17]
- The government's Policy Statement 2.0 on digital assets said it would propose a change to profits tax concessions. [S:a29b51bffc6b, para 15] The change was to add specified digital assets to the qualifying transactions for privately offered funds and FIHVs. [S:a29b51bffc6b, para 15] It was to take effect from the 2025/26 year of assessment, if LegCo approves. [S:a29b51bffc6b, para 15]
- The 2026-27 Budget said a bill was due in the first half of 2026. [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 98] That bill would class digital assets as qualifying investments for these concessions. [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 98] The target is the 2025/26 year of assessment. [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 98]

## What your bank must do

These duties bind only once the bill passes and takes effect. The bill is not yet law.

**Obligations**
- [ ] Map whether any group entity carries out crypto exchange transactions for customers as a business. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.50M] Include acting as a go-between. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.50M]
- [ ] Test each such entity, including branches, against the Hong Kong link (nexus) rules. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.50N(1)-(2)]
- [ ] Plan to register by 31 January of the year after the entity first meets a nexus test. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.50O(2)]
- [ ] Plan for due diligence from 1 January 2027. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, Clause 1(3)] Collect self-certifications from existing users within 12 months. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, 'Due diligence requirements']
- [ ] Prepare CRS systems for amended CRS due diligence from 1 January 2028. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, Clause 1(4)]; [S:275d5cc93a88, para 4.18]

**Controls & monitoring**
- [ ] Keep CARF due-diligence evidence and reporting records for six years after each return's due date. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, 'Record keeping requirements']
- [ ] Keep oversight of any outsourced CARF work. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.80R(2)] Under the bill, using a service provider would not in itself be a reasonable excuse. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.80R(2)]
- [ ] Plan to send test data files to the IRD for checking if the bank uses its own in-house software. [S:275d5cc93a88, Chapter 6 item (1)(c)] The consultation's timetable set the fourth quarter of 2027 for this testing. [S:275d5cc93a88, Chapter 6 item (1)(c)]

**Notify / consult HKMA or SFC**
- [ ] Note that CARF registration and returns would go to the IRD, not to the HKMA or SFC. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, 'Reporting portal and mandatory registration requirement'] The IRD's planned CARF Portal is the channel for them. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, 'Reporting portal and mandatory registration requirement'] Watch for the portal and the data schema (the technical format for the data). [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, 'Reporting portal and mandatory registration requirement']

**Counterparty due diligence**
- [ ] Note that a crypto trading platform or broker the bank partners with may itself be an RCASP with its own reporting duties. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, 'Individuals and entities subject to due diligence and reporting requirements']

## Talking points

**To the CCO**
- The CARF bill had its First Reading on 3 June 2026. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, Overview] If passed, CARF duties would start on 1 January 2027, and amended CRS duties on 1 January 2028. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, Overview]
- Using a vendor for CARF work is not, in itself, a reasonable excuse for failing to register, check customers or report. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.80R(2)]

**To business heads**
- Offering crypto exchange services to customers as a business could make an entity an RCASP. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.50M] That is true even when it only acts as a go-between. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.50M]
- New crypto customers will need to give a tax-residence self-certification. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, 'Due diligence requirements'] Existing customers will need to give one within 12 months of the start date. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, 'Due diligence requirements']

**To the CEO**
- Hong Kong committed to CARF in December 2024. [S:ea81f92ea327, para 4] It targets first data exchanges from 2028. [S:ea81f92ea327, para 4]
- The government linked CARF to Hong Kong's reputation as a financial centre. [S:ab980a841782, para 3]

**To Risk / CRO**
- Under the bill, fines could add up. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.80R(4)-(5)] A failure that continues after conviction could cost HK$500 a day. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.80R(4)-(5)] A due-diligence breach could instead cost HK$1,000 per affected user or controlling person. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.80R(4)-(5)]
- The consultation proposed that entities in both regimes report crypto proceeds under both CARF and CRS. [S:275d5cc93a88, para 4.17]

## Common mix-ups

- **Myth:** CARF is already law. **Fact:** CARF is in a bill before LegCo. The IRD says the dates apply only if the bill passes. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, Overview]
- **Myth:** Registration is due by 31 December of the year the link is first met. **Fact:** That date was the consultation's main proposal. [S:275d5cc93a88, Chapter 6 item (1)(b) and footnote 45] The bill sets 31 January of the year after the link is first met. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.50O(2)]
- **Myth:** Amended CRS starts in 2029. **Fact:** Its duties start on 1 January 2028. [S:275d5cc93a88, para 4.18]; [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, Clause 1(4)] The first exchange of amended CRS data is in 2029. [S:275d5cc93a88, para 4.18]
- **Myth:** CARF covers CBDCs and e-money. **Fact:** CARF leaves them out. The amended CRS brings them in instead. [S:275d5cc93a88, paras 1.5, 4.3]
- **Myth:** The HKMA or SFC supervises CARF. **Fact:** The IRD runs registration, returns and penalties. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, 'Reporting portal' and 'Penalty provisions']

## Read these first

1. **Inland Revenue (Amendment) (CARF and Amended CRS) Bill 2026** — LegCo / IRD, gazetted 22 May 2026. Read Clause 1 (start dates). Read ss.50M-50R (definitions, Hong Kong link, registration, due diligence, returns). Read ss.80R, 82E-82F (offences, financial penalty). This is the text that would become law. https://www.ird.gov.hk/eng/pdf/carf/Inland%20Revenue%20(Amendment)%20(Crypto-Asset%20Reporting%20Framework%20and%20Amended%20Common%20Reporting%20Standard)%20Bill%202026(eng).pdf
2. **IRD: Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework page** — IRD. Read the Overview and the sections on the Hong Kong link, due diligence, registration and penalties. It sums up the bill's proposals in plain language. https://www.ird.gov.hk/eng/tax/dta_carf.htm
3. **FSTB/IRD consultation paper on implementing CARF and amending CRS** — FSTB/IRD, 9 Dec 2025. Read paras 4.3-4.18 (amended CRS and dual reporting). Read Chapter 6 (timeline). It sets out the CRS changes that matter to banks. https://www.gov.hk/en/residents/government/publication/consultation/docs/2026/crypto-framework.pdf

## Open items

- The documents reviewed for this guide do not record the CARF bill passing as of 25 September 2026. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, Overview]; [S:d5097f447cf9, para 1]
- The consultation also proposed compulsory CRS registration for all reporting financial institutions (RFIs) from January 2027. [S:275d5cc93a88, paras 5.3, 5.9-5.12, 5.15, Chapter 6 item (2)(a)] It also proposed heavier CRS penalties. [S:275d5cc93a88, paras 5.3, 5.9-5.12, 5.15, Chapter 6 item (2)(a)] The bill's list of provisions in the documents reviewed shows no registration clause for RFIs. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, Contents] The documents do not say whether that proposal moved to other legislation.
- The IRD page does not say whether the final bill keeps the proposed default of reporting under both regimes.
- The IRD page says two lists will come in due course: reportable jurisdictions and partner jurisdictions. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, 'Lists of reportable jurisdictions' and 'Reporting portal'] The CARF Portal and the data schema will also come in due course. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, 'Lists of reportable jurisdictions' and 'Reporting portal']
- Concessions for funds and FIHVs: the 2026 Policy Address says a bill easing taxes has already passed. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 40] That bill covers fund vehicles, single-family offices and people who earn carried interest (fund managers' share of profits). [S:ef3648ff1610, para 40] No document reviewed for this guide has a bill text confirming how the enacted law treats digital assets.
- The documents reviewed do not say whether tokenised deposits (bank deposits recorded as digital tokens) count as specified electronic money products for CRS.

## Related modules

[A1](#m-A1), [A3](#m-A3), [C1](#m-C1), [C5](#m-C5), [D3](#m-D3), [E1](#m-E1), [E3](#m-E3)

title: What's coming: the pipeline
md:
This module is for the bank's Head of Compliance (digital assets). After reading it, you can list what is still coming in Hong Kong digital assets. You can say how far along each item is. You can also quote the targets that the government and regulators have stated, and only those.

## In 60 seconds

Four new licensing regimes for virtual asset (VA) services are coming. They cover dealing, custody (holding assets for clients), advisory and management. [S:4a0342268bf2, paras 2, 4] All four now have consultation conclusions (the published outcome of a public consultation). [S:ff3df4326e0f, para 2]; [S:4a0342268bf2, para 3] The government says one bill for all four will go to the Legislative Council (LegCo) in 2026. [S:4a0342268bf2, para 3]; [S:c6df52e680de, Reply part (3)]

An earlier plan proposed an over-the-counter (OTC) licence, run by Customs, for firms that trade virtual assets directly with customers. [S:27d27650e820, paras 1.1, 1.10] That plan was revised into a wider dealing proposal under Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) licensing. [S:27d27650e820, paras 1.1, 1.10]

For trading platforms, the SFC has set out three things:

- a framework for licensed platforms to propose perpetual contracts for professional investors. [S:089ec86e2407, para 3] Perpetual contracts are derivatives with no expiry date. Professional investors are institutions and wealthy investors who meet legal thresholds.
- a pilot for secondary trading (buying and selling after first issue) of tokenised funds (fund units recorded as digital tokens). [S:bbd10edd41cf, paras 1-2]
- standards for platforms dealing in stablecoins from issuers licensed by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA). [S:19d52ade6849, paras 2, 4-5] Stablecoins are tokens designed to hold a steady value against a currency.

The 2026 Policy Address sets three dated plans for market infrastructure. [S:ef3648ff1610, paras 35(ii), 35(iv), 50] The HKMA plans two upgrades to EnsembleTX (its project for settling tokenised deposits between banks) by around end-2026. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 50] Tokenised deposits are bank deposits recorded as digital tokens. The upgrades are settlement in central bank money (money held at the central bank) and 24/7 operation. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 50] The HKMA will also test tokenised Exchange Fund Bills (short-term HKMA debt) by year-end. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(ii)] CMU OmniClear (the company that runs the Central Moneymarkets Unit (CMU) bond settlement system) is to set up a digital asset platform in 2026. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(iv)]

The Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF) is a tax reporting standard for crypto-assets. A bill sets 1 January 2027 as the start date for its CARF rules. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, Clause 1(3)] The bill is before LegCo. [S:d5097f447cf9, para 1] Customs plans digital-asset analytics systems by 2029. [S:ef3648ff1610, Annex (I) New Indicators, item 209]

## Status board

As of 25 September 2026. Dates are as stated in each source. Targets are the government's or the regulator's own words. They are not forecasts.

Abbreviations and terms in this table:

- FSTB = Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau
- CCE = Commissioner of Customs and Excise
- ATMs = automated teller machines
- AIs = authorized institutions (banks under the Banking Ordinance)
- LCs = licensed corporations (firms licensed by the SFC)
- VATP = VA trading platform; VATPs = VA trading platforms
- RI = registered institution (a bank registered with the SFC); RIs = registered institutions
- Policy Address = the Chief Executive's yearly policy speech
- e-HKD = a digital form of the Hong Kong dollar
- HKEX = Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing
- CrypTech = an SFC technology initiative with market and anti-money laundering surveillance parts
- RCASP = Reporting Crypto-Asset Service Provider (a firm with reporting duties under CARF); RCASPs = more than one RCASP
- CRS = Common Reporting Standard (the existing tax reporting standard for financial accounts)
- C&ED = Customs and Excise Department
- AML = anti-money laundering
- DATAS = Digital Asset Transaction Analytics System
- AMLAS = AML Analytics System
- FATF = Financial Action Task Force (the global standard setter against money laundering)
- VASP = VA service provider; VASPs = VA service providers
- DeFi = decentralised finance (financial services run by software on blockchains)

| Instrument | Issuer | Date | Status (chip) | Applies to | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| VA OTC licensing by CCE | FSTB | 8 Feb 2024 | Superseded | VA OTC shops, ATMs and online platforms (AIs, LCs, VATPs proposed exempt) | [S:efcdb0ae3849, paras 2.6, 2.23]; [S:27d27650e820, paras 1.1, 1.9] |
| VA dealing + VA custodian regimes | FSTB + SFC | Consulted 27 Jun 2025; conclusions 24 Dec 2025 | Conclusions published | Dealers, custodians; banks register, HKMA is frontline regulator | [S:7395a53cc85a, paras 1, 4]; [S:ff3df4326e0f, para 2] |
| VA advisory + VA management regimes | FSTB + SFC | Consulted 24 Dec 2025; conclusions 26 May 2026 | Conclusions published | Advisers, managers; only banks may register | [S:4a0342268bf2, paras 1-3]; [S:6186c01c6649, fns 9-10] |
| Single bill for the four regimes | Government + SFC | This year (stated 24 Jun 2026) | Stated target | As above | [S:c6df52e680de, Reply part (3)] |
| VATP perpetual contracts framework | SFC | 11 Feb 2026 | Issued; VATPs submit proposals to SFC | Licensed VATPs; professional investors only | [S:089ec86e2407, para 3]; [S:49f642bdee28, 'Background'; 'Eligible investors and reference assets'] |
| Secondary trading of tokenised SFC-authorised products | SFC | 20 Apr 2026 | Issued (pilot framework) | Product issuers, intermediaries incl. VATPs | [S:bbd10edd41cf, paras 1-2, 7] |
| Tokenised gold and other real-world-asset products on licensed platforms | SFC (per Policy Address) | 16 Sep 2026 | Stated target | VATPs, product issuers | [S:ef3648ff1610, para 49(ii)] |
| Relevant (HKMA-licensed issuer) stablecoins on VATPs | SFC | 27 May 2026 | Issued | VATPs, LCs (RIs via HKMA circular) | [S:19d52ade6849, paras 2, 4-5, fn 2] |

| Tokenised Exchange Fund Bills operational tests | HKMA | By end-2026 | Stated target | Banks | [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(ii)] |
| CMU OmniClear digital asset platform | CMU OmniClear | 2026 | Stated target | Digital bond issuance and settlement | [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 114]; [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(iv)] |

## Key facts

- The February 2024 OTC proposal would have created a licence run by the CCE. [S:efcdb0ae3849, paras 2.6, 2.23] The licence was for businesses offering spot trading of virtual assets (VAs), meaning buying and selling for immediate delivery. [S:efcdb0ae3849, paras 2.6, 2.23] Banks and other firms regulated by the SFC or the HKMA were proposed to be exempt. [S:efcdb0ae3849, paras 2.6, 2.23]
- The June 2025 dealing paper widened that plan. [S:27d27650e820, paras 1.1, 1.8-1.10] It proposed covering simple conversions (one VA for another, or for ordinary money). [S:27d27650e820, paras 1.1, 1.8-1.10] It also proposed covering more complex services, such as brokerage and block trading (large trades arranged privately). [S:27d27650e820, paras 1.1, 1.8-1.10] The reason was that the consultation found more varied business models. [S:27d27650e820, paras 1.1, 1.8-1.10]
- For dealing and custody, the SFC will be the standard setter (the body that writes the rules). [S:7395a53cc85a, para 4] The HKMA will be the frontline regulator (day-to-day supervisor) for registered banks and stored value facilities (licensed e-wallet and prepaid card operators). [S:7395a53cc85a, para 4]
- The December 2025 conclusions align VA dealing with Type 1 (dealing in securities), an existing SFC licence type. [S:6186c01c6649, paras 3-5, 26] The SFC will require VA dealers to keep client VAs with VA custodians regulated by the SFC. [S:6186c01c6649, paras 3-5, 26]
- No arrangement is planned to let existing dealing or custody firms carry on while they apply. Each regime takes full effect on its start date. [S:6186c01c6649, paras 31, 35-36]; [S:f41a543388bc, paras 48, 51] A faster approval process is planned for two groups: [S:6186c01c6649, paras 31, 35-36]; [S:f41a543388bc, paras 48, 51]
  - VATPs, LCs and RIs already providing VA dealing.
  - VATP associated entities (the platform's group company that holds client assets) and banks already assessed for VA custody.
- Start dates are not set yet. [S:6186c01c6649, para 32] The government and the SFC will consider how long the market needs to adjust. [S:6186c01c6649, para 32]
- VA advisory will align with Type 4 (advising on securities). VA management will align with Type 9 (asset management). [S:4a0342268bf2, para 2] For these two services, only banks could register with the SFC instead of getting a licence. [S:6186c01c6649, fns 9-10]
- VA management will have no small-amount exception. [S:01c5c5c4045f, paras 32, 68] Some Type 9 firms now manage portfolios whose VA share is below the current threshold. [S:01c5c5c4045f, paras 32, 68] By the start date, these firms will need a licence or registration, or should wind down that business. [S:01c5c5c4045f, paras 32, 68]
- In June 2026, the government said the bill for all four regimes would go to LegCo that year. [S:c6df52e680de, Reply part (3)] The bill is to cover stablecoins, among other VAs. [S:c6df52e680de, Reply part (3)]
- Under the SFC framework, VATPs should offer perpetual contracts only to professional investors. [S:49f642bdee28, 'Eligible investors and reference assets'; 'Margin arrangements and loss allocation management'] Margin collateral (assets a client posts to back its trades) should be one of these: [S:49f642bdee28, 'Eligible investors and reference assets'; 'Margin arrangements and loss allocation management']
  - fiat money (ordinary government-issued currency)
  - stablecoins regulated by the HKMA
  - tokenised deposits regulated by the HKMA
- The first products under the SFC's tokenised-fund trading framework are expected to be tokenised money market funds (funds that hold short-term debt). [S:bbd10edd41cf, para 6] The SFC will then assess how they work before it considers a wider range of products. [S:bbd10edd41cf, para 6]
- Relevant Stablecoins are specified stablecoins from HKMA-licensed issuers. [S:19d52ade6849, preamble, para 2] For these coins, the SFC does not require VATPs and LCs to apply the retail liquidity and index requirements. [S:19d52ade6849, paras 4-5] Those are the tests a token normally has to pass before retail clients can trade it. [S:19d52ade6849, paras 4-5] Disclosures to clients should still cover two things: [S:19d52ade6849, paras 4-5]
  - the stabilisation mechanism (how the coin keeps its value steady)
  - the redemption arrangements (how holders swap coins back for money)
- At first, EnsembleTX settles transfers of tokenised deposits between banks through the Hong Kong dollar (HKD) real-time gross settlement (RTGS) system. [S:8b67e8dc510f, para 3] RTGS means each payment settles in full, one by one, as it happens. Planned upgrades would move EnsembleTX to 24/7 settlement in tokenised central bank money. [S:8b67e8dc510f, para 3]
- The 2026 Policy Address says the HKMA will test tokenised Exchange Fund Bills by year-end. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(ii)] The aim is to help banks use the more than HK$1.3 trillion of these bills round the clock. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(ii)]
- The SFC plans to launch its system for monitoring digital-asset custody in the second half of 2026. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 51(iii)] The CrypTech market and AML surveillance components are to follow in 2027. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 51(iii)]
- C&ED plans to launch two systems by 2029: DATAS and AMLAS. [S:ef3648ff1610, Annex (I) New Indicators, item 209]
- At its June 2026 Plenary (full meeting), the FATF approved two papers for publication. [S:43fd79de14c1, section (3)(e)] One is a seventh targeted update on how countries apply its VA/VASP standards. The other is a DeFi report. [S:43fd79de14c1, section (3)(e)] Both are to be published in due course. [S:43fd79de14c1, section (3)(e)]

## What your bank must do

**Obligations**
- [ ] List your bank's current and planned VA dealing, custody, advisory and management activity. Firms now doing VA activities under SFC licence or registration conditions will need a licence or registration under the new regimes. [S:01c5c5c4045f, para 62]
- [ ] Plan for a fixed start date with no transition. No arrangement is planned to let existing firms carry on while they apply. [S:6186c01c6649, paras 31-32, 34] Dealers that have not contacted the SFC or HKMA may have to stop operating on that date. [S:6186c01c6649, paras 31-32, 34]
- [ ] Note the marketing ban that applies once the regimes are in force. Firms without a licence or registration will be prohibited from actively marketing VA advisory or management services to the Hong Kong public. [S:01c5c5c4045f, para 70]

**Controls & monitoring**
- [ ] Note the SFC's stated plan to launch its system for monitoring digital-asset custody in the second half of 2026. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 51(iii)]
- [ ] Track the CARF start date for any group company that may be an RCASP. The bill sets that date as 1 January 2027. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, Clause 1(3)]

**Notify / consult HKMA or SFC**
- [ ] Note that the regulators encourage firms interested in VA dealing to approach the SFC early, or the HKMA where relevant. [S:6186c01c6649, para 33] The aim is to begin pre-application talks (informal talks before a formal application). [S:6186c01c6649, para 33]
- [ ] Note that existing and would-be VA advisers and managers are strongly encouraged to start pre-application talks with the SFC early. [S:4a0342268bf2, para 7] This matters if your bank gives VA advice or manages VAs, or plans to.

**Counterparty due diligence**
- [ ] Under the dealing regime, check that the VA custodians holding client assets are regulated by the SFC. [S:6186c01c6649, para 26]
- [ ] Know the scope of the SFC's 27 May 2026 circular. It covers only Relevant Stablecoins. [S:19d52ade6849, preamble, para 2] These are specified stablecoins issued by an HKMA-licensed issuer and authorised under its licence. [S:19d52ade6849, preamble, para 2] The circular does not cover other stablecoins. [S:19d52ade6849, preamble, para 2]

## Talking points

**To the CCO**
- All four VA regimes for intermediaries now have conclusions, and one bill is targeted for 2026. [S:c6df52e680de, Reply part (3)] No arrangement is planned to let existing firms carry on while they apply. [S:6186c01c6649, para 31]; [S:01c5c5c4045f, para 63]
- For dealing and custody, banks register with the SFC, and the HKMA is their frontline regulator. [S:7395a53cc85a, para 4]; [S:27d27650e820, para 1.10]

**To business heads**
- VA management will have no small-amount exception. A manager will need a licence or registration even if VAs are only a small share of a portfolio. [S:01c5c5c4045f, paras 32, 68]
- Under the SFC framework, VATP perpetual contracts may take HKMA-regulated tokenised deposits as margin collateral. [S:49f642bdee28, 'Margin arrangements and loss allocation management']

**To the CEO**
- The HKMA plans central bank money settlement and 24/7 operation for EnsembleTX by around end-2026. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 50]
- CMU OmniClear is to set up a digital asset platform in 2026 for issuing and settling digital bonds. [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 114]

**To Risk / CRO**
- C&ED aims to launch its digital-asset transaction analytics system, DATAS, by 2029. [S:ef3648ff1610, Annex (I) New Indicators, item 209]
- The FATF's next VA/VASP update and its DeFi report are approved but not yet published. [S:43fd79de14c1, section (3)(e)]

## Common mix-ups

- **Myth:** The Customs OTC licence is still coming. **Fact:** The 2025 dealing proposal revised that plan. It put VA dealing under SFC licensing instead. [S:27d27650e820, paras 1.1, 1.9-1.10]
- **Myth:** Conclusions mean the regimes are law. **Fact:** A bill is still to be introduced. [S:c6df52e680de, Reply part (3)] Start dates are not set. [S:6186c01c6649, para 32]
- **Myth:** Retail clients can trade VATP perpetual contracts. **Fact:** Under the SFC framework, only professional investors should be offered them. [S:49f642bdee28, 'Eligible investors and reference assets']
- **Myth:** VA dealers will have the same custodian choice as VA managers. **Fact:** Dealers will have to use custodians regulated by the SFC. [S:6186c01c6649, para 26] Private funds managed by VA managers, by contrast, keep the flexibility to appoint qualified custodians anywhere in the world. [S:01c5c5c4045f, para 56]
- **Myth:** Policy Address items are rules with legal force. **Fact:** They are stated plans. The Policy Address says what the SFC and HKMA will do or are planning to do. [S:ef3648ff1610, paras 49-51]

## Read these first

1. **Consultation Conclusions on VA dealing and further consultation on VA advisory/management** — FSTB + SFC, 24 Dec 2025. Read paras 3-5, 26, 29-36 and footnotes 9-10. They cover the core design, the custody rule, the transition and bank registration. https://apps.sfc.hk/edistributionWeb/gateway/EN/consultation/doc?refNo=25CP12
2. **Consultation Conclusions: VA advisory and VA management** — FSTB + SFC, 26 May 2026. Read paras 6-12, 32, 56-57 and 62-70. They cover scope, the lack of a small-amount exception, custody choice and start dates. https://www.fstb.gov.hk/fsb/en/publication/consult/doc/VASPVAMSP_consultation_conclusion_e.pdf
3. **The Chief Executive's 2026 Policy Address** — Hong Kong Government, 16 Sep 2026. Read paras 35-36, 49-51 and 99, and Annex (I) New Indicators, item 209. This is the latest official list of stated targets. https://www.policyaddress.gov.hk/2026/public/pdf/policy/policy-full_en.pdf

## Open items

- As of 25 September 2026, the documents reviewed for this guide include no bill text for the four VA regimes.
- Start dates for the VA regimes are not set. [S:6186c01c6649, para 32]; [S:01c5c5c4045f, para 64]
- The SFC intends to align custodian requirements with those now applied to SFC-licensed VATPs. [S:f41a543388bc, para 38] It will look at a flexible approach to custody technology and storage ratios (how much client VA is kept offline versus online). [S:f41a543388bc, para 38] The detailed requirements are not in the documents reviewed for this guide.
- The CARF bill was introduced into LegCo on 3 June 2026. [S:d5097f447cf9, para 1] The Second Reading debate (where LegCo debates the bill's main principles) was adjourned. [S:d5097f447cf9, para 1] The documents reviewed for this guide do not record whether the bill has passed.
- The FATF seventh targeted update and DeFi report were not yet published as of the SFC circular of 14 July 2026. [S:43fd79de14c1, section (3)(e)]

## Related modules

[A1](#m-A1), [A3](#m-A3), [C1](#m-C1), [C2](#m-C2), [C3](#m-C3), [C5](#m-C5), [D5](#m-D5), [E2](#m-E2), [E3](#m-E3)

title: Wholesale money, CBDC and cross-border projects
md:
Central bank digital currency (CBDC) is money that a central bank issues in digital form. This module explains the CBDC work of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA). It runs from the digital Hong Kong dollar (e-HKD) to the mBridge and Ensemble projects. The module is for the bank's Head of Compliance (digital assets). After it, you can say what compliance role the published designs give to banks.

## In 60 seconds

The HKMA has worked on the e-HKD since 2017. [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'e-HKD for financial institutions' section] Its first projects looked at wholesale use: money that moves only between banks and other financial institutions. [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'e-HKD for financial institutions' section] It ran two rounds of market consultation on a retail e-HKD (one for the public) in 2021-2022. [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'HKMA's Policy Stance on e-HKD used in retail applications' and 'e-HKD Pilot Programme Phase 1' and 'Phase 2' sections] It also ran two industry pilot phases in 2023-2025. [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'HKMA's Policy Stance on e-HKD used in retail applications' and 'e-HKD Pilot Programme Phase 1' and 'Phase 2' sections] In October 2025 the HKMA said it would prioritise wholesale uses. [S:6bd9e65817c4, para 4] It has not yet decided whether or when to introduce a retail e-HKD. [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Policy Stance and Three-Rail Approach']

Its cross-border work started with Project Inthanon-LionRock (a joint project with the Bank of Thailand). That project grew into mBridge, a multi-CBDC platform. A multi-CBDC platform is one shared system where several central banks' digital currencies can move. [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Project Inthanon-LionRock' section] The mBridge platform reached minimum viable product (MVP) stage, meaning a first working version, in June 2024. [S:db56d97e2206, para 1]

Project Ensemble explores how banks settle tokenised deposits with each other. A tokenised deposit is an ordinary bank deposit recorded as a digital token. [S:8b67e8dc510f, paras 1 and 3] EnsembleTX — the pilot phase — first settles these payments through Hong Kong's Real Time Gross Settlement (RTGS) system for HKD. [S:8b67e8dc510f, paras 1 and 3] RTGS settles each payment between banks one by one, as it happens. EnsembleTX is to move in stages to tokenised central bank money. [S:8b67e8dc510f, paras 1 and 3] Ensemble has tie-ups with the central banks of France, Thailand and Brazil. [S:0ed273d6f63f, paras 2-3; S:aabff1db2350, paras 1 and 3; S:8d9f12b43ada, para 1] It also has a memorandum of understanding (MoU), a formal cooperation agreement, with Shanghai bodies. [S:eb28508e5032, para 2]

In the mBridge designs, each bank runs its own anti-money laundering (AML), know-your-customer (KYC) and sanctions checks. [S:947fa49606ab, s.6.5.2, p.30; S:89b8fcadfaa8, p.3] Each bank runs these checks off the platform, in its own systems. [S:947fa49606ab, s.6.5.2, p.30; S:89b8fcadfaa8, p.3]

## Status board

As of 25 September 2026.

Also the Bank for International Settlements (BIS) Innovation Hub (BISIH) Hong Kong Centre. Saudi Central Bank joined the MVP platform. | MVP 5 Jun 2024 | Pilot | Participating banks | [S:db56d97e2206, paras 1 and 3, fn 1] [S:2ffb8727bb2f, Reply (4)] |
