## Key facts

- The HKMA's e-HKD work began in 2017 with Project LionRock. [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'e-HKD for financial institutions' section] LionRock was a proof of concept, meaning a small test of whether an idea works. It involved the three note-issuing banks (the banks that issue Hong Kong banknotes) and Hong Kong Interbank Clearing Limited. [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'e-HKD for financial institutions' section]
- In October 2021 an HKMA technical paper proposed a two-tier design. [S:59a20457a2fc, Executive Summary points 3-4] Under it, the central bank issues e-HKD and banks distribute it. [S:59a20457a2fc, Executive Summary points 3-4] The paper said this design was not a blueprint. [S:59a20457a2fc, Executive Summary points 3-4]
- The April 2022 policy paper noted that full anonymity is generally not seen as workable for a CBDC. [S:3b42966a786e, Section 5.3, p.34] The reason given was anti-money laundering and counter-financing of terrorism (AML/CFT) duties. [S:3b42966a786e, Section 5.3, p.34] The paper pointed to tiered wallets as a common approach. Tiered wallets have limits that rise as the user passes more identity checks. [S:3b42966a786e, Section 5.3, p.34]
- In September 2022 the HKMA set out a three-rail approach, meaning three parallel work streams. [S:35cb94c89a11, Rail 1 section, p.10] It said early legal research suggested existing law was not adequate to issue a digital legal tender with enough certainty. [S:35cb94c89a11, Rail 1 section, p.10] Legal tender is money the law recognises for paying debts.
- Phase 1 of the pilot had 16 firms running 14 pilots. [S:9f8886b0fb21, Executive Summary, p.6; s.3.1, p.11] It found possible value in three features. [S:9f8886b0fb21, Executive Summary, p.6; s.3.1, p.11]
  - Programmability: rules built into the money about when and how it moves.
  - Tokenisation: recording money or assets as digital tokens.
  - Atomic settlement: both sides of a deal settle at the same instant, or neither does.
- In September 2024 the project became Project e-HKD+. It covers both e-HKD and tokenised deposits. [S:2f93aa2b9560, paras 1-2] Phase 2 ran 11 pilot groups. [S:2f93aa2b9560, paras 1-2]
- On 28 October 2025 the HKMA made wholesale payments the priority for future e-HKD work, ahead of retail use. [S:6bd9e65817c4, para 4]
- The HKMA's September 2026 CBDC page says it has not yet decided if, or when, it would introduce an e-HKD. [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Policy Stance and Three-Rail Approach']
- Inthanon-LionRock ran in Q4 2019. [S:6b0fae230518, para 1 and fn 1] In February 2021 the PBoC DCI and the Central Bank of the UAE joined. [S:6b0fae230518, para 1 and fn 1] The project was then renamed the m-CBDC Bridge (multiple-CBDC Bridge). [S:6b0fae230518, para 1 and fn 1]
- The HKMA page says the BISIH Hong Kong Centre gave 'strong support' as the project became mBridge. [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Project Inthanon-LionRock' section]
- In the 2022 mBridge pilot, 20 banks in four jurisdictions made more than 160 payments and foreign exchange trades. [S:947fa49606ab, s.1 Executive Summary, p.4] These were worth over US$22 million in total. [S:947fa49606ab, s.1 Executive Summary, p.4]
- At MVP in June 2024, the listed project team was the HKMA, BoT, PBoC DCI, CBUAE and BISIH Hong Kong Centre. [S:db56d97e2206, fn 1, para 3] The Saudi Central Bank was welcomed as the next full participant. [S:db56d97e2206, fn 1, para 3]
- In October 2025 the Government told the Legislative Council that mBridge had become part of Hong Kong's financial market infrastructure. [S:2ffb8727bb2f, Reply (4)] It also said participating Hong Kong banks set their own fees. [S:2ffb8727bb2f, Reply (4)]
- Project Aurum built a two-tier test version: a wholesale system between banks, plus retail wallets. [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Collaborative Projects'] Project Sela tested a different design. Private go-between firms, called access enablers, connect directly to the central bank's CBDC ledger. [S:f9000467b0ee, s.1 Introduction, p.7]
- Project Ensemble explores settling tokenised money between banks, using the e-HKD as a wholesale CBDC. [S:5a9cad53f2be, para 2] A wholesale CBDC is central bank digital money used only by banks and other financial institutions. Ensemble starts with tokenised deposits. [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Project Ensemble' section]
- The Government's November 2025 digital green bonds had HKD and renminbi (RMB) tranches, or portions. [S:ac6cd085a325, 'Integration of digital money in the settlement process' item] Those tranches had an option to settle in tokenised central bank money, alongside traditional payment systems. [S:ac6cd085a325, 'Integration of digital money in the settlement process' item] The Government called it the world's first digital bond offering to use e-CNY and e-HKD in settlement. [S:ac6cd085a325, 'Integration of digital money in the settlement process' item]
- Tier-4 personal e-CNY wallets for Hong Kong residents cap balances at RMB 10,000. [S:08caafe0cfe7, Annex 2] They allow retail payments only, not person-to-person transfers. [S:08caafe0cfe7, Annex 2]
- By end-January 2026, about 80,000 e-CNY wallets had been registered with Hong Kong mobile numbers. [S:062b0a1547b9, Reply (1)] In addition, 18 local banks let users top up these wallets through the FPS. [S:062b0a1547b9, Reply (1)]

## What your bank must do

These are pilot and research designs, not binding rules. Neither the HKMA nor the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) has made them rules. The lines below show what the published designs expect of participating banks.

**Obligations**
- [ ] On mBridge, run AML, counter-terrorist financing (CTF) and sanctions checks off the platform before sending a payment. [S:947fa49606ab, s.6.5.2, p.30] The receiving bank runs its own check before confirming the payment. [S:947fa49606ab, s.6.5.2, p.30]
- [ ] On mBridge, meet each jurisdiction's AML, CTF and sanctions laws. [S:947fa49606ab, s.7.2(d), p.35] The platform attaches a pass or fail certificate to each transaction, based on the bank's own off-platform check. [S:947fa49606ab, s.7.2(d), p.35]

**Controls & monitoring**
- [ ] Keep KYC, AML and CTF checks in the bank's own systems, outside the mBridge platform ("off-bridge"). [S:89b8fcadfaa8, p.3]
- [ ] If the bank takes a role in distributing e-HKD, note the 2022 policy paper. [S:3b42966a786e, Section 5.4, p.35] It said a two-tier design could give customer-facing institutions two tasks: customer due diligence (checking who customers are) and record-keeping. [S:3b42966a786e, Section 5.4, p.35]

**Notify / consult HKMA or SFC**
- [ ] Banks may use the HKMA Supervisory Incubator for distributed ledger technology (DLT). [S:1b1a0de5de5a, paras 2-3] DLT is a shared record kept in step across many parties. The Incubator lets banks reaffirm their risk controls before a full DLT launch. [S:1b1a0de5de5a, paras 2-3] Tokenised deposits are a core focus. [S:1b1a0de5de5a, paras 2-3]

**Counterparty due diligence**
- [ ] On mBridge, foreign banks can hold and use a CBDC. [S:947fa49606ab, s.7.1.1, pp.31-32] Only domestic banks can swap their reserves at the central bank for that CBDC, or swap it back. [S:947fa49606ab, s.7.1.1, pp.31-32] Check which role each counterparty has.

## Talking points

**To the Chief Compliance Officer (CCO)**
- mBridge leaves AML and sanctions screening to each bank, off the platform. [S:947fa49606ab, s.6.5.2, p.30]
- The 2022 e-HKD policy paper said a two-tier design could task customer-facing institutions with customer due diligence. [S:3b42966a786e, Section 5.4, p.35]

**To business heads**
- The HKMA's e-HKD focus is now wholesale payments, to support tokenisation and cross-border payments. [S:6bd9e65817c4, para 4]
- In Phase 2, commercial banks leaned slightly towards tokenised deposits over e-HKD. [S:bdefe7fc69d4, Executive Summary, p.2]

**To the Chief Executive Officer (CEO)**
- mBridge reached MVP in June 2024. [S:db56d97e2206, para 1] The Government calls it part of Hong Kong's financial market infrastructure. [S:2ffb8727bb2f, Reply (4)]
- The HKMA has not decided to issue a retail e-HKD. [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Policy Stance and Three-Rail Approach']

**To Risk / Chief Risk Officer (CRO)**
- The 2022 mBridge pilot ran on one central cloud system in Hong Kong. [S:947fa49606ab, s.5.1, p.16; s.7.1.3, p.33] The pilot report said holding the data in a single cloud raised privacy concerns. [S:947fa49606ab, s.5.1, p.16; s.7.1.3, p.33]
- In Phase 2, privacy tools using zero-knowledge proofs were tested on public blockchains. A zero-knowledge proof shows a fact is true without revealing the data behind it. [S:bdefe7fc69d4, Section 4 'Privacy', p.30] These tools made transactions up to 320 times more costly in gas fees, the fees paid to process each transaction. [S:bdefe7fc69d4, Section 4 'Privacy', p.30]

## Common mix-ups

- **Myth:** Hong Kong is about to launch a retail e-HKD. **Fact:** The HKMA has made wholesale the priority. It has made no launch decision. [S:6bd9e65817c4, paras 4-5; S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Policy Stance and Three-Rail Approach']
- **Myth:** mBridge screens payments for sanctions. **Fact:** Each bank screens payments itself, off the platform. [S:947fa49606ab, s.6.5.2, p.30]
- **Myth:** Any bank can create any CBDC on mBridge. **Fact:** Only domestic banks can request issuance or redemption of their home CBDC. [S:89b8fcadfaa8, p.2]
- **Myth:** e-CNY wallets work like general-purpose wallets. **Fact:** They do not allow person-to-person transfers. [S:08caafe0cfe7, Annex 2 'Usage']
- **Myth:** Inthanon-LionRock and mBridge are different projects. **Fact:** mBridge is the renamed later phase of the same project. [S:3044ec37475a, Executive Summary, p.7]

## Read these first

1. **HKMA Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC) page** — HKMA, updated Sep 2026. Read the policy stance, mBridge, Ensemble and Collaborative Projects sections. This is the HKMA's own current summary. https://www.hkma.gov.hk/eng/key-functions/international-financial-centre/fintech/central-bank-digital-currency/
2. **Project mBridge: Connecting economies through CBDC** — pilot report, Oct 2022. Read s.6.4 (privacy) and s.6.5.2 (payments). Then read s.7.1 and s.7.2 (sovereignty, legal, AML and sanctions). This report gives the clearest statement of bank compliance duties on a CBDC platform. https://www.hkma.gov.hk/media/eng/doc/key-information/press-release/2022/20221026e3a1.pdf
3. **e-HKD Pilot Programme Phase 2 Report** — HKMA, 28 Oct 2025. Read the Executive Summary and Section 5 ('Path Forward'). It explains why the HKMA put wholesale use first. https://www.hkma.gov.hk/media/eng/doc/key-information/press-release/2025/20251028e4a1.pdf

## Open items

- No official Hong Kong document reviewed for this guide describes any change in BISIH's role in mBridge after June 2024. This module states BISIH's role only as of the 2024 MVP release and the HKMA's CBDC page.
- In October 2025 the HKMA said groundwork for a retail e-HKD would be finished in the first half of 2026. [S:6bd9e65817c4, para 5] Its September 2026 page says this preparation work is completed. [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'e-HKD for individuals and corporates' section] The page gives no launch decision. [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'e-HKD for individuals and corporates' section]
- The e-HKD Industry Forum's planned common token standards (shared technical rules for tokens) are not yet in the documents reviewed for this guide. [S:6bd9e65817c4, para 6]
- The HKMA and the PBoC have been working on upgrading e-CNY wallets and raising their limits. [S:2ffb8727bb2f, Reply (3) and (5); S:062b0a1547b9, Reply (2)] As of March 2026, this work had no finalised proposals or timetable. [S:2ffb8727bb2f, Reply (3) and (5); S:062b0a1547b9, Reply (2)]
- None of the documents reviewed for this guide gives outcomes of the BDF, BoT, BCB and Shanghai collaborations.

## Related modules

[A1](#m-A1), [C5](#m-C5), [E1](#m-E1), [E3](#m-E3)

title: Glossary and timeline
md:
This page is a quick reference for the bank's Head of Compliance (digital assets). Look up a term in plain English. Or see where any document sits in the 2017–2026 sequence. Every line gives its official source. As of 25 Sep 2026.

## How to use this page

Abbreviations used on this page:

- AI (AIs) = authorized institution(s)
- AML = anti-money laundering
- AMLO = Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance
- BIS = Bank for International Settlements
- CBDC = central bank digital currency
- CFT = counter-financing of terrorism
- CMU = Central Moneymarkets Unit
- CP = consultation paper
- DLT = distributed ledger technology (shared databases, such as blockchains)
- e-CNY = the digital renminbi
- e-HKD = a possible digital Hong Kong dollar
- FATF = Financial Action Task Force
- FSTB = Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau
- HKMA = Hong Kong Monetary Authority
- IRD = Inland Revenue Department
- KYC = know your customer (identity checks)
- LC (LCs) = licensed corporation(s)
- LegCo = Legislative Council
- ML/TF: ML = money laundering; TF = terrorist financing
- MoU = memorandum of understanding (a formal agreement to work together)
- OECD = Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development
- OTC = over the counter (trading directly with a dealer, not on an exchange)
- RI (RIs) = registered institution(s)
- SFC = Securities and Futures Commission
- SFO = Securities and Futures Ordinance
- VA (VAs) = virtual asset(s)
- VASP (VASPs) = virtual asset service provider(s)
- VATP (VATPs) = virtual asset trading platform(s)

How the page works:

- Part A defines about 80 terms. Each one points to the official document and paragraph that sets out the idea.
- Part B lists about 100 dated events from 2017 to September 2026. Each event is a fact about what was published or done. Targets appear only as the source states them.
- Dates are as the source gives them. If a source gives only a month or a year, so does this page.

## Part A: Glossary

**Institutions and legal status**

| Term | Plain definition | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Authorized Institution (AI) | A bank or other institution that the HKMA has authorised. The HKMA's anti-money laundering guideline (its AML/CFT Guideline) sets the standards AIs should meet, including AIs that are also RIs. The HKMA issues that guideline under s.7 of the AMLO and s.7(3) of the Banking Ordinance. | [S:7bfdad704174, paras 1.1, 1.3] |
| Registered Institution (RI) | An AI that the SFC has registered to carry on one or more regulated activities (types of securities business, such as dealing or advising). The HKMA supervises RIs day to day, as frontline supervisor. Ultimate responsibility stays with the SFC. | [S:8934af8cc884, paras 2.1.2, 2.1.3, 2.2.1] |
| Licensed corporation (LC) | A firm that the SFC has licensed to carry on regulated activities. The joint circulars cover LCs and RIs together, calling both 'intermediaries'. | [S:b79266f3da51, paras 4-6] |
| HKMA | The Hong Kong Monetary Authority, Hong Kong's banking regulator. Among its other roles, it grants licences to stablecoin issuers under the Stablecoins Ordinance. | [S:35e1ac2b815a, para 2]; [S:afb6cd0da6ff, para 1] |
| SFC | The Securities and Futures Commission, Hong Kong's securities regulator. It licenses VA trading platforms. The Government proposes that the SFC lead licensing and standard-setting for VA dealing and VA custody (safekeeping). | [S:2e5c35b38cc3, para 1]; [S:a29b51bffc6b, paras 5-6] |
| FSTB | The Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau, the government bureau for financial policy. It issued Policy Statement 2.0. It runs the VA licensing consultations jointly with the SFC. | [S:a29b51bffc6b, para 2]; [S:7395a53cc85a, para 1] |
| Frontline regulator | The body that supervises a firm day to day. This is the HKMA's proposed role for banks under the coming VA dealing and custody regimes. Under these regimes, the HKMA would supervise banks, while the SFC sets the standards. | [S:7395a53cc85a, para 4] |
| SB-1 | A chapter of the HKMA's Supervisory Policy Manual (its supervision handbook). It covers how the HKMA supervises RIs' regulated activities. It is a statutory guideline, issued under s.7(3) of the Banking Ordinance. | [S:8934af8cc884, p.1 'Purpose', 'Classification'] |
| Executive officer | A person who directly supervises a regulated activity at an RI. The RI appoints this person with the HKMA's written consent. Each activity needs at least two. | [S:8934af8cc884, paras 2.2.4, 4.3.9] |

**Virtual assets and platforms**

| Term | Plain definition | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Virtual asset (VA) | The legal term for crypto and similar digital tokens. The AMLO defines it in s.53ZRA. Policy Statement 2.0 (June 2025) says the Government will now say 'digital assets' instead. | [S:8a016a912528, footnote 1]; [S:a29b51bffc6b, footnote 1] |
| Digital asset (HKMA custody usage) | A broad term in the HKMA's custody guidance. It covers VAs, tokenised securities and other tokenised assets (assets recorded as digital tokens). It also covers the keys, seeds and backups (the secret codes that give access) used to reach those assets. | [S:ed61d7c335e7, footnote 1, p.1] |
| VASP | A business that provides VA services, such as trading or transfers, to customers. The HKMA expects banks to assess each VASP customer's ML/TF risk on its own facts. That assessment includes extra due diligence (deeper checks) where needed. | [S:642680fa4467, p.4, item (b)] |
| VATP | An online platform where people buy and sell VAs. In SFC usage, it is a company licensed under the SFO for Types 1 and 7 (dealing in securities, and automated trading services). A company holding an AMLO VA service licence also counts. | [S:19d52ade6849, footnote 1] |
| Deemed-to-be-licensed | A platform that may keep operating while the SFC decides its licence application. It was operating before 1 June 2023 and met the conditions for this status. It is not licensed and may never be. | [S:c787f990209d, Note 1, 'Reminder for investors', Note 2] |
| Non-contravention period | A grace period of 12 months, from 1 June 2023 to 31 May 2024. VATPs already running, with a genuine Hong Kong presence, could operate during it. Doing so did not breach the AMLO licensing rule. | [S:2e5c35b38cc3, para 6] |
| Associated Entity | A company that holds a VATP's client assets on trust (for the clients, not for itself). It is a Hong Kong subsidiary wholly owned by the VATP. It does no other business. | [S:f1bbafccd556, paras 1.1, 10.1] |
| Cold storage | Keeping the keys to VAs offline, away from the internet. The SFC expects VATPs to keep 98% of client VAs in cold storage. | [S:f1bbafccd556, para 10.6(c)] |
| Compensation arrangement | Cover that repays clients if their VAs are lost. A VATP should hold an SFC-approved arrangement of this kind. It should cover potential loss of 50% of client VAs in cold storage. It should also cover 100% of those in hot storage (kept online) and other storage. For bank custody, the HKMA's May 2026 guidance instead expects the bank to be liable to clients and to have adequate financial resources. | [S:f1bbafccd556, para 10.22]; [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(n)] |
| Professional investor | An institution, or a wealthy person or firm, that meets a legal test. The SFO defines the term in Schedule 1, Part 1, s.1. Any other person is a 'retail client'. | [S:19d52ade6849, footnote 4] |
| Complex product | An investment product whose terms and risks are hard for a typical investor to understand. It triggers the SFC's complex-product rules. These include a suitability check (whether the product fits the client), even if the firm did not solicit (actively offer) the sale. The joint circular says VA-related products are very likely complex. | [S:8a016a912528, paras 5-6.1] |
| Joint circular | A notice from the SFC and HKMA together on intermediaries' VA activities. The December 2023 version replaced the January 2022 and October 2023 versions. A supplement followed in September 2025. | [S:8a016a912528, note after para 3, p.1]; [S:b79266f3da51, para 1] |
| Staking | Locking a client's VAs into a proof-of-stake network to earn rewards. In such a network, holders who lock up tokens help check and confirm transactions. | [S:b79266f3da51, para 4] |
| Shared order book | One pool of buy and sell orders shared by an SFC-licensed VATP and an overseas platform in its group. Every order is fully pre-funded (paid for up front). Trades settle delivery-versus-payment: the asset and the payment change hands together. | [S:f009f1a6d615, paras 1, 3, 10, 13] |
| Perpetual contract | A contract that tracks a VA's price, uses leverage (borrowed exposure) and has no end date. Under the SFC's February 2026 framework, licensed VATPs may propose to offer them. They should be offered to professional investors only. | [S:49f642bdee28, 'Scope of application', 'Eligible investors and reference assets'] |
| Funding rate | Regular payments between the two sides of a perpetual contract. One side gains if the price rises (long) and the other if it falls (short). The payments keep the contract's price near the spot (current market) price. The SFC expects settlement at least once every 24 hours. | [S:49f642bdee28, 'Scope of application', 'Trading and settlement'] |
| Travel Rule (VA transfers) | The rule that sender and recipient details travel with a transfer. For banks, the HKMA Guideline sets customer due diligence (checks on the customer) for one-off VA transfers of HK$8,000 or more. It points to AMLO Schedule 2 s.13A. RIs must also take into account the VA parts of Chapter 12 of the SFC AML Guideline. | [S:7bfdad704174, para 4.2.1(b)(iii), fn 15; para 1.3, fn 1] |
| Unhosted wallet | A VA wallet (software or hardware) through which the owner holds and moves VAs, keeping the private key (the secret code that moves the VAs). The HKMA's May 2025 consultation proposed a check by licensed stablecoin issuers. They would check whether each customer's wallet is custodial (run by a provider) or unhosted. | [S:0d6e6d0253ff, footnote 4, paras 3.2.2-3.2.4] |
| Suspicious VATPs list | A public SFC list of suspicious trading platforms. It helps the public spot suspicious platforms doing business in Hong Kong. | [S:ea8889eb1fc4, item 2]; [S:dddd919625e9, para 3] |

**Coming VA regimes**

| Term | Plain definition | Source |
|---|---|---|
| VA dealing service | Dealing in VAs (buying and selling them) as a business. The June 2025 proposal covers this business in Hong Kong. It runs from simple conversion (swapping one asset for another) to brokerage and block trades (very large deals). Banks would register with the SFC, with the HKMA as frontline regulator. | [S:27d27650e820, para 1.10] |
| VA custodian service | Keeping VAs safe for others as a business. Under the December 2025 conclusions, it means holding, for others, the private keys or similar tools that can move VAs. Trustees or managers that only hand custody to someone else are out of scope. | [S:f41a543388bc, paras 6-8] |
| VA advisory / VA management | Advising clients on VAs, and managing VA portfolios for them. Both are proposed licensing regimes. Their scope will match the SFO regimes for advising on securities (Type 4) and asset management (Type 9). | [S:4a0342268bf2, para 2] |
| Deeming / grandfathering | Letting firms already in business carry on under a new regime, as if licensed, while they apply. None is planned for the VA dealing or VA custodian regimes. | [S:6186c01c6649, para 31]; [S:f41a543388bc, para 48] |
| Expedited approval | A faster route to approval. It is promised for SFC-licensed VATPs. It is also promised for LCs and RIs that already provide VA dealing services. | [S:6186c01c6649, paras 35-36] |
| MPC (multi-party computation) provider | A technology firm that splits control of a private key among several parties. Whether it needs a custodian licence depends on the facts of each case. The main tests are whether it can move client VAs on its own, and whether clients can always reach their assets independently. | [S:f41a543388bc, para 11] |
| VA OTC regime | A scheme to license OTC VA trading businesses. The February 2024 proposal was for the Commissioner of Customs and Excise to license spot VA trading (buying and selling for immediate delivery). The proposal also covered shops and crypto cash machines. The June 2025 dealing proposal revised the scheme. | [S:efcdb0ae3849, para 2.6]; [S:27d27650e820, para 1.1] |

**Stablecoins and bank capital**

| Term | Plain definition | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Stablecoins Ordinance (Cap. 656) | Hong Kong's stablecoin law. Stablecoins are tokens designed to hold a steady value. The law set up licensing for regulated stablecoin activities and came into force on 1 August 2025. | [S:0df2de5234dc, paras 1-2] |
| Fiat-referenced stablecoin (FRS) | A stablecoin whose value is tied to one or more fiat currencies (ordinary government-issued money). An HKMA licence is needed to issue one in Hong Kong as a business. A licence is also needed to issue one tied to the Hong Kong dollar as a business, in or outside Hong Kong. | [S:79b5b51a1a1b, p.4 'What to regulate']; [S:35e1ac2b815a, para 2] |
| Relevant Stablecoin | A stablecoin issued by an HKMA-licensed issuer under its licence. It is a 'specified stablecoin', a category set out in law. | [S:19d52ade6849, para 2] |
| Register of licensed stablecoin issuers | The HKMA's public list of licensed stablecoin issuers. The HKMA keeps it under s.21 of Cap. 656. | [S:270f1f7324ab, intro paragraph] |
| Stablecoin issuer sandbox | A controlled space where would-be stablecoin issuers could test their plans with the HKMA. The HKMA launched it in March 2024 to share its supervisory expectations. Admission was not an HKMA endorsement. Participants had to apply separately for a licence. | [S:f2a668eb3b93, Annex, Objectives] |
| Cryptoasset (capital rules) | In the bank capital rules, a digital form of value. It relies mainly on cryptography (code-based security) and DLT or similar technology. It can be used to pay, to invest, or to access goods or services. | [S:b7d630146e6c, para 1.2.1] |
| Group 1a / 1b | Classes of cryptoasset treated like the traditional asset behind them. Group 1a is tokenised traditional assets. Group 1b is stablecoins with effective stabilisation mechanisms (ways to keep the price steady). Both carry the same capital requirements as the underlying traditional asset. An infrastructure add-on (an extra charge for technology risk) may apply on top. | [S:b7d630146e6c, para 1.3.2] |
| Group 2a / 2b | Cryptoassets with the toughest capital treatment. They are unbacked cryptoassets, and tokenised assets or stablecoins that fail the classification conditions. They are fully capitalised: in effect, the bank holds capital equal to the whole exposure. Limited hedging (offsetting positions) is recognised for 2a, and none for 2b. | [S:b7d630146e6c, para 1.3.3] |
| CRP-1 | The HKMA's guidance on sorting cryptoassets into these groups. It is non-statutory (not issued under a law). If it differs from the Banking (Capital) Rules, the Rules prevail. | [S:b7d630146e6c, p.1 'Classification', para 1.1.4] |
| Negative vetting | LegCo's 28-day review of subsidiary legislation (detailed rules made under an existing law). The amendment rules on cryptoasset capital, disclosure and exposure limits completed this review in August 2025. | [S:974899bbef4d, p.1] |

**Tokenisation and digital money**

| Term | Plain definition | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Tokenised deposit | A commercial bank deposit in digital token form. The bank itself issues it. | [S:5a9cad53f2be, para 2]; [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Project Ensemble'] |
| Tokenised product (HKMA) | A digital token version of a real-world investment product, recorded on DLT. In HKMA usage, it covers products not regulated under the SFO, and excludes stablecoins. The sales rules for the underlying product generally apply to its tokenised form too. | [S:b2719f3dcb37, 'Coverage', fn 1; 'General principle', pp.1-2] |
| Tokenised security (SFC) | A traditional security, such as a share or bond, wrapped in a digital token. The SFC judges whether it is complex by looking through to the underlying security. | [S:a9aa06fbcc12, paras 23-24] |
| Cash token | A digital token that stands in for cash. In Project Evergreen, the CMU minted (created) each token as a claim on the HKMA for one Hong Kong dollar. | [S:a0b44be27c40, para 33] |
| Non-native issuance | A bond issued first in the normal way, then turned into tokens on a DLT platform. In Project Evergreen, the CMU made its book entries first. The investors' beneficial interests (ownership rights) were then recorded on the ledger. | [S:a0b44be27c40, paras 25-26] |
| CMU / CMU OmniClear | CMU: the Central Moneymarkets Unit, a bond settlement system. CMU OmniClear: the company that runs it for the HKMA. The HKMA owns the CMU. CMU OmniClear Limited is a wholly owned subsidiary of the Exchange Fund (Hong Kong's official reserves), set up in October 2024. | [S:d43a14fd959f, paras 1-3] |
| Digital Bond Grant Scheme | An HKMA grant for issuing digital bonds in Hong Kong. It pays up to HK$2.5 million per eligible digital bond issue. It is open for an initial three years from November 2024. | [S:633ce27d4f9b, paras 2-3] |
| Supervisory Incubator | An HKMA arrangement that lets banks check their DLT risk controls before a full launch. Banks can choose to run live trials. | [S:1b1a0de5de5a, paras 1, 3] |
| DLT | Distributed ledger technology: a database shared and copied across many computers, such as a blockchain. The HKMA's non-binding considerations expect an AI's board and senior management to take full responsibility for DLT risks. | [S:1884530ff235, Introduction; item 1] |
| CBDC / e-HKD | CBDC: central bank digital currency, meaning money a central bank issues in digital form. The e-HKD is the HKMA's possible digital Hong Kong dollar, for wholesale and retail uses. The HKMA currently gives priority to wholesale use (between banks and other financial institutions). | [S:d51dc8884c8a, introduction] |
| Wholesale CBDC (wCBDC) | Central bank digital money used for settlement between banks. It is the basis of Project Ensemble. | [S:5a9cad53f2be, paras 1-2] |
| Project e-HKD+ | The new name for Project e-HKD from September 2024. The project widened from the e-HKD alone to new forms of digital money, including tokenised deposits. | [S:2f93aa2b9560, para 1] |
| Three-rail approach | The HKMA's three-part path for the e-HKD. Rail 1 lays the foundations. Rail 2 covers use cases and pilots. Rail 3 covers implementation planning. | [S:d51dc8884c8a, 'Three-rail approach'] |
| Project Ensemble / EnsembleTX | Project Ensemble: HKMA work on settling deals in tokenised money. EnsembleTX: its pilot phase using real money, from November 2025. | [S:8b67e8dc510f, paras 1-2] |
| Ensemble Architecture Community | A group the HKMA formed in May 2024. Its members are regulators, banks and technology firms. It develops industry standards so that systems can work together (interoperability). | [S:0169bc8fbb4d, paras 1-3] |
| mBridge | A shared platform for cross-border payments in several central banks' digital currencies. It settles payment-versus-payment (both currencies swap at once), in real time, 24/7. | [S:6b0fae230518, para 2] |
| Off-bridge compliance | Doing compliance checks outside the mBridge platform. Banks meet each jurisdiction's KYC and AML/CFT rules off the platform. | [S:89b8fcadfaa8, p.3] |
| PvP / DvP | PvP: payment-versus-payment. DvP: delivery-versus-payment. In PvP, two payments in different currencies settle together. In DvP, an asset and its payment settle together. The Ensemble Sandbox was built to test both for settlement between banks. The SFC describes DvP as a simultaneous exchange of assets that lowers the risk of one side not delivering. | [S:460620ab7f2b, para 2]; [S:f009f1a6d615, para 13] |
| Atomic settlement | Settling both sides of a deal at the same instant. Each side depends on the other. | [S:9f8886b0fb21, s.4.1.3, p.30] |
| Purpose-bound money | Money with rules attached about how it can be used. It works as a 'wrapper' that sets conditions while leaving the underlying value intact. Phase 2 pilots examined it as an alternative to a natively programmable e-HKD (one with rules built into the money itself). A natively programmable e-HKD could weaken fungibility (every unit being interchangeable). | [S:bdefe7fc69d4, Section 4 'Programmability', p.33; Glossary, p.43] |
| Access Enabler | In Project Sela, a new type of go-between that serves retail CBDC users directly. It handles tasks such as onboarding and KYC. It does not hold users' CBDC or its own liquidity (cash reserves). | [S:f9000467b0ee, Section 2, p.8] |
| e-CNY tier-4 wallet | A basic personal wallet for the digital renminbi. It is opened with a Hong Kong mobile number, without real-name checks. The balance is capped at 10,000 renminbi. It allows retail payments only, not person-to-person transfers. | [S:08caafe0cfe7, Annex 2] |

**Tax and financial-crime data**

| Term | Plain definition | Source |
|---|---|---|
| CARF | Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF): an OECD standard for tax authorities to swap crypto-asset tax data automatically each year. | [S:ea81f92ea327, para 2] |
| RCASP / HKRCASP | RCASP: a reporting crypto-asset service provider. HKRCASP: an RCASP that meets a test of its link to Hong Kong. Under the 2026 Bill, an RCASP is a business that carries out crypto exchange transactions for customers. | [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, ss.50M-50N] |
| CRS / AEOI | CRS: the Common Reporting Standard. AEOI: automatic exchange of information. The CRS is the OECD model for swapping financial account information automatically each year. Hong Kong has run it since 2018. | [S:ab980a841782, final para] |
| RFI | Reporting financial institution (RFI): a financial institution that reports account data under the CRS. Under the amended CRS, these institutions report gross proceeds (total sale amounts) from sales of relevant crypto-assets by default. | [S:275d5cc93a88, Abbreviations; para 4.14] |

title: How regulation writes the P&L
md:
A P&L (profit and loss statement) shows what a business earns and what it spends. After reading, you can trace the main cost lines of a digital-asset business back to the rule that sets them. You can explain to a Chief Financial Officer (CFO) why the same client asset can cost very different amounts of capital, liquidity and staff time.

## In 60 seconds

Capital comes first. The Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) is the global body that writes bank capital standards. Hong Kong's rules putting its cryptoasset standard into law were set to take effect on 1 January 2026. [S:277820235891, paras 1-2 and closing para] Group 2b, the group for cryptoassets that fail the other tests, carries a 1,250% risk weight. [S:9e8d84c87168, Part XII CAE1 explanatory note, column (c), p.215] A risk weight scales how much capital a bank holds against an asset. The minimum total capital ratio is 8%. [S:5d0c13e09312, para 2.1.2] So 1,250% times 8% is 100%: at the minimum, the bank holds capital equal to the whole exposure.

Liquidity comes second. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) sets how tokenised deposits and stablecoins count in its liquidity tests. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3, paras 4-7] A stablecoin is a token built to keep a steady value against a currency. A bank that issues a stablecoin redeemable within the 30-day test period must generally assume all of it flows out. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3, para 7]

Custody brings liability. The HKMA expects a bank custodian to be liable to clients for loss of their digital assets from an incident attributable to the bank. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(n)] Licences bring fixed costs. Non-bank firms face minimum capital. [S:f1bbafccd556, para 6.2; S:f41a543388bc, paras 41-42] There are licence fees. [S:6186c01c6649, para 67] A registered bank needs named senior managers for each activity. [S:8934af8cc884, para 2.2.4] A bill for the Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF), a global tax-reporting standard, was introduced into the Legislative Council (LegCo) on 3 June 2026. [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, Overview section]

## Key facts

**Capital**
- Every cryptoasset exposure sits in Group 1a (tokenised traditional assets), Group 1b (stablecoins with an effective stabilisation mechanism) or Group 2 (the rest). [S:b7d630146e6c, paras 1.3.1-1.3.3]
- Group 1a exposures in the banking book generally follow the capital rules for the underlying traditional asset. [S:5d0c13e09312, para 8.7.1]
- A Group 2 asset reaches Group 2a, where limited hedging counts, only if it meets all three hedging recognition criteria. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 3.1.1] One test is an average market capitalisation of at least HK$78 billion over the previous year. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 3.1.1] Group 2 assets that get no hedging recognition are Group 2b. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 1.3.3]
- Group 2b exposures take a 1,250% risk weight. [S:9e8d84c87168, Part XII CAE1 explanatory note, column (c), p.215] This conservative treatment generally also covers credit valuation adjustment (CVA) risk, the risk of loss from a trading counterparty's weaker credit. [S:5d845665ba83, para 4.3.2]
- A bank must notify the HKMA before acquiring a new type of cryptoasset. It treats the asset as Group 2b until the HKMA agrees the bank's classification. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2]
- The HKMA's disclosure notes describe a Group 2 exposure limit of 1% of Tier 1 capital (a bank's core capital). [S:9e8d84c87168, Part XII CAE1 explanatory note, row 8, p.215] A bank designated as globally or domestically systemically important faces a capital add-on when its Group 2 exposure ratio exceeds the set limits. [S:5d0c13e09312, para 8.7.4(d)] For such a bank, the add-on covers Group 2 exposure between 1% and 2% of Tier 1 capital. [S:9e8d84c87168, Part XII CAE1 explanatory note, row 9, p.215] Above 2%, such a bank reports one total risk-weighted amount for all its Group 2 exposures. [S:9e8d84c87168, Part XII CAE1 explanatory note, row 10, p.215]
- A registered institution (RI) is a bank that the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) has registered for securities business. The HKMA says an RI must treat a loan backed only by virtual asset (VA) collateral as a clean (unsecured) loan for capital. [S:e64b7b0267b2, para (9), p.5]

**Liquidity**
- The liquidity coverage ratio (LCR) tests whether a bank holds enough easy-to-sell assets for 30 days of stressed outflows. The net stable funding ratio (NSFR) tests whether long-term assets have stable funding. (concept)
- The HKMA's liquidity rules for cryptoassets below apply to category 1 institutions, the banks that run the LCR. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3, paras 1-9]
- High-quality liquid assets (HQLA) are assets a bank can sell fast in a crisis. A cryptoasset counts as HQLA only if it is a Group 1a token of an eligible asset. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3, para 1] It must also pass the usual HQLA tests. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3, para 1]
- A bank that issues tokenised deposits meeting set conditions may treat them as deposits or unsecured funding. Even then, they cannot count as stable retail deposits. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3, para 4] If the bank cannot always identify the holders, it must treat them as other unsecured wholesale funding. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3, para 4]
- A bank holding another bank's tokenised deposits treats them like unsecured loans to financial institutions. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3, para 5]
- A bank holding a stablecoin generally counts a 0% LCR inflow and an 85% required stable funding factor. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3, para 7] A bank issuing one must apply a 100% LCR outflow if holders can redeem within the LCR period. Lower rates may apply if the backing assets would qualify as HQLA. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3, para 7]
- The HKMA may apply stricter liquidity treatment to a cryptoasset. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3, para 9] One example it gives: a bank that issues a stablecoin, or is a major service provider to one, may need to fund redemptions without a contract, to protect its franchise. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3, fn 98]
- Stablecoin reserves may include bank deposits with terms of up to three months. [S:240be6833157, para 2.3.1] In June 2026 the Government said HKMA rules have issuers place reserve assets with banks in Hong Kong. [S:c6df52e680de, Reply (1)]
- The HKMA expects an issuer to manage the reserves' intraday liquidity, taking into account trading hours and early-withdrawal terms on deposits. [S:240be6833157, para 6.4.3]
- The 2026 Policy Address says the HKMA plans 24/7 operations for EnsembleTX (its tokenisation pilot) by around end-2026. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 50] It also plans settlement in central bank digital currency by then. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 50] The HKMA also plans tests of tokenised Exchange Fund Bills (short-term HKMA debt) by end-2026, to help banks use them round the clock. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(ii)]

**Custody liability and insurance**
- The HKMA expects a bank custodian to keep adequate financial resources for potential losses, which may include insurance. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(n)] The May 2026 circular replaced the HKMA's February 2024 custody circular. [S:ed61d7c335e7, p.2]
- The HKMA expects 98% of client VA holdings in cold storage, meaning keys kept offline. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(l) and fn 8] It also expects security monitoring to run 24/7. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 23]
- For licensed trading platforms, the SFC expects an approved compensation arrangement covering 50% of client VA holdings in cold storage and 100% elsewhere. [S:f1bbafccd556, para 10.22]

**Licence capital and fees**
- A licensed trading platform must always hold HK$5 million or more in paid-up capital. [S:f1bbafccd556, para 6.2] Its required liquid capital is at least HK$3 million. [S:f1bbafccd556, para 6.3]
- Under the planned custodian regime, the SFC is to set baseline minimums for non-bank VA custodians only. These are HK$10 million paid-up capital and HK$3 million liquid capital. [S:f41a543388bc, paras 41-42] Banks are left out because HKMA capital requirements already apply to them. [S:f41a543388bc, para 41]
- A licensed stablecoin issuer needs paid-up capital of at least HK$25 million. [S:240be6833157, para 5.1.1] A bank licensee follows the Banking Ordinance instead. [S:240be6833157, para 5.1.3]
- Licence fees for VA dealing are to be benchmarked to fees for Type 1 (securities dealing) under the securities law. [S:6186c01c6649, para 38] For VA advice and management, the benchmark proposed is Types 4 and 9. As at December 2025, each of those types cost an RI HK$23,500 to apply and HK$35,000 a year. [S:6186c01c6649, para 67]
- An RI needs at least two executive officers for each regulated activity, each approved in writing by the Monetary Authority. [S:8934af8cc884, para 2.2.4]
- Banks already assessed by the HKMA for VA custody, and already providing it, are to get faster licensing under the custodian regime. [S:f41a543388bc, para 51]

**Compliance and technology**
- The HKMA requires registered institutions to take into account the SFC's anti-money laundering (AML) guideline for VA matters. [S:7bfdad704174, para 1.4 and fn 1] Under that guideline, for a VA transfer of HK$8,000 or more, the sending firm must obtain fuller sender and recipient details. It must pass them to the receiving firm securely and immediately. [S:08a762f7233e, paras 12.11.5-12.11.10] This is known as the travel rule.
- The SFC expects licensed VA service providers and internet brokers to adopt phishing-resistant login and device binding by 8 July 2027. [S:724f4d9f786e, paras 5, 21(c)]
- The HKMA doubled its AML on-site examinations of banks, from 14 in 2024 to 28 in 2025. [S:100b982aadca, p.85]
- On 9 March 2026 the HKMA said it expects every bank's board to oversee and endorse a strategic business plan within six months. The plan responds to distributed ledger technology (DLT) and other technology change. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, p.2] The HKMA expects banks to discuss new digital-asset activities with it before launch. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, p.2]

**Tax and accounting**
- The Inland Revenue Department (IRD) says profits from selling digital assets held as long-term investments are not chargeable to profits tax. Whether an asset is capital or trading stock depends on the facts. [S:1afc18524517, para 46]
- Hong Kong-sourced profits from trading or exchanging cryptocurrency as a business are chargeable to profits tax. [S:1afc18524517, para 47]
- The 2026-27 Budget said the Government would classify digital assets as qualifying investments for fund and family-office tax concessions. [S:654fa5eba8cf, para 98] A bill widening those regimes was gazetted on 12 June 2026. It is a bill, not yet law. [S:fca785b80cff, paras 1-2] In August 2026 it was still before a LegCo Bills Committee. If passed, it would apply from the 2025/26 year of assessment. [S:103ce885d306, para 6]
- The SFC reports that the Government confirmed the stamp duty waiver for transfers of Hong Kong-listed exchange-traded funds (ETFs) also covers tokenised ETFs. [S:8e1426ec511f, p.65, 'Driving tokenised products']
- If passed, the CARF bill would start on 1 January 2027. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, Clause 1(3)-(4)] A Hong Kong reporting crypto-asset service provider would have to register with the Commissioner of Inland Revenue. The deadline would be 31 January of the year after it first meets the Hong Kong link tests. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.50O(1)-(2)] Failing to comply without reasonable excuse would be an offence punishable by a fine. [S:e8c0a71f0cc5, s.80R(1)-(5)]
- Hong Kong-incorporated banks with cryptoasset exposures must publish a template every six months. It shows how their accounts classify and measure those exposures. [S:9e8d84c87168, Template CAE2, p.216]

## Industry view

- KPMG (an accounting and advisory firm) published its Hong Kong Banking Report 2026, with reported figures for surveyed Hong Kong banks. It found their average cost-to-income ratio fell from 42.1% to 41.9% in 2025. [I:1dfc7a0205ff, Performance section, p.8] The same report found staff costs rose 6.7%. [I:1dfc7a0205ff, Performance section, p.8] A cost-to-income ratio is operating costs divided by operating income.
- Morgan McKinley (a recruitment firm) publishes a salary guide. Its 2026 Hong Kong guide (reported pay ranges) puts a head of compliance at a median of HK$180,000 a month. [I:79e4be81501c, salary table, Compliance rows] Its range runs from HK$130,000 to HK$250,000. [I:79e4be81501c, salary table, Compliance rows]
- A 2022 BCBS study (global, reported, 19 banks) found about half of banks' reported crypto exposures came from custody, wallet, insurance and similar services. [I:d89ae309f669, pp.104-105, section 2.3]
- Two 2026 Hong Kong fund documents are the source here (reported figures). One is from China Asset Management (Hong Kong), the other from Bosera Asset Management (International). Each sets the custodian and administrator fee at up to 1% a year of net asset value. That fee includes the VA sub-custodian. [I:ee50e4efff6f, PDF p.11; I:d81073907a14, PDF p.95] The Bosera prospectus says its sub-custodian will have cover at 50% for cold-storage client assets and 100% for hot-storage ones. [I:d81073907a14, PDF p.118]
- The International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) Interpretations Committee (global standard-setter, 2019 agenda decision) said a cryptocurrency holding is not cash or a financial asset. [I:21d967bdefd5, pp.1-2] Such holdings fall under the inventory standard when held for sale in ordinary business, and otherwise under the intangible-asset standard. [I:21d967bdefd5, p.1, 'Which IFRS Standard applies']

## How it works commercially

- **Capital cost.** A business line uses capital. The bank expects a return on it, often called a hurdle rate (the minimum return a project must beat). A higher risk weight means more capital, so the line must earn more to clear the hurdle. (concept)
- **Balance-sheet or fee business.** Holding a coin on the bank's own books uses capital. Holding it for a client in segregated custody mainly uses operations and liability cover. (concept) The HKMA expects client assets to be kept apart from the bank's own. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 6 and fn 6]
- **Funding value.** Funding that liquidity rules treat as stable is worth more to a bank than wholesale funding. (concept)
- **Net interest margin.** Net interest margin is the gap between what a bank earns on assets and pays on funding. Reserve deposits from a stablecoin issuer earn this gap for the bank that holds them. (concept)
- **Fixed and variable costs.** Key management, monitoring and licences cost roughly the same at low and high volume. Fees on trades or assets grow with volume. So scale decides whether a line covers its costs. (concept)

The business lines show these levers one by one. See "Virtual-asset custody", "Stablecoin roles for banks", "Tokenised deposits and payments", "Virtual-asset dealing" and "Virtual-asset financing and margin".

> **Analysis — not official**
> **Question:** For a new digital-asset product, what does one extra unit of client business add to profit after the rules take their share?
> **How to think about it:**
> - Start with income per unit: a fee on assets held, a spread on trades, or a margin on deposits.
> - Take off variable costs per unit: the travel-rule data, blockchain monitoring and any insurance priced on value held.
> - Charge the capital the unit uses, at the bank's hurdle rate. A unit on the bank's own books in Group 2b carries a 1,250% risk weight [S:9e8d84c87168, Part XII CAE1 explanatory note, column (c), p.215]. The HKMA expects a unit held for a client in custody to be kept apart from the bank's own assets [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 6].
> - Charge the liquidity cost: funding that counts as wholesale is worth less than stable retail funding [S:69600121310a, Annex 3, para 4].
> - Then compare the total contribution with the fixed cost of keys, staff, licences and named managers. A line with a small contribution per unit needs high volume to break even.
> **What it depends on:** the asset's capital group; whether the bank owns the asset or only safekeeps it; volumes and fee levels; the hurdle rate; the final licensing rules.
> **Official signposts:** HKMA classification decisions on new asset types [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2]; the custodian bill and its start date [S:f41a543388bc, para 65]; EnsembleTX moving to 24/7 [S:ef3648ff1610, para 50]; progress of the CARF bill [S:d70ae2cbc9d1, Overview section].
> **What this is not:** Not a forecast, not advice, and not the regulator's view.

## Talking points

**To the CEO**
- Basel crypto capital rules were set to take effect in Hong Kong on 1 January 2026. [S:277820235891, closing para]
- The HKMA expected each board to endorse a strategic business plan within six months of 9 March 2026. [S:3ec5b269b5dc, letter body, p.2]

**To the CCO**
- We must notify the HKMA before we acquire any new type of cryptoasset. [S:b7d630146e6c, para 2.1.2]
- Under the SFC's AML guideline, VA transfers of HK$8,000 or more must carry fuller sender and recipient details. [S:08a762f7233e, paras 12.11.5-12.11.10]

**To business heads**
- Group 2b cryptoassets on our own books take a 1,250% risk weight. At the 8% minimum ratio, capital equals the exposure. [S:9e8d84c87168, Part XII CAE1 explanatory note, column (c), p.215; S:5d0c13e09312, para 2.1.2]
- The HKMA expects us, as custodian, to be liable for client asset losses from incidents attributable to us. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(n)]

**To Risk / CRO**
- An issued stablecoin redeemable within the LCR period means a 100% assumed outflow. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3, para 7]
- Tokenised deposits with unknown holders count as other unsecured wholesale funding. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3, para 4]

## Common mix-ups

- **Myth:** Custody of client coins costs the same as holding coins ourselves. **Fact:** The 1,250% weight applies to Group 2b cryptoasset exposures. [S:9e8d84c87168, Part XII CAE1 explanatory note, column (c), p.215] For custody, the HKMA expects segregation, and liability backed by adequate financial resources. [S:ce05e67bcdce, paras 6, 11(n)]
- **Myth:** Tokenised deposits are just deposits for liquidity. **Fact:** They cannot get stable retail deposit rates. Unknown holders mean wholesale treatment. [S:69600121310a, Annex 3, para 4]
- **Myth:** Banks need the 50%/100% insurance cover. **Fact:** That is the SFC's expectation for trading platforms. [S:f1bbafccd556, para 10.22] The HKMA's 2026 guidance for banks uses liability plus adequate financial resources. [S:ce05e67bcdce, para 11(n)]
- **Myth:** Crypto gains are always tax-free in Hong Kong. **Fact:** Gains on long-term investments are not chargeable to profits tax. [S:1afc18524517, para 46] Hong Kong-sourced profits from a crypto trading business are taxed. [S:1afc18524517, para 47]
- **Myth:** The fund tax concession for digital assets is already law. **Fact:** It is in a bill gazetted in June 2026. [S:fca785b80cff, paras 1, 4] In August 2026 LegCo was still scrutinising it. [S:103ce885d306, para 6]

## Read these first

1. **Supervisory Policy Manual (SPM) module on liquidity risk, Annex 3** — HKMA, V.5, 19 December 2025. Read paras 1-9 for how tokens and stablecoins count in the LCR and NSFR. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20251217-7-EN/LM-1.pdf
2. **Updated Guidance on Expected Standards on Provision of Custodial Services for Digital Assets** — HKMA, 27 May 2026. Read paras 6, 11, 14, 19 and 21-23 for liability, storage and monitoring. https://brdr.hkma.gov.hk/eng/doc-ldg/docId/getPdf/20260527-7-EN/20260527-7-EN.pdf
3. **Consultation Conclusions on VA custodian services** — Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau (FSTB) and SFC, 24 December 2025. Read paras 41-42 and 51 for capital baselines and faster licensing. https://www.fstb.gov.hk/fsb/en/publication/consult/doc/Custodian_consultation_conclusion_e.pdf
4. **Guideline on Supervision of Licensed Stablecoin Issuers** — HKMA, 1 August 2025. Read paras 2.2-2.3, 5.1 and 6.4 for reserves, capital and liquidity. https://www.hkma.gov.hk/media/eng/doc/key-functions/ifc/stablecoin-issuers/Guideline_on_supervision_of_licensed_stablecoin_issuers_eng.pdf
5. **Departmental Interpretation and Practice Notes (DIPN) No. 39, on profits tax and digital assets** — IRD, March 2020. Read paras 41-52. https://www.ird.gov.hk/eng/pdf/dipn39.pdf
6. **CARF and Amended Common Reporting Standard (CRS) Bill 2026** — IRD, 22 May 2026. Read Clause 1 and ss.50M-50Q and 80R. https://www.ird.gov.hk/eng/pdf/carf/Inland%20Revenue%20(Amendment)%20(Crypto-Asset%20Reporting%20Framework%20and%20Amended%20Common%20Reporting%20Standard)%20Bill%202026(eng).pdf

## Open items

- The sources reviewed hold no final rules on the April 2026 Banking (Capital) Rules proposals. [S:f6b5ade120fe, landing page]
- No official source gives the cost of insurance for VA custody in Hong Kong.
- The fund tax bill and the CARF bill had not passed as of 25 September 2026 in the sources reviewed.
- Final fee levels and start dates for the VA dealing, custodian, advisory and management regimes were not set in the sources reviewed. The Government and SFC said they would consider the dealing start date. [S:6186c01c6649, para 32]
- No HKMA guidance on intraday liquidity for 24/7 tokenised settlement was found in the sources reviewed.

## Related modules

[D1](#m-D1), [D2](#m-D2), [D3](#m-D3), [D5](#m-D5), [C3](#m-C3), [C4](#m-C4), [C5](#m-C5), [F1](#m-F1), [F3](#m-F3), [F5a](#m-F5a)

title: Market structure: who does what
md:
A P&L (profit and loss statement) shows what a business earns and spends. This module maps the regulated firms in Hong Kong's digital-asset market and how each type earns money. After reading, you can name each firm type and say how many hold a licence, using official registers. You can explain where a bank can compete, supply or partner. You can also read listed firms' published figures without mistaking them for market shares.

## In 60 seconds

Hong Kong licenses digital-asset firms by activity, such as running a trading platform or issuing stablecoins. [S:4a0342268bf2, para 6] The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) licenses virtual asset trading platforms (VATPs), which are exchanges for crypto tokens. It listed 13 licensed platforms at end-June 2026, with six applications under review. [S:c24d834af185, p.30] The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) licenses stablecoin issuers. A stablecoin is a token built to keep a steady value against a currency. The HKMA register, dated 23 April 2026, lists two licensed issuers. [S:270f1f7324ab, Register table] The HKMA granted those two licences from 36 first-batch applicants. [S:193316443831, Assessment of licence applications, paras 1-2] A digital bank serves clients mainly online. [S:5422156398b3, para 1] The HKMA listed eight digital banks at 31 August 2026. [S:577cadbd3cd8, List, rows 5-12]

Other firm types are still waiting for their own licence. Planned regimes for virtual asset (VA) dealers and custodians are at the conclusions stage. [S:6186c01c6649, para 49; S:f41a543388bc, para 65] So are regimes for VA advisers and managers. [S:4a0342268bf2, para 1] On 24 June 2026 the Government said it will put one bill covering all four to the Legislative Council (LegCo) in 2026. [S:c6df52e680de, Reply (3)] Some licensed firms are joint ventures. The HKMA names one licensed stablecoin issuer as a joint venture of three firms, one of them a bank. [S:193316443831, para 1]

## Key facts

**Virtual asset trading platforms**
- The SFC's list showed 13 licensed platforms and six applicants at its 29 May 2026 update. [S:b14be2203d39, Licensed platforms table; Last update line] The SFC stresses that applicants are not licensed. [S:b14be2203d39, Applicant list and notes]
- At 30 June 2026 the SFC counted 159 licensees under Hong Kong's anti-money laundering ordinance (AMLO), Cap. 615, the law that licenses platforms. That is 13 licensed providers plus 146 licensed individuals. [S:c24d834af185, p.32, table 'Licensees under the AMLO']
- The first platform licence was granted in December 2020, for professional investors only. [S:60682e9fd7fa, main text and Note 1]
- Since November 2025, licensed platforms may pool orders with overseas affiliates in a shared order book. [S:8e1426ec511f, p.64, 'Increasing market accessibility'] Affiliates may also act as market makers, meaning firms that quote buy and sell prices. [S:8e1426ec511f, p.64, 'Increasing market accessibility']
- A bank offering VA dealing may partner only with SFC-licensed platforms. It either introduces clients to the platform or uses an omnibus account (one pooled account for many clients). [S:8a016a912528, para 17]
- A licensed platform must keep at least HK$5 million of paid-up capital. [S:f1bbafccd556, para 6.2]

**Stablecoin issuers**
- The register of 23 April 2026 lists Anchorpoint Financial Limited (FRS01) and The Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation Limited (FRS02). Both licences took effect on 10 April 2026. [S:270f1f7324ab, Register table]
- The HKMA received first-batch applications from 36 entities by 30 September 2025. [S:193316443831, Assessment of licence applications, para 1] It granted licences to two of them. [S:193316443831, Assessment of licence applications, para 2]
- On 10 June 2026 the Government said that if more licences are granted, the total number will stay very limited. [S:3f0fcc104e61, Reply (2)]
- On 28 April 2026 both licensees confirmed they had not yet issued regulated stablecoins. [S:275e7319a841, paras 2-3]
- An issuer must not pay interest to holders. [S:fe4baea8dd7d, para 3.13.1] A non-bank issuer needs paid-up capital of at least HK$25 million. [S:240be6833157, para 5.1.1]

**VA custodians**
- Under the planned regime, platform-linked firms, banks and local banks' subsidiaries that safekeep client keys would need a licence or registration. [S:f41a543388bc, para 35] The FSTB (Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau) and the SFC aim to put a bill to LegCo in 2026. [S:f41a543388bc, para 65]
- Under the planned dealing regime, the SFC is to require VA dealers to use SFC-regulated custodians. [S:6186c01c6649, para 26]
- The SFC expects the trustee of an SFC-authorised VA fund to delegate custody only to three kinds of firm. These are a licensed platform, a bank (or a local bank's subsidiary) meeting HKMA custody standards, or another firm the SFC accepts. [S:c79c4686c5e0, para 20]

**Tokenisation platforms**
- The Central Moneymarkets Unit (CMU) is Hong Kong's central securities depository, a system that holds securities and settles trades in them. CMU OmniClear (CMU OmniClear Limited) runs it for the HKMA. It sits under a holding company, CMU OmniClear Holdings Limited. [S:9c8855ec55a1, para 2] On 12 November 2025 the HKMA said Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing Limited (HKEX) would buy newly issued shares for a 20% stake. [S:9c8855ec55a1, para 2] Once the deal completed, the HKMA said, the Exchange Fund would own 80% of the holding company and HKEX 20%. [S:9c8855ec55a1, para 2] The HKMA called the deal a joint venture. [S:9c8855ec55a1, para 2]
- The 2026 Policy Address says CMU OmniClear is to set up a digital asset platform in 2026 for issuing and settling digital bonds. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(iv)] It also says HKEX is building a multi-asset tokenisation platform on a blockchain. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 46(v)]
- It says digital bonds issued in Hong Kong took nearly 50% of the global market over 2025 and the first half of 2026. [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35]
- At end-June 2026, the SFC counted 15 tokenised retail products. Their tokenised classes had assets under management of HK$10.3 billion. [S:c24d834af185, p.33]

**VA fund managers and advisers**
- The SFC's terms and conditions for VA fund managers apply in two cases. One is a fund with a stated VA objective. The other is a fund that plans to put 10% or more of its gross assets into them. [S:40148cf96f41, Part I, p.3]
- The SFC counted 2,358 firms holding a Type 9 licence (asset management) at end-2025. The count covers all asset classes. [S:6d9deb07299d, Section VI, para 43] It gives no separate count for VA managers.
- The 11 VA spot exchange-traded funds (ETFs) had a combined market value of US$451 million at end-June 2026. [S:c24d834af185, p.31] Three of these ETFs may stake through licensed platforms. [S:c24d834af185, p.31]
- The Government and the SFC have yet to set a start date for the advisory and management regimes. [S:01c5c5c4045f, para 64]

**OTC dealers**
- An over-the-counter (OTC) dealer trades directly with clients rather than on an exchange. (concept)
- The dealing regime is to cover anyone who, as a business, makes or offers deals to buy or sell virtual assets, in line with securities dealing. [S:6186c01c6649, para 3] Payment firms offering conversion into or out of virtual assets may need a licence. [S:6186c01c6649, para 4]
- Existing dealers are not to get a period to keep trading while they apply. [S:6186c01c6649, para 31] Licensed platforms, and SFC-licensed or SFC-registered firms that already deal in virtual assets, are to get faster approval. [S:6186c01c6649, paras 35-36]

**Digital banks**
- The HKMA listed eight digital banks at 31 August 2026, all incorporated in Hong Kong. [S:577cadbd3cd8, List, rows 5-12]
- A person holding more than 50% of a local bank should normally be a supervised bank or financial institution. Otherwise the HKMA expects a Hong Kong holding company with supervisory conditions. [S:5422156398b3, para 9] Banks may apply to own one. So may technology companies and other non-financial firms. [S:5422156398b3, para 9]
- The HKMA would be concerned by a digital bank chasing market share with heavy early losses and no credible plan for profit. [S:5422156398b3, para 19]
- By end-July 2024, six of the eight then called virtual banks were registered with the SFC for securities business. [S:a4db9f935749, Executive Summary, para 12] In August 2024 the HKMA said it would remove the rule that they mainly serve retail clients. It pointed to their growing links with digital-asset and Web3 firms. [S:a4db9f935749, Executive Summary, para 14]

**Joint ventures and partnerships**
- On 10 April 2026 the HKMA described Anchorpoint as a joint venture. [S:193316443831, para 1] It named the three partners in this order: Standard Chartered Bank (Hong Kong) Limited, HKT (HKT Limited) and Animoca Brands Limited. [S:193316443831, para 1] The HKMA does not state the shareholdings. [S:193316443831, para 1]
- EnsembleTX (the HKMA's pilot for settling tokenised deposits between banks) has annexes dated November 2025. They name seven Tokenised Deposit Banks and 13 other industry pioneers. [S:d193f12a5f78, Annexes A-B] The seven banks include Fusion Bank Limited [S:d193f12a5f78, Annex A], which is on the HKMA's digital bank list. [S:577cadbd3cd8, List, rows 5-12]
- The Ensemble Sandbox list revised on 7 April 2025 shows banks in its trade theme. Technology firms there include Ant Digital Technologies and Microsoft Hong Kong Limited. [S:5f8362ecd97f, p.2]
- Project mBridge is a shared platform for cross-border payments in central bank digital currency. In June 2024 the HKMA was one of its project team members. [S:db56d97e2206, para 1 and fn 1]

## Industry view

Each figure below is a firm's own reported number from its filing. The firms differ in scope and period, so the figures are not market shares.

- **HashKey Holdings Limited (HashKey)** (Hong Kong-listed; 2025 annual results, reported): group revenue of HK$723.1 million. [I:786f45f6ea11, PDF p.11] The segment HashKey calls "transaction facilitation services" brought HK$522.8 million, asset management HK$117.1 million and on-chain services HK$83.2 million. [I:786f45f6ea11, PDF p.11] Group trading volume was HK$590.8 billion. [I:786f45f6ea11, PDF p.11] The group also reports business outside Hong Kong. [I:786f45f6ea11, PDF p.11]
- **HashKey** (interim results to 30 June 2026, reported): revenue of HK$342.5 million and trading volume of HK$282.2 billion. [I:9ca15dca711d, PDF p.3; PDF p.11]
- **OSL Group Limited (OSL)** (Hong Kong-listed; 2025 annual report, reported): digital asset transaction services income of HK$326.8 million. [I:e2df03a8c8a6, PDF p.126, Note 6] Software-as-a-service income was HK$133.1 million and custody income HK$16.1 million. [I:e2df03a8c8a6, PDF p.126, Note 5] Transaction volume was HK$201.2 billion. [I:e2df03a8c8a6, PDF p.12, MD&A] These are group figures. OSL reports income from Asia Pacific and Europe. [I:e2df03a8c8a6, PDF p.127, Note 6]
- **Circle Internet Group** (US-listed stablecoin issuer, not on the HKMA register [S:270f1f7324ab, Register table]; fourth quarter of 2025, global, reported): reserve income of US$733 million. [I:c835a8109c3f, Fourth Quarter 2025 Financial Highlights] Distribution, transaction and other costs were US$461 million. [I:c835a8109c3f, Fourth Quarter 2025 Financial Highlights]

## How it works commercially

- **Trading platforms** earn a fee on each trade. The take rate is fee income divided by trading volume. Platforms may also earn from listing, custody and staking. (concept)
- **Stablecoin issuers** earn the return on the reserve assets behind their coins. They pay distributors and run costs out of that return. Income moves with interest rates and the value of coins in circulation. (concept)
- **Custodians** charge a yearly fee on the value of assets they hold. Their main costs are key security, monitoring, audit and liability cover. (concept)
- **Tokenisation platforms** charge issuers to create tokens and charge users to settle and service them. (concept)
- **Fund managers** charge a management fee on assets under management (AUM), the value of client money they run. Some funds also pay a performance fee. (concept)
- **OTC dealers** earn the spread, the gap between the price they buy at and the price they sell at. (concept)
- **Digital banks** earn net interest margin, the gap between what they earn on loans and pay on deposits, plus fees. (concept)
- A bank can meet each firm type in three roles: competitor, supplier or joint-venture partner. As a supplier, it offers accounts, custody or credit. (concept) The business lines "Banking the digital-asset industry" and "Infrastructure as a service" cover the supplier role.

> **Analysis — not official**
> **Question:** For each firm type, is it a rival, a customer or a partner for our bank?
> **How to think about it:**
> - List each firm type and ask what it buys from banks: accounts, reserve deposits, custody, credit or settlement.
> - Mark where rules create demand a bank could serve, such as dealers needing regulated custodians [S:6186c01c6649, para 26] or issuers placing reserve assets with Hong Kong banks [S:c6df52e680de, Reply (1)].
> - Mark where the bank needs a licensed partner, such as a licensed platform for VA dealing [S:8a016a912528, para 17].
> - Compare building a unit, partnering, or holding a stake through a joint venture, using the patterns regulators have already described.
> **What it depends on:** how many firms hold each licence; when the new regimes start; the bank's own licences; its appetite for partner risk.
> **Official signposts:** the SFC platform list [S:b14be2203d39, Licensed platforms table]; the HKMA issuer register [S:270f1f7324ab, Register table]; the combined VA bill [S:c6df52e680de, Reply (3)]; the CMU OmniClear platform [S:ef3648ff1610, para 35(iv)].
> **What this is not:** Not a forecast, not advice, and not the regulator's view.

## Talking points

**To the CEO**
- Hong Kong had 13 licensed trading platforms at end-June 2026. [S:c24d834af185, p.30] The HKMA register of 23 April 2026 lists two stablecoin issuers. [S:270f1f7324ab, Register table]
- One licensed issuer is a joint venture that includes Standard Chartered Bank (Hong Kong) Limited. [S:193316443831, para 1]

**To the CCO**
- For VA dealing we may partner only with SFC-licensed platforms. [S:8a016a912528, para 17]
- The SFC says applicants on its list are not licensed. [S:b14be2203d39, Applicant list and notes]

**To business heads**
- Planned rules would make VA dealers use SFC-regulated custodians. [S:6186c01c6649, para 26]
- The HKMA requires licensed stablecoin issuers to place reserve assets with banks in Hong Kong. [S:c6df52e680de, Reply (1)]

**To Risk / CRO**
- Licensed platforms may now pool orders with overseas affiliates. [S:8e1426ec511f, p.64, 'Increasing market accessibility']
- Neither licensed issuer had issued a regulated stablecoin as of 28 April 2026. [S:275e7319a841, paras 2-3]

## Common mix-ups

- **Myth:** Every name on the SFC platform list is licensed. **Fact:** The list has a separate section for applicants. The SFC says applicants are not licensed. [S:b14be2203d39, Applicant list and notes]
- **Myth:** VA custodians and OTC dealers already have their own licence. **Fact:** Both regimes are at the conclusions stage, with a bill targeted for 2026. [S:f41a543388bc, para 65; S:6186c01c6649, para 49]
- **Myth:** Only banks can own a digital bank. **Fact:** Technology companies and other non-financial firms may apply to own one. [S:5422156398b3, para 9]
- **Myth:** A listed platform's revenue shows its market share. **Fact:** Each filing covers its own firm, scope and period. Its revenue is not a share of a market. (concept)

## Read these first

1. **Lists of virtual asset trading platforms** — SFC, last updated 29 May 2026. Read the licensed table and the applicant notes. https://www.sfc.hk/en/Welcome-to-the-Fintech-Contact-Point/Virtual-assets/Virtual-asset-trading-platforms-operators/Lists-of-virtual-asset-trading-platforms
2. **Register of licensed stablecoin issuers** — HKMA, 23 April 2026. https://www.hkma.gov.hk/eng/regulatory-resources/registers/register-of-licensed-stablecoin-issuers/
3. **SFC Quarterly Report, April-June 2026** — SFC, 26 August 2026. Read pp.30-33 for counts of platforms, funds and tokenised products. https://www.sfc.hk/-/media/EN/files/COM/QR-Reports/202604-06/E-SFC-QR4-6.pdf?rev=182fe897bb1f4b1591f202de12feaf0d
4. **List of digital banks** — HKMA, as at 31 August 2026. https://www.hkma.gov.hk/media/eng/doc/key-functions/banking-stability/banking-policy-and-supervision/list_of_digital_banks.xls
5. **HKEX as a strategic shareholder in CMU OmniClear Holdings** — HKMA, 12 November 2025. https://www.hkma.gov.hk/eng/news-and-media/press-releases/2025/11/20251112-3/
6. **Consultation conclusions on VA dealing** — FSTB and SFC, 24 December 2025. Read paras 3-4, 26, 31-36 and 49. https://apps.sfc.hk/edistributionWeb/gateway/EN/consultation/doc?refNo=25CP12

## Open items

- The sources reviewed give no official count of firms holding SFC terms to manage VA portfolios.
- The sources reviewed include no list of the banks registered with the SFC for VA dealing, advice or distribution.
- Counts here are snapshots at the dates shown, such as 29 May, 30 June and 31 August 2026. Registers can change after those dates.
- The sources reviewed give no market shares, revenues or client numbers for individual platforms, issuers or banks.
- The sources reviewed do not show when regulated stablecoins were first issued, if at all, after 28 April 2026.
